definition_paragraphs.text: Meteorologists prepare short-term or long-term weather forecasts used in aviation, shipping, agriculture and other areas and for the information of the general public. They conduct research related to the composition, structure and dynamics of the atmosphere.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: investigating direction and speed of air movements, pressures, temperatures, humidity, physical and chemical transformation of pollutants and other phenomena such as cloud formation and precipitation, electrical disturbances or solar radiation;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: studying data collected from meteorological stations, radar and satellite imagery and computer model output  to plot and forecast weather conditions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing and reporting short-term or long-term weather maps, forecasts and warnings relating to atmospheric phenomena such as cyclones, storms and other hazards to life and property and disseminating information about atmospheric conditions through a variety of media including radio, television, print and the Internet;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: conducting experiments in fog dispersal, cloud seeding, rain enhancement and other types of weather modification programs;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: developing and testing mathematical computer models of weather and climate for experimental or operational use;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: participating in studies of the effect of weather on the environment;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: analyzing the impact of industrial projects and human activity on the climate and quality of the air and work with the social science, engineering and economic communities to develop appropriate mitigation strategies;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: engaging in the design and development of new equipment and procedures for meteorological data collection, remote sensing, or for related applications;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: conducting research on and improving or developing concepts, theories and operational methods related to the composition, structure and dynamics of the atmosphere and preparing scientific papers and reports on the outcome of this research; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: preparing scientific papers and reports.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Chemists conduct research, improve or develop concepts, theories and operational methods, or apply scientific knowledge relating to chemistry, to develop new knowledge or products and for quality and process control.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting research and improving or developing concepts, instruments, theories and operational methods related to chemistry;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: conducting experiments, tests and analyses to investigate chemical composition and energy and chemical changes in various natural or synthetic substances, materials and products;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: developing procedures for environmental control, quality control and various other procedures for manufacturers or users;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: conducting programs of sample and data collection and analysis to identify and quantify environmental toxicants;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: participating in interdisciplinary research and development projects working with chemical engineers, biologists, microbiologists, agronomists, geologists or other professionals;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: using micro-organisms to convert substances into new compounds;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: determining ways to strengthen or combine materials or develop new materials;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: reproducing and synthesizing naturally occurring substances and creating new artificial substances; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: preparing scientific papers and reports.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Geologists and geophysicists conduct research; improve or develop concepts, theories and operational methods, or apply scientific knowledge relating to geology and geophysics in such fields as oil, gas and mineral exploration and extraction, water conservation, civil engineering, telecommunications and navigation, and assessment and mitigation of the effects of development and waste disposal projects on the environment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting research and improving or developing concepts, theories and operational methods related to geology and geophysics;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: studying composition and structure of the Earth's crust, examining rocks, minerals, fossils and other materials, to determine processes affecting the development of the Earth, trace evolution of past life, establish nature and chronology of geological formations and assess their commercial applications;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: interpreting research data and preparing geological reports, maps, charts and diagrams, reports and papers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: applying geological knowledge to problems encountered in civil engineering projects such as the construction of dams, bridges, tunnels, and large buildings; and land reclamation projects;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: using various remote sensing programs to investigate and measure seismic, gravitational, electrical, thermal, and magnetic forces affecting the Earth;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: estimating weight, size and mass of the Earth and composition and structure of its interior, and studying the nature, activity and predictability of volcanoes, glaciers and earthquakes;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: charting the Earth's magnetic field and applying this and other collected data for broadcasting, navigation and other purposes;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: studying and measuring physical properties of seas and the atmosphere and their inter-relationship, such as the exchange of thermal energy;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: locating and determining the nature and extent of oil, gas and mineral deposits using seismological, gravimetric, magnetic, electrical or radiometric methods;  identifying deposits of construction materials and determining their characteristics and suitability for use as concrete aggregates, road fill or for other applications;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: researching the movement, distribution and physical properties of ground and surface waters; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: advising in areas such as waste management, route and site selection and the restoration of contaminated sites.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: OTHER PHYSICAL AND EARTH SCIENCE PROFESSIONALS
MATHEMATICIANS, ACTUARIES, STATISTICIANS AND DATA SCIENTISTS

definition_paragraphs.text: Mathematicians, actuaries, statisticians and data scientists conduct research, improve or develop mathematical, actuarial and statistical concepts, theories and operational models and techniques and apply this knowledge to a wide range of  tasks in such fields as engineering, business and social and other sciences.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: studying, improving and developing mathematical, actuarial and statistical theories and techniques; advising on or applying mathematical principles, models and techniques to a wide range of tasks in the fields of engineering, natural, social or life sciences; conducting logical analyzes of management problems, especially in terms of input-output effectiveness, and formulating mathematical models of each problem usually for programming and solution by computer; designing and putting into operation pension schemes and life, health, social and other types of insurance systems;  applying mathematics, statistics, probability and risk theory to assess potential financial impacts of future events.

Planning and organizing surveys and other statistical collections, and designing questionnaires; evaluating, processing, analyzing, and interpreting statistical data and preparing them for publication; advising on or applying various data collection methods and statistical methods and techniques, and determining reliability of findings, especially in such fields as business or medicine as well as in other areas of natural, social or life sciences; preparing scientific papers and reports; supervising the work of mathematical, actuarial and statistical assistants and statistical clerks.

definition_paragraphs.text: Mathematicians develop mathematical models, concepts, theories, operational methods and techniques to provide solution to the problems. They provide advice on the practical application of mathematics in the field of business, engineering and all other sciences.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: developing and/or improving mathematical  theories, principles, concepts and operational methods and techniques

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: advising on or applying mathematical concepts, theories and principles to an extensive tasks in the fields of engineering and all sciences

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: conducting logical analyzes of management problems, especially in terms of input-output effectiveness, and formulating mathematical models of each problem usually for programming and solution by computer; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: supervising the work of mathematical assistants and clerks.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Workers in this unit group conduct research, improve or develop mathematical and other aspects of statistical concepts,  theories and operational methods and techniques, and advise on or engage in their practical application, in such  fields  as  business  or medicine, as well as in other areas of natural, social or life sciences.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: studying, improving and developing statistical theories and methodologies;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: planning  and  organizing  surveys  and  other  statistical collections, and designing questionnaires;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: evaluating,   processing,   analyzing,   and   interpreting statistical data and preparing them for publication;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: advising on or applying various data collection methods and statistical methods  and   techniques,   and   determining reliability  of  findings, especially  in  such  fields as business or medicine as well as in other areas of  natural, social or life sciences; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: preparing scientific papers and reports.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Actuaries conduct research and improve or develop mathematical and actuarial concepts, theories and operational methods and techniques and advise on or engage in their practical application in such fields as engineering, business and social and other sciences.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: studying, improving and developing actuarial theories and techniques;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: designing and putting into operation pension schemes and life, health, social and other types of insurance systems;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: applying mathematics, statistics, probability and risk theory to assess potential financial impacts of future events;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: evaluating, processing, analyzing, and interpreting statistical data and preparing them for publication;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: preparing scientific papers and reports; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: supervising the work of  actuarial assistants and statistical clerks.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Data scientists use analytical tools and techniques to extract meaningful insights from data. They may use a variety of methods to obtain data, including through access to other organizations’ databases or by using web-scraping tools. They develop algorithms and models to support programs for machine learning. They often use data visualization software to present their findings, and make recommendations for business decisions or process changes based on the results of their analysis.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining which data are available and useful for the project;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: collecting, categorizing, and analyzing data;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: creating, validating, testing, and updating algorithms and models;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: using data visualization software to present findings; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: making business recommendations to stakeholders based on data analysis

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Life science professionals apply knowledge gained from research into human, animal and plant life and their interactions with each other and the environment to develop new knowledge, improve agricultural and forestry production, and solve human health and environmental problems.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: collecting, analyzing and evaluating experimental and field data to identify and develop new processes and techniques; providing advice and support to governments, organizations and businesses about ecological sustainable development of natural resources.

records.title: BIOLOGISTS, BOTANISTS, ZOOLOGISTS AND RELATED SCIENTISTS

definition_paragraphs.text: Biologists, botanists, zoologists and related professionals study living organisms and their interactions with each  other and with the environment, and apply this knowledge to solve human health and environmental problems. They work in diverse fields such as botany, zoology, ecology, marine biology, genetics, immunology, pharmacology, toxicology, physiology, bacteriology and virology.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: undertaking research in laboratories and in the field to increase scientific knowledge of living organisms; to discover new information; to test hypotheses; to solve problems in areas such as the environment, agriculture and health; and to develop new products, processes and techniques for pharmaceutical, agricultural and environmental use;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: designing and conducting experiments and tests;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: gathering human, animal, insect and plant specimens and data, and studying their origin, development, chemical and physical form, structure, composition, and life and reproductive processes;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: examining living organisms using a variety of specialized equipment, instruments, technologies and techniques such as electron microscopes, telemetry, global positioning systems, biotechnology, satellite imaging, genetic engineering, digital imaging analysis, polymerase chain reaction and computer modelling;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: identifying, classifying, recording and monitoring living organisms and maintaining databases;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: to the scientific community in scientific journals or at conferences for scrutiny and further debate;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: designing and carrying out environmental impact assessments to identify changes caused by natural or human factors; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: providing advice to governments, organizations and businesses in areas such as conservation, management of natural resources, the effects of climate change and pollution.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Farming, forestry and fisheries advisers study and provide assistance and advice on farm, forestry and fisheries management, including cultivation, fertilization, harvesting, soil erosion and composition, disease prevention, nutrition, crop rotation and marketing. They develop techniques for increasing productivity, and study and develop plans and policies for land and fisheries management.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: collecting and analyzing data and samples related to produce, feed, soil, water quality and other factors affecting farm, forest or fishery production;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: advising on techniques for improving the production of crops, livestock and fish, and alternative production options;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: advising on livestock and crop disease, control of pests and weeds, soil improvement, animal husbandry and  feeding programs;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: studying the environmental factors affecting commercial crop production, pasture growth, animal breeding, fish stocks and the growth and health of forest trees;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: studying the effects of cultivation techniques, soils, insects, diseases and fisheries practices on animal, crop, forestry and fisheries yield;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: studying fish migration, growth, feeding and spawning and devising methods of collecting, fertilizing, incubating and hatching fish eggs;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: researching into characteristics, use capability and productivity of soils and applying findings to development of improved agricultural, horticultural and forestry practices;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: developing procedures and techniques for solving agricultural problems and improving the efficiency of production;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: managing forest and fisheries resources to maximize their long-term commercial, recreational and environmental benefits;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: studying the propagation and culture of forest trees, methods for improving the growth of stock, and the effects of thinning on forest yields;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: investigating, planning and implementing management procedures to cope with the effects of fires, floods,  droughts, soil erosion, pests and diseases; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: preparing scientific reports and conducting advisory information sessions and lectures for farming, forestry and fishing communities and other groups.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Environmental protection professionals study and assess the effects on the environment of human activity such as air, water and noise pollution, soil contamination, climate change, toxic waste and depletion and degradation of  natural resources. They develop plans and solutions to protect, conserve, restore, minimize and prevent further damage to the environment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: Environmental protection professionals study and assess the effects on the environment of human activity such as air, water and noise pollution, soil contamination, climate change, toxic waste and depletion and degradation of  natural resources. They develop plans and solutions to protect, conserve, restore, minimize and prevent further damage to the environment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: conducting research, performing tests, collecting samples, performing field and laboratory analysis to identify sources of environmental problems and recommending ways to prevent, control and remediate the impact of environmental problems;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assessing the likely impact that potential or proposed activities, projects and developments may have on the environment, and recommending whether such developments should proceed;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: developing and coordinating the implementation of environmental management systems to enable organizations to identify, monitor and control the impact of their activities, products and services on the environment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: conducting audits to evaluate environmental impact of existing activities, processes, wastes, noises and substances;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assessing an organization's compliance with government and internal environmental regulations and guidelines, identifying violations and determining appropriate remedial action;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: providing technical advice and support services to organizations on how best to deal with environmental problems in order to reduce environmental damage and minimize financial loss; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: developing conservation plans.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Engineering professionals (excluding electrotechnology) design, plan and organize the testing, construction, installation and maintenance of structures, machines and their components, and production systems and plants, and plan production schedules and work procedures to ensure engineering projects are undertaken safely, efficiently and in a cost effective manner.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: planning and designing chemical process systems, civil engineering projects, mechanical equipment and systems, mining and drilling operations, and other engineering projects; specifying and interpreting drawings and plans, and determining construction methods; supervising the construction of structures, water and gas supply and transportation systems, and the manufacture, installation, operation and maintenance of equipment, machines and plant; organizing and managing project labor and the delivery of materials, plant and equipment; estimating total costs and preparing detailed cost plans and estimates as tools for budgetary control; resolving design and operational problems in the various fields of engineering through the application of engineering technology.

definition_paragraphs.text: Industrial and production engineers conduct research and design, organize and oversee the construction, operation and maintenance of process plant and installations. They establish programs for the coordination of manufacturing activities; and assess cost effectiveness and safety.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: studying functional statements, organizational charts and project information to determine functions and responsibilities of workers and work units and to identify areas of duplication;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: establishing work measurement programs and analyzing work samples to develop standards for labor utilization;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: analyzing workforce utilization, facility layout, operational data and production schedules and costs to determine optimum worker and equipment efficiencies;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: developing specifications for manufacture, and determining materials, equipment, piping, material flows, capacities and layout of plant and systems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: organizing and managing project labor and the delivery of materials, plant and equipment;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: establishing standards and policies for installation, modification, quality control, testing, inspection and maintenance according to engineering principles and safety regulations;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: inspecting plant to improve and maintain performance;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: directing the maintenance of plant buildings and equipment, and coordinating the requirements for new designs, surveys and maintenance schedules;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: advising management on new production methods, techniques and equipment; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: liaising with materials buying, storing and controlling departments to ensure a steady flow of supplies.

examples.title: Industrial and production quality control engineer

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Civil engineers conduct research, advise on, design, and direct construction; manage the operation and maintenance of civil engineering structures; or study and advise on technological aspects of particular materials.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting research and developing new or improved theories and methods related to civil engineering;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: advising on and designing structures such as bridges, dams, docks, roads, airports, railways, canals, pipelines, waste-disposal and flood-control systems, and industrial and other large buildings;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: determining and specifying construction methods, materials and quality standards, and directing construction work;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: establishing control systems to ensure efficient functioning of structures as well as safety and environmental protection;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: organizing and directing maintenance and repair of existing civil engineering structures;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: analyzing the behavior of soil and rock when placed under pressure by proposed structures and designing structural foundations; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: analyzing the stability of structures and testing the behavior and durability of materials used in their construction.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Environmental engineers conduct research, advise on, design and direct implementation of solutions to prevent, control or remedy negative impacts of human activity on the environment utilizing a variety of engineering disciplines. They conduct environmental assessments of construction and civil engineering projects and apply engineering principles to pollution control, recycling and waste disposal.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting research, assessing and reporting on the environmental impact of existing and proposed construction, civil engineering and other activities;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: inspecting industrial and municipal facilities and programs to evaluate operational effectiveness and ensure compliance with environmental regulations;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: designing and overseeing the development of systems, processes and equipment for control, management, or  remediation of water, air, or soil quality;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing environmental engineering assistance in network analysis, regulatory analysis, and planning or reviewing database development;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: obtaining, updating, and maintaining plans, permits, and standard operating procedures;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: providing engineering and technical support for environmental remediation and litigation projects, including remediation system design and determination of regulatory applicability;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring progress of environmental improvement programs;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: advising corporations and government agencies of procedures to follow in cleaning up contaminated sites to protect people and the environment; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: collaborating with environmental scientists, planners, hazardous waste technicians, engineers from other disciplines, and specialists in law and business to address environmental problems.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Mechanical engineers conduct research; advise on, design, and direct production of machines, aircraft, ships, machinery and industrial plant, equipment and systems; advise on and direct their functioning, maintenance and repair; or study and advise on mechanical aspects of particular materials, products or processes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising on and designing machinery and tools for manufacturing, mining, construction, agricultural, and other industrial purposes;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: advising on and designing steam, internal combustion and other non-electric motors and engines used for propulsion of railway locomotives, road vehicles or aircraft, or for driving industrial or other machinery;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: advising on and designing: hulls, superstructures and propulsion systems of ships; mechanical plant and equipment for the release, control and utilization of energy; heating, ventilation and refrigeration systems, steering gear, pumps, and other mechanical equipment;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: advising on and designing airframes, undercarriages and other equipment for aircraft as well as suspension systems, brakes, vehicle bodies and other components of road vehicles;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: advising on and designing non-electrical parts of apparatus or products such as word processors, computers, precision instruments, cameras and projectors;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: establishing control standards and procedures to ensure efficient functioning and safety of machines, machinery, tools, motors, engines, industrial plant, equipment, or systems; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: ensuring that equipment, operation and maintenance comply with design specifications and safety standards.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Chemical engineers conduct research and develop, advise on and direct commercial-scale chemical processes and production of various substances and items such as crude oil, petroleum derivatives, food and drink products, medicines, or synthetic materials. They direct maintenance and repair of chemical plant and equipment and study and advise on chemical aspects of particular materials, products or processes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting research and advising on, and developing commercial-scale chemical processes to refine crude oil and other liquids or gases, and to produce substances and items such as petroleum derivatives, explosives, food and drink products, medicines, or synthetic materials;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: specifying chemical production methods, materials and quality standards and ensuring that they conform to specifications;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: establishing control standards and procedures to ensure safety and efficiency of chemical production operations and safety of workers operating equipment or working in close proximity to on-going chemical reactions;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: designing chemical plant equipment and devising processes for manufacturing chemicals and products;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: performing tests throughout stages of production to determine degree of control over variables, including temperature, density, specific gravity, and pressure;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: developing safety procedures to be employed;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: preparing estimates of production costs and production progress reports for management; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: performing laboratory studies of steps in manufacture of new products and testing proposed process in small scale operation such as a pilot plant.

examples.title: Petroleum and natural gas chemical engineer

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: MINING ENGINEERS, METALLURGISTS AND RELATED PROFESSIONALS

definition_paragraphs.text: Mining engineers, metallurgists and related professionals conduct research on and design and develop and maintain commercial-scale methods of extracting metals from their ores, or minerals, water, oil or gas from the earth and of developing new alloys, ceramic and other materials, or study and advise on mining or metallurgical aspects of particular materials, products or processes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining the location and planning the extraction of coal, metallic ores, non-metallic minerals, and building materials, such as stone and gravel;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: determining most suitable methods of efficient mining and extraction, types of machinery to be used, planning layout and directing construction of shafts and tunnels;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: determining drilling site and devising methods of controlling the flow of water, oil or gas from wells;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: planning and directing storage, initial treatment and transportation of water, oil or gas;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: establishing safety standards and procedures and first-aid facilities, especially underground;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: conducting research, developing methods of extracting metals from their ores and advising on their application;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: investigating properties of metals and alloys, developing new alloys and advising on and supervising technical aspects of metal and alloy manufacture and processing;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: maintaining technical liaison and consultancy with other relevant specialists such as geologists and geophysicists; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: examining deposits or mines to evaluate profitability.

examples.title: Petroleum and natural gas extraction engineer

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers engineering professionals not classified elsewhere in minor group 214, Engineering professionals (excluding electrotechnology) or in minor group 215, Electrotechnology engineers. For instance, the group includes those who conduct research, advise on or develop engineering procedures and solutions concerning workplace safety, biomedical engineering, optics, materials, nuclear power generation and explosives.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: applying knowledge of engineering to the design, development, and evaluation of biological and health systems and products, such as artificial organs, prostheses, and instrumentation;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: designing devices used in various medical procedures, imaging systems such as magnetic resonance imaging, and devices for automating insulin injections or controlling body functions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: designing components of optical instruments such as lenses, microscopes, telescopes, lasers, optical disc systems and other equipment that utilize the properties of light;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: designing, testing, and coordinating the development of explosive ordnance material to meet military procurement specifications;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: designing and overseeing construction and operation of nuclear reactors and power plants and nuclear fuels reprocessing and reclamation systems;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: designing and developing nuclear equipment such as reactor cores, radiation shielding, and associated instrumentation and control mechanisms;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: assessing damage and providing calculations for marine salvage operations;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: studying and advising on engineering aspects of particular manufacturing processes, such as those related to glass, ceramics, textiles, leather products, wood, and printing; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: identifying potential hazards and introducing safety procedures and devices.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Electrotechnology engineers conduct research on and design, advise, plan and direct the construction and operation of electronic, electrical and telecommunications systems, components, motors, and equipment. They organize and establish control systems to monitor the performance and safety of electrical and electronic assemblies and systems.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: conducting research, advising on and directing the maintenance and repair of electrical, electronic and telecommunications products and systems; advising on and designing power stations and systems that generate, transmit and distribute electrical power; establishing control standards to monitor performance and safety of electrical, electronic and telecommunication systems and equipment.

definition_paragraphs.text: Electrical engineers conduct research and advise on, design, and direct the construction and operation of electrical systems, components, motors and equipment, and advise on and direct their functioning, maintenance and repair, or study and advise on technological aspects of electrical engineering materials, products and processes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising on and designing power stations and systems which generate, transmit and distribute electrical power;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: supervising, controlling and monitoring the operation of electrical generation, transmission and distribution systems;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: advising on and designing systems for electrical motors, electrical traction and other equipment, or electrical domestic appliances;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: specifying electrical installation and application in industrial and other buildings and objects;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: establishing control standards and procedures to monitor performance and safety of electrical generating and distribution systems, motors and equipment; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: determining manufacturing methods for electrical systems, as well as maintenance and repair of existing electrical systems, motors and equipment.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Electronics engineers conduct research on, design, and direct the construction functioning, maintenance and repair of electronic systems and study and advise on technological aspects of electronic engineering materials, products or processes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising on and designing electronic devices or components, circuits, semi-conductors, and systems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: specifying production or installation methods, materials and quality standards and directing production or installation work of electronic products and systems;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: establishing control standards and procedures to ensure efficient functioning and safety of electronic systems, motors and equipment;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: organizing and directing maintenance and repair of existing electronic systems and equipment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: designing electronic circuits and components for use in fields such as aerospace guidance and propulsion control, acoustics, or instruments and controls;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: researching and advising on radar, telemetry and remote control systems, microwaves and other electronic equipment;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: designing and developing signal processing algorithms and implementing these through appropriate choice of hardware and software; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: developing apparatus and procedures to test electronic components, circuits and systems.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Telecommunications engineers conduct research and advise on, design, and direct the construction functioning, maintenance and repair of telecommunication systems and equipment. They study and advise on technological aspects of telecommunication engineering materials, products or processes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising on and designing telecommunications devices or components, systems, equipment and distribution centers;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: specifying production or installation methods, materials, quality and safety standards and directing production or installation work of telecommunications products and systems;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: organizing and directing maintenance and repair of existing telecommunication systems, motors and equipment;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: researching and advising on telecommunications equipment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: planning and designing communications networks based on wired, fiber optical and wireless communication media;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: designing and developing signal processing algorithms and implementing these through appropriate choice of  hardware and software; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: designing telecommunications networks and radio and television distribution systems, including both cable and over the air.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Architects, planners, surveyors and designers plan and design landscapes, building exteriors and interiors; products for manufacture; and information for visual communication, publication and display. They conduct survey work to precisely position geographical features, design, prepare and revise maps, and develop and implement plans and policies for controlling the use of land.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: determining the objectives and constraints of the design brief by consulting with clients and stakeholders; formulating design concepts and plans that harmonize aesthetic considerations with technical, functional, ecological and production requirements; preparing sketches, diagrams, illustrations, animations; plans, maps, charts, samples and models to communicate design concepts and other information; analyzing photographs, satellite imagery, survey documents and data, maps, records, reports and statistics; undertaking research and analyzing functional, spatial, commercial, cultural, safety, environmental  and aesthetic  requirements.

definition_paragraphs.text: Building architects design commercial, industrial, institutional, residential and recreational buildings and plan and monitor their construction, maintenance and rehabilitation.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: developing new or improved architectural theories and methods;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: inspecting sites and consulting clients, management and other stakeholders to determine type, style and size of proposed buildings and alterations to existing buildings;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: providing information regarding designs, materials and estimated building times;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing project documentation, including sketches and scale drawings, and integrating structural, mechanical and aesthetic elements in final designs;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: writing specifications and contract documents for use by builders and calling tenders on behalf of clients;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: making necessary contacts to ensure feasibility of projects regarding style, cost, timing, and compliance with regulations;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: identifying and finding best solutions for problems regarding function and quality of interior environments of buildings and making necessary designs, drawings and plans;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: monitoring construction or rehabilitation work to ensure compliance with specifications and quality standards; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: maintaining technical liaison and consultancy with other relevant specialists.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Landscape architects plan and design landscapes and open spaces for projects such as, parks, schools, institutions, roads, external areas for commercial, industrial and residential sites, and plan and monitor their construction, maintenance and rehabilitation.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: developing new or improved theories and methods in landscape architecture;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: inspecting sites and consulting clients, management and other stakeholders to determine type, style and size  of proposed buildings, parks, roads and other open spaces;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: compiling and analyzing site and community data about geographical and ecological features, landforms, soils, vegetation, site hydrology, visual characteristics and human-made structures, to formulate land use and development recommendations, and for preparing environmental impact statements;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing reports, site plans, working drawings, specifications and cost estimates for land development, showing location and details of proposals, including ground modeling, structures, vegetation and access;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: writing specifications and contract documents for use by builders and civil engineering contractors and calling tenders on behalf of clients;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: making necessary contacts to ensure feasibility of projects regarding style, cost, timing, and compliance with regulations;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: identifying and finding best solutions for problems regarding function and quality of exterior environments and making necessary designs, drawings and plans;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: monitoring construction or rehabilitation work to ensure compliance with specifications and quality standards; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: maintaining technical liaison and consultancy with other relevant specialists.

definition_paragraphs.text: Product and garment designers design and develop products for manufacture and prepare designs and specifications of products for mass, batch and one-off production.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining the objectives and constraints of the design brief by consulting with clients and stakeholders;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: formulating design concepts for clothing, textiles, industrial, commercial and consumer products, and jewelry;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: harmonizing aesthetic considerations with technical, functional, ecological and production requirements;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing sketches, diagrams, illustrations, plans, samples and models to communicate design concepts;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: negotiating design solutions with clients, management, and sales and manufacturing staff;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: selecting, specifying and recommending functional and aesthetic materials, production methods and finishes for manufacture;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: detailing and documenting the selected design for production;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing and commissioning prototypes and samples; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: supervising the preparation of patterns, programs and tooling, and the manufacturing process.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Town and traffic planners develop and implement plans and policies for the controlled use of urban and rural land and for traffic systems. They conduct research and provide advice on economic, environmental and social factors affecting land use and traffic flows.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning layout and coordinating development of urban areas;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: compiling and analyzing data on economic, legal, political, cultural, demographic, sociological, physical and environmental factors affecting land use;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: conferring with government authorities, communities and specialists in fields such as architecture, planning, social science the environment and the law;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: devising and recommending use and development of land, and presenting narrative and graphic plans, programs and designs to groups and individuals;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: advising governments, companies and communities on urban and regional planning issues and proposals;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: reviewing and evaluating environmental impact reports;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: planning layout and coordinating development of urban areas;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: planning and the development of land areas for parks, schools, institutions, airports, roadways and related projects, and for commercial, industrial and residential sites; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: planning and advising on routing and control of road traffic and public transportation systems for efficiency and safety.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Cartographers and surveyors determine the exact position of, or prepare and revise digital, graphic and pictorial maps, charts or other visual representation of, natural and constructed features and boundaries of land, seas, underground areas and celestial bodies, applying scientific and mathematical principles.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: surveying, measuring and describing land surfaces, mines, underground surfaces, sea, river and lake beds;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: noting exact position of various features and recording survey data in digital form;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: making charts and maps to be used in determining navigable waters and channels and in planning construction of marine structures;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: planning and conducting aerial photographic surveys;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: designing, compiling and revising maps and charts using aerial and other photographs, satellite imagery, survey documents and data, existing maps and records, reports and statistics;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: undertaking research and development of surveying and photogrammetric measurement systems, cadastral systems and land information systems;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: studying and advising on technical, aesthetic and economic aspects of map production; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: maintaining technical liaison and consultancy with other relevant specialists.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Graphic and multimedia designers design information content for visual and audio communication, publication and display using print, film, electronic, digital and other forms of visual and audio media. They create special effects, animation, or other visual images for use in computer games, movies, music videos, print media and advertisements.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining the objectives and constraints of the design brief by consulting with clients and stakeholders;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: undertaking research and analyzing functional communication requirements;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: formulating design concepts for the subject to be communicated;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing sketches, diagrams, illustrations and layouts to communicate design concepts;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: designing complex graphics and animation to satisfy functional, aesthetic and creative requirements of the design brief;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: creating two-dimensional and three-dimensional images depicting objects in motion or illustrating a process, using computer animation or modeling programs;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: negotiating design solutions with clients, management, sales and production staff;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: selecting, specifying or recommending functional and aesthetic materials and media for publication, delivery or display;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: detailing and documenting the selected design for production; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: supervising or carrying out production in the chosen media.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Health professionals  conduct research, improve or  develop concepts, theories and operational methods, and apply scientific  knowledge relating to medicine, nursing, dentistry, veterinary medicine, pharmacy, and  promotion of health.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include: conducting research and obtaining scientific knowledge through the study of human and animal disorders and  illnesses and ways of treating them; advising on or applying preventive and  curative measures, or promoting health; preparing scientific papers and  reports. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Medical doctors study, diagnose, treat and prevent illness, disease, injury, and other physical and mental impairments in humans through the application of the principles and procedures of modern medicine. They plan,  supervise and evaluate the implementation of care and treatment plans by other health care providers, and conduct medical education and research activities.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: conducting physical examinations of patients and interviewing them and their families  to determine their health status ; ordering diagnostic tests and analyzing findings; prescribing and administering curative treatments and preventive measures; performing surgery and other clinical procedures;  monitoring  patients’  progress and response to treatment; advising on health, nutrition and lifestyle behaviors which aid prevention or treatment of disease and disorders; identifying and managing complications before, during and after childbirth; planning, managing and implementing referral plans for patients in need of specialized, long-term or other types of health care services; exchanging medical information with other health professionals to ensure continuing and comprehensive care; reporting births, deaths and notifiable diseases to government authorities; conducting research into human disorders and illnesses and preventive or curative methods.

definition_paragraphs.text: Generalist medical practitioners diagnose, treat and prevent illness, disease, injury, and other physical and mental impairments and maintain general health in humans through application of the principles and procedures of modern medicine.  They do not limit their practice to certain disease categories or methods of treatment, and may assume responsibility for the provision of continuing and comprehensive medical care to individuals, families and communities.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting physical examinations of patients and interviewing them and their families to determine their health status;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: ordering laboratory tests,  X-rays and other diagnostic procedures and analyzing findings to determine the nature of disorders or illnesses;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: providing continuing medical care for patients including prescribing, administering, counselling on and monitoring curative treatments and preventive measures;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing surgery and other clinical procedures;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: advising individuals, families and communities on health, nutrition and lifestyle which aid prevention or treatment of disease and disorders;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: providing referrals to patients and families for specialized care in hospitals, rehabilitation centers or other types of health care centers;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: identifying, managing and providing referrals for complications before, during and after childbirth;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: recording patients' medical information and history and exchanging information with specialist practitioners and other health workers as required for continuing medical care;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: reporting births, deaths and notifiable diseases to government authorities to meet legal and professional requirements;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: conducting research in human health and medical services and disseminating the findings such as through scientific reports; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: planning and participating in programs designed to prevent the occurrence and spread of common diseases.

examples.title: Resident medical officer specializing in general practice

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Specialist medical practitioners diagnose, treat and prevent illness, disease, injury, and other physical and mental impairments in humans, using specialized testing, diagnostic, medical, surgical, physical and psychiatric techniques, through application of the principles and procedures of modern medicine. They specialize in certain disease categories, types of patient or methods of treatment and may conduct medical education and research in their chosen areas of specialization.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting physical examinations of patients and interviewing them and their families  to determine their health status;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: considering medical information provided by a referring doctor or other health care provider;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: ordering specialized diagnostic tests to determine the nature of disorders or illnesses;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: prescribing, administering and monitoring patients' responses to treatments, medications, anesthetics, psychotherapies, physical rehabilitation programmes and other preventive and curative measures;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: performing surgery of a general or specialized nature;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: managing complications before, during and after childbirth;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: recording patients' medical information and exchanging information with other health professionals to ensure the provision of comprehensive care;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: reporting births, deaths and notifiable diseases to government authorities to meet legal and professional requirements;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: providing information to patients and families and communities about preventive measures, treatment and care for specific ailments;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: performing autopsies to determine cause of death;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: conducting research into specific human disorders and illnesses and preventive or curative methods and disseminating the findings such as through scientific reports; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: planning and participating in programs designed to prevent the occurrence and spread of specific diseases.

examples.title: Resident medical officer in specialist training

related_occupations.title: Resident medical officer specializing in general practitioner
related_occupations.raw: Resident medical officer specializing in general practitioner - 2211

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Nursing and midwifery professionals provide treatment and care services for people who are physically or mentally ill, disabled or infirm, and others in need of care due to potential risks to health including before, during and after childbirth. They assume responsibility for the planning, management and evaluation of the care of patients, including the supervision of other health care workers, working autonomously or in teams with medical  doctors and others in the practical application of preventive and curative measures.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: assessing, planning, providing and evaluating nursing and midwifery care for  patients according to the practice and standards of modern nursing and midwifery; coordinating the care of patients in consultation with other health professionals and members of health teams; developing and implementing care plans, treatments and therapies, including administering medications; monitoring and alleviating pain and discomfort experienced by patients using a variety of therapies, including the use of pain-killing drugs; monitoring patients' health condition, including progress of pregnancy and responses to curative treatment; providing information to patients, families and communities about a range of health issues, including prevention of illness, treatment and care, pregnancy and childbirth, and other topics; supervising and coordinating the work of other health care workers; conducting research on nursing and midwifery practice and preparing scientific papers and reports.

definition_paragraphs.text: Nursing professionals provide treatment, support and care services for people who are in need of nursing care due to the effects of ageing, injury, illness or other physical or mental impairment, or potential risks to health. They assume responsibility for the planning and management of the care of patients, including the supervision of other health care workers, working autonomously or in teams with medical doctors and others in the practical application of preventive and curative measures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning, providing and evaluating nursing care for patients according to the practice and standards of modern nursing;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: coordinating the care of patients in consultation with other health professionals and members of health teams;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: developing and implementing care plans for the biological, social, and psychological treatment of patients in collaboration with other health professionals;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: planning and providing personal care, treatments and therapies including administering medications, and monitoring responses to treatment or care plan;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: cleaning wounds and applying surgical dressings and bandages;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: monitoring pain and discomfort experienced by patients and alleviating pain using a variety of therapies, including the use of pain-killing drugs;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: planning and participating in health education programmes, health promotion and nurse education activities in clinical and community settings;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: answering questions from patients and families and providing information about prevention of ill-health, treatment and care;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: supervising and coordinating the work of other nursing, health and personal care workers; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: conducting research on nursing practices and procedures and disseminating findings such as through scientific papers and reports.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Midwifery professionals plan, manage, provide and evaluate midwifery care services before, during and after pregnancy and childbirth. They provide delivery care for reducing health risks to women and newborn children, working autonomously or in teams with other health care providers.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning, providing and evaluating care and support services for women and babies before, during and after pregnancy and childbirth according to the practice and standards of modern midwifery care;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: providing advice to women and families and conducting community education on health, nutrition, hygiene, exercise, birth and emergency plans, breastfeeding, infant care, family planning and contraception, lifestyle and other topics related to pregnancy and childbirth;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assessing progress during pregnancy and childbirth, managing complications and recognizing warning signs requiring referral to a medical doctor with specialized skills in obstetrics;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: monitoring the health status of newborns, managing complications and recognizing warning signs requiring referral to a medical doctor with specialized skills in neonatology ;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: monitoring  pain and discomfort experienced by women during labor and delivery and alleviating pain using  a variety of therapies, including the use of pain-killing drugs;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: reporting births to government authorities to meet legal and professional requirements;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: conducting research on midwifery practices and procedures and disseminating findings such as through scientific papers and reports; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: planning and conducting midwifery education activities in clinical and community settings.

definition_paragraphs.text: Traditional and complementary medicine professionals prevent, diagnose and treat illness, disease, injury, and other physical and mental impairments and maintain general health in humans by applying knowledge, skills and practices acquired through extensive study of  the theories, beliefs and experiences, originating in specific cultures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting physical examinations of patients and interviewing them and their families to determine their health status;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: developing and implementing treatment plans for physical, mental and psychosocial ailments using applications such as acupuncture, ayurvedic, homoeopathic and herbal medicine;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: evaluating and documenting patients' progress through treatment plans;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing health, nutrition and lifestyle advice to individuals, families and communities;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: prescribing and preparing traditional medicines, such as herbal, plant, mineral and animal extracts, to stimulate the body's capacity for self-healing;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: exchanging  information about patients with other health care workers as needed to ensure continuing and comprehensive health care; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: conducting research into traditional and complementary medicines and treatments and disseminating findings such as through scientific papers and reports.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Paramedical practitioners provide advisory, diagnostic, curative and preventive medical services for humans more limited in scope and complexity than those carried out by medical doctors. They work autonomously or with limited supervision of medical doctors, and  apply advanced clinical procedures for treating and preventing diseases, injuries and other physical or mental impairments common to specific communities.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting physical examinations of patients and interviewing them and their families  to determine their health status, and recording patients' medical information;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: performing basic or more routine medical and surgical procedures, including prescribing and administering treatments, medications and other preventive or curative measures, especially for common diseases and disorders;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: administering  or ordering diagnostic tests, such as x-ray, electrocardiogram, and laboratory tests;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing therapeutic procedures, such as injections, immunizations, suturing and wound care, and infection management;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: assisting medical doctors with complex surgical procedures;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: monitoring patients'  progress and response to treatment, and identifying signs and symptoms requiring referral to medical doctors;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: advising patients and families on diet, exercise and other habits which aid prevention or treatment of disease and disorders;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: identifying and referring complex or unusual cases to medical doctors,  hospitals or other places for specialized care; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: reporting births, deaths and notifiable diseases to government authorities to meet legal and professional reporting requirements.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Veterinarians diagnose, prevent and treat diseases, injuries and dysfunctions of animals. They may provide care to a wide range of animals or specialize in the treatment of a particular animal group or in a particular specialty area, or provide professional services to commercial firms producing biological and pharmaceutical products.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining the presence and nature of abnormal conditions by physical examination, laboratory testing and through diagnostic imaging techniques including radiography and ultrasound;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: treating animals medically and surgically, and administering and prescribing drugs, analgesics, and general and local anesthetics;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: performing surgery, dressing wounds and setting broken bones;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: rendering obstetric and dental services to animals;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: participating in programs designed to prevent the occurrence and spread of animal diseases;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: inoculating animals against, and testing for, infectious diseases and notifying authorities of outbreaks of infectious animal diseases;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: performing autopsies to determine cause of death;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: advising clients on health, nutrition and feeding, hygiene, breeding and care of animals; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: providing euthanasia services for animals.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Other health professionals provide health services related to dentistry, pharmacy, environmental health and hygiene, occupational health and safety, physiotherapy, nutrition, hearing, speech, vision and rehabilitation therapies.  This minor group includes all human health professionals, except doctors, traditional and complementary medicine practitioners, veterinarians, nurses, midwives and paramedical professionals.

Dentists diagnose, treat and prevent diseases, injuries and abnormalities of the teeth, mouth, jaws and associated tissues by applying the principles and procedures of modern dentistry. They use a broad range of specialized diagnostic, surgical and other techniques to promote and restore oral health.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: diagnosing diseases, injuries, irregularities and malformations of teeth and associated structures in the mouth  and jaw using a range of methods such as radiographs, salivary tests and medical histories;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: providing preventative oral health care such as periodontal treatments, fluoride applications and oral health promotion;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: administering anesthetics to limit the amount of pain experienced by patients during procedures;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: prescribing medication for relief of ongoing  pain after procedures;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: providing restorative oral care such as implants, complex crown and bridge restorations, and orthodontics, and repairing damaged and decayed teeth;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: providing surgical treatments such as extraction of teeth, biopsy of tissue, and performing orthodontic treatment;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: measuring and taking impressions of patients' jaws and teeth in order to determine the shape and size of dental prostheses;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: designing, making, and fitting prosthodontic appliances such as space maintainers, bridges, and dentures, or  writing fabrication instructions or prescriptions for dental prosthetic technicians;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: restoring oral function with removable and fixed oral prostheses;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: educating patients and families on dental hygiene, nutrition and other measures to take care of oral health; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: supervising dental hygienists, dental assistants and other staff.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Pharmacists store, preserve, compound, and dispense medicinal products and counsel on the proper use and adverse effects of drugs and medicines following prescriptions issued by medical doctors and other health professionals. They contribute to researching, testing preparing, prescribing and monitoring medicinal therapies for optimizing human health.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: receiving prescriptions for medicinal products from medical doctors and other health professionals, checking patients' medicine histories, and ensuring proper dosage and methods of administration and drug compatibility before dispensing;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing or supervising the preparation and labelling of liquid medicines, ointments, powders, tablets and other medications to fill prescriptions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: providing  information and advice to prescribers and clients regarding drug interactions, incompatibility and contra-indications, side effects, dosage and proper medication storage;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: collaborating with other health care professionals to plan, monitor, review, and evaluate the quality and effectiveness of the medicine therapy of individual patients, and the effectiveness of particular drugs or therapies;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: maintaining prescription files and recording issue of narcotics, poisons and habit-forming drugs in accordance with legal and professional requirements;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: storing and preserving vaccines, serums and other drugs subject to deterioration;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: advising clients on and supplying non-prescription medicines and diagnostic and therapeutic aids for common conditions;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: supervising and coordinating the work of pharmacy technicians, pharmacy interns and pharmacy sales assistants;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: conducting research to develop and improve pharmaceuticals, cosmetics and related chemical products;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: conferring with chemists, engineering professionals and other professionals about manufacturing techniques and ingredients;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: testing and analyzing drugs to determine their identity, purity and strength in relation to specified standards;

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: evaluating labels, packaging and advertising of drug products; and

tasks.label: m
tasks.text: developing information and risks of particular drugs.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: ENVIRONMENTAL AND OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND HYGIENE PROFESSIONALS

definition_paragraphs.text: Environmental and occupational health and hygiene professionals assess, plan and implement programs to recognize, monitor and control environmental factors that can potentially affect human health, to ensure safe and healthy working conditions, and to prevent disease or injury caused by chemical, physical, radiological and biological agents or ergonomic factors.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: developing, implementing and reviewing programs and policies to minimize potential environmental and occupational risks to health and safety;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing and implementing plans and strategies for the safe, economic and suitable disposal of commercial,  industrial, medical and household wastes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: implementing prevention programs and strategies for communicable diseases, food safety, waste water treatment and disposal systems, recreation and domestic water quality, contaminated and hazardous substances;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: identifying, reporting and documenting hazards, and assessing and controlling risks in the environment and workplace and advising on compliance with relevant law and regulations;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: developing, implementing and monitoring programs to minimize workplace and environmental pollution involving chemical, physical and biological hazards;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: advising methods to prevent, eliminate, control, or reduce the exposure of workers, students, the public and the environment to radiological and other hazards;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: promoting ergonomic principles within the workplace such as matching furniture, equipment and work activities to the needs of employees;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: providing education, information, training, and advice to persons at all levels on aspects of occupational hygiene and environmental health;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: recording and investigating injuries and equipment damage, and reporting safety performance; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: coordinating arrangements for the compensation, rehabilitation and return to work of injured workers.

related_occupations.raw: Specialist medical practitioner in public health - 2212

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Physiotherapists assess, plan and implement rehabilitative programs that improve or restore human motor functions, maximize movement ability, relieve pain syndromes, and treat or prevent physical challenges associated with injuries, diseases and other impairments. They apply a broad range of physical therapies and techniques such as movement, ultrasound, heating, laser and other techniques.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: administering muscle, nerve, joint and functional ability tests to identify and assess physical problems of patients;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: establishing treatment goals with patients and designing treatment programs to reduce physical pain, strengthen muscles, improve cardiothoracic, cardiovascular and respiratory functions, restore joint mobility, and  improve balance and coordination;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: developing, implementing and monitoring programs and treatments using the therapeutic properties of exercise, heat, cold, massage, manipulation, hydrotherapy, electrotherapy, ultraviolet and infra-red light and ultrasound in the treatment of patients;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: instructing patients and their families in procedures to be continued outside clinical settings;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: recording information on patients' health status and responses to treatment in medical records-keeping systems, and sharing information with other health professionals as required to ensure continuing and comprehensive care;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: developing and implementing programmes for screening and prevention of common physical ailments and disorders; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: supervising the work of physiotherapy assistants and others.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Dieticians and nutritionists assess, plan and implement programs to enhance the impact of food and nutrition on human health.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: instructing individuals, families and communities on nutrition, the planning of diets and preparation of food to maximize health benefits and reduce potential risks to health;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: planning diets and menus, supervising the preparation and serving of meals, and monitoring food intake and quality to provide nutritional care in settings offering food services;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: compiling and assessing data relating to health and nutritional status of individuals, groups and communities  based on nutritional values of food served or consumed;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: planning and conducting nutrition assessments, intervention programmes, and education and training to improve nutritional levels among individuals and communities;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: consulting with other health professionals and care providers to manage the dietary and nutritional needs of patients;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: developing and evaluating food and nutrition products to meet nutritional requirements; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: conducting research on nutrition and disseminating the findings at scientific conferences and in other settings.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Audiologists and speech therapists evaluate, manage and treat physical disorders affecting human hearing, speech, communication and swallowing. They prescribe corrective devices or rehabilitative therapies for hearing loss, speech disorders, and related sensory and neural problems and provide counselling on hearing safety and communication performance.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: evaluating hearing, speech and language performance in patients to determine the nature of hearing and communication disorders;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: administering hearing or speech/language tests or other examinations  using specialized diagnostic instruments and equipment, and interpreting test results alongside other medical, social and behavioral diagnostic data to determine appropriate courses of treatment ;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: planning, directing and participating in counselling, screening, speech rehabilitation  and other programs related to hearing and communication;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: prescribing hearing aids and other assistive devices according to patients’ needs and instructing them in their  use;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: planning and conducting treatment programs to manage physical disorders affecting speech and swallowing in patients such as stuttering and feeding disorders ;

tasks.label: f
