tasks.text: counselling and guiding hearing and/or language-impaired individuals, their families, teachers and employers; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: referring patients and families to additional medical or educational services if needed.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Optometrists and ophthalmic opticians provide diagnosis,  management and treatment services for disorders of the eyes and visual system. They counsel on eye care and prescribe optical aids or other therapies for visual disturbance.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: examining patients’ eyes and conducting diagnostic tests to assess ocular health and determine the nature and extent of vision problems and abnormalities;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: testing visual function using specialized instruments and equipment for measuring visual acuity and refractive error, function of visual pathways, visual fields, eye movements, freedom of vision and intraocular pressure;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: detecting, diagnosing and managing eye disease, including prescribing medications for the treatment of eye disease;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: consulting  with and referring patients to ophthalmologists or other health professionals if additional medical treatment is necessary;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: detecting and diagnosing eye movement disorders and defects of binocular function, and planning and managing treatment programs, including counselling patients in eye exercises to coordinate movement and focusing of eyes;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: prescribing corrective eyeglasses, contact lenses and other vision aids, and checking  optical devices for performance, safety, comfort and lifestyle; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: advising on visual health matters such as contact lens care, vision care for the elderly, optics, visual ergonomics, and occupational and industrial eye safety.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers health professionals not classified elsewhere in sub-major group 22, Health professionals. For instance, the group includes occupations such as podiatrist, occupational therapist and other health professionals.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: interviewing patients and conducting diagnostic tests  to determine their health status and the nature of physical or mental disorders, illnesses or other health problems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: developing and implementing treatment plans for injuries, illnesses and other physical and mental impairments;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: evaluating and documenting patients' progress through treatment plans, and referring patients and families to medical doctors or other health care providers for specialized, rehabilitative or other care services as needed;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assessing functional limitations of clients resulting from illness, disability or other impairment, and providing therapy;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: recommending environmental adaptations in the home, leisure, work and school environments on an individual or group basis to enable them to perform their daily activities and occupations;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: planning and implementing therapeutic programs on an individual and group basis for improving and maintaining physical, cognitive, emotional and social functioning, including through the use of arts and crafts, dance and movement, music and other recreational activities;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: identifying and prescribing treatments for conditions affecting the foot, ankle and related structures of the leg due to illness, disease or other physical impairment, and prescribing corrective footwear and advising on foot  care to manage foot ailments; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: performing minor surgical procedures such as on the foot and ankles.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Teaching professionals teach the theory and practice of one or more  disciplines at different educational levels, conduct research and improve or  develop concepts, theories and operational methods pertaining to their particular discipline, and prepare scholarly papers and books.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include:  conducting classes, courses, or tutorials at a particular educational level,  for educational and vocational purposes, including private lessons; conducting adult literacy programmes; teaching and educating persons learning difficulties or special needs; designing and modifying curricula; inspecting and advising on teaching methods and aids; participating in decisions concerning the organization of teaching  and related activities at schools and universities; conducting research in particular subjects to improve or develop concepts, theories or operational methods for application in industrial and other  fields; preparing scholarly papers and books.  Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: University and higher education teachers prepare and deliver lectures and conduct tutorials in one or more subjects within a prescribed course of study at a university or other higher educational institution. They conduct  research, and prepare scholarly papers and books.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: designing and modifying curricula and preparing courses of study in accordance with requirements;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing and delivering lectures and conducting tutorials, seminars and laboratory experiments;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: stimulating discussion and independent thought among students;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: supervising, where appropriate, experimental and practical work undertaken by students;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: administering, evaluating and marking examination papers and tests;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: directing research of post-graduate students or other members of department;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: researching into and developing concepts, theories and operational methods for application in industrial and other fields;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing scholarly books, papers or articles; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: participating in departmental and faculty meetings and in conferences and seminars.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Vocational education teachers teach or instruct vocational or occupational subjects in adult and further education institutions and to senior students in secondary schools and colleges. They prepare students for employment in specific occupations or occupational areas for which university or higher education is not normally required.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: developing curricula and planning course content and methods of instruction;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: determining training needs of students or workers and liaising with individuals, industry and other education sectors to ensure provision of relevant education and training programs;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: presenting lectures and conducting discussions to increase students' knowledge and competence;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: instructing and monitoring students in the use of tools, equipment and materials and the prevention of injury and damage;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: observing and evaluating students' work to determine progress, provide feedback, and make suggestions for improvement;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: administering  oral, written or performance tests to measure progress, evaluate training effectiveness and assess competency;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: preparing  reports and maintaining records such as student grades, attendance rolls, and training activity details;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: supervising independent or group projects, field placements, laboratory work, or other training;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: providing individualized instruction and tutorial or remedial instruction;  and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: conducting on-the-job training sessions to teach and demonstrate principles, techniques, procedures, or methods of designated subjects.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Secondary education teachers teach one or more subjects at secondary education level, excluding subjects intended to prepare students for employment in specific occupational areas.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: designing and modifying curricula and preparing educational courses of study in accordance with curriculum guidelines;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: establishing and enforcing rules for behavior and procedures for maintaining order among students;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing and giving lessons, discussions, and demonstrations in one or more subjects;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: establishing clear objectives for all lessons, units, and projects and communicating those objectives to students;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: preparing materials and classrooms for class activities;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: adapting teaching methods and instructional materials to meet students' varying needs and interests;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: observing and evaluating students’ performance and behavior;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing, administering and marking tests,  assignments and examinations to evaluate pupils' progress;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: preparing reports about pupils' work and conferring with other teachers and parents;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: participating in meetings concerning the school's educational or organizational policies; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: planning, organizing and participating in school activities such as excursions, sporting events and concerts.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: PRIMARY SCHOOL AND EARLY CHILDHOOD TEACHERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Primary school and early childhood teachers teach a range of subjects at the primary level of education and organize educational activities for children below primary school age.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: preparing programme of learning and giving instruction in a range of subjects at the primary education level, planning and organizing activities designed to facilitate children’s development of language, physical and social skills; preparing reports. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Primary school teachers teach a range of subjects at the primary education level.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: preparing daily and longer term lesson plans in accordance with curriculum guidelines;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: instructing children individually and in groups, using various teaching methods and materials (e.g. computers, books, games), adapting to children’s varying needs;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: maintaining discipline and good working habits in the classroom;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: planning and conduct activities with the children such as sporting activities, concerts and excursions;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: assigning and grading class work and homework;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: preparing, administering, and grading tests and assignments to evaluate children’s progress;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: observing and evaluating children’s performance and behavior;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: supervising children during classes and at other times in the school day, including the playground during breaks;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: participating in staff meetings and other sessions, and conferring with other teachers concerning educational issues; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: preparing for and attending parent meetings to discuss children’s progress and problems.

definition_paragraphs.text: Early childhood educators promote the social, physical, and intellectual development of children below primary school age through the provision of educational and play activities.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning and organizing individual and group activities designed to facilitate the development of children's motor skills, cooperative and social skills, confidence and understanding;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: promoting language development through story-telling, role-play, songs, rhymes and informal conversations and discussions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: leading  children in activities that, provide opportunities for creative expression through the media of art, dramatic play, music and physical fitness;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: observing children in order to evaluate progress and to detect signs of developmental, emotional or health related problems with parents;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: observing and assessing nutritional health, welfare and safety needs of students and identifying factors which may impede students' progress;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: supervising children's activities to ensure safety and resolve conflicts;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: guiding and assisting children in the development of proper eating, dressing and toilet habits;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: discussing progress or problems of children with parents and other staff members and identifying appropriate actions and referrals to other services; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with other service providers working with young children.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Other teaching professionals conduct research and advise on teaching methods, teach people with learning difficulties or special needs; teach non-native languages for migration and related purposes; give private tuition; teach arts, information technology and other subjects outside the mainstream primary, secondary and higher education systems and provide other teaching services not classified elsewhere in Sub-major group 23, Teaching professionals.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: conducting research and developing or advising on teaching methods, courses and aids; teaching physically handicapped children, young persons or adults or those with learning difficulties or other with special needs, teaching non-native languages for migration purposes; teaching students in practice, theory and performance of music, drama, dance, visual and other arts; developing, scheduling and conducting training programs and courses for information technology users.

definition_paragraphs.text: Education methods specialists conduct research and develop or advise on teaching methods, courses and aids. They review and examine teachers' work, the functioning of educational institutions and the results achieved and recommend changes and improvements.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: researching into current developments in curricula, teaching methods and other educational practices, and advising on necessary changes and possible improvements;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: evaluating and advising on contents of courses and methods of examination;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: researching into audio-visual and other teaching aids and advising on, planning and organizing their introduction in educational establishments;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: documenting subjects and courses developed, and evaluating new courses;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: providing  ongoing professional development, training and consultative services to teachers;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: organizing and conducting workshops and conferences to train teachers in new programs and methods;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: developing the structure, content and objectives of new educational courses and programs;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: visiting schools periodically and conferring with administrative and teaching staff on questions relating to curricula, teaching methods, equipment and other matters;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: visiting classrooms to observe teaching techniques and to evaluate teachers performance, and scholastic results obtained; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: preparing reports and making recommendations to educational authorities concerning possible changes and improvements in curricula, teaching methods, and other matters.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Special needs teachers teach physically or mentally handicapped children, young persons, or adults, or those with learning difficulties or other special needs. They promote the social, emotional, intellectual and physical development of their students.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assessing students' abilities and limitations with regard to intellectual, physical, social and emotional impairments, exceptional intellectual gifts, or other specific problems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: designing or modifying curricula and preparing and delivering programmes, lessons and activities adapted to students’ abilities and needs;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: giving instruction on an individual or group basis using special techniques or aids appropriate to students’ needs;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: employing special educational strategies and techniques during instruction to improve the development of sensory- and perceptual-motor skills, language, cognition, and memory;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: establishing  and enforcing rules for behavior and policies and procedures to maintain order among students;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: teaching academic subjects, and practical and self-help skills to students with  hearing, sight and other impairments;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: stimulating and developing students’ confidence interests, abilities, manual skills and coordination;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: conferring with other staff members to plan and schedule lessons for special needs students;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: preparing and maintaining student data and other records and submitting reports;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: administering various forms of assessment and evaluating progress of each student; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: conferring with students, parents, head teacher and other relevant  professionals involved in the students’ care to develop individual educational plans designed to promote students' development.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Other language teachers teach non-native languages to adults and children who are learning a language for reasons of migration, to fulfil employment requirements or opportunities, to facilitate participation in educational programmes delivered in a foreign language, or for personal enrichment. They work outside the mainstream primary, secondary and higher education systems, or in support of students and teachers within those systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assessing the level of ability and the extent of language difficulties of students,  and establishing students' needs and learning goals;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: planning, preparing and delivering lessons and workshops for groups and individuals with content and rate of progression adapted to students’ abilities and needs;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: designing and producing teaching materials and adapting existing materials;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assessing students' progress;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: assisting students in classroom settings where subjects are taught in a language other than the students’ native language;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: providing assistance to other teachers by designing special teaching programs for students still learning the main language of instruction;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: assigning and correcting work, and preparing and grading exams; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: assessing, recording and reporting on students’ progress.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Other music teachers teach students in the practice, theory and performance of music outside the mainstream primary, secondary and higher education systems, but may provide private or small group tuition as an extra curricular activity in association with mainstream educational institutions.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assessing the students’ level of ability and determining needs and learning goals;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: planning, preparing and delivering programs of study, lessons and workshops for individual students and groups;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing and presenting material on the theory and interpretation of music;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: instructing and demonstrating practical aspects of singing or of playing a particular instrument;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: teaching students to read and write musical notation;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assigning exercises and teaching pieces of music relevant to students’ level of ability, interests and talents;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: assessing students and offering advice, criticism and encouragement;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: revising curricula, course content, course materials and methods of instruction;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: preparing students for examinations, performances and assessments;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: arranging visits and tours to musical performances; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: organizing and assisting in auditions or performances of students' work.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Other arts teachers teach students in the practice, theory and performance of dance, drama, visual and other arts (excluding music) outside the mainstream primary, secondary and higher education systems, but may provide private or small group tuition as an extra curricular activity in association with mainstream educational institutions.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assessing the students’ level of ability and determining learning needs;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: planning, preparing and delivering programs of study, lessons and workshops for individual students and groups;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing and presenting material on the theory of the subject area being studied;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: instructing and demonstrating practical aspects of drama, dance, visual or other arts;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: assigning exercises and work relevant to students’ level of ability, interests and talents;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assessing students and offering advice, criticism and encouragement;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: revising curricula, course content, course materials and methods of instruction;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing students for examinations, performance and assessments;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: arranging visits and tours to exhibitions and  performances; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: organizing and assisting in performances or exhibitions of students' work.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Information technology trainers develop, schedule and conduct training programs and courses for computer and other information technology users outside the mainstream primary, secondary and higher education systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: identifying the information technology training needs and requirements of individual users and organizations;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing and developing instructional training material and aids such as handbooks, visual aids, online tutorials, demonstration models, and supporting training reference documentation;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: designing, coordinating, scheduling and conducting training and development programs that can be delivered in the form of individual and group instruction, and facilitating workshops meetings; demonstrations and conferences;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: monitoring and performing ongoing evaluation and assessment of training quality and effectiveness, and reviewing and modifying training objectives, methods and course deliverables;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: gathering, investigating and researching background materials to gain a full understanding of the subject matter and systems; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: keeping up-to-date with new product version releases, advances in software, and general information technology trends, writing end user products and materials such as user training, tutorial and instruction manuals, online help, and operating and maintenance instructions.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers teaching professionals not classified elsewhere in Sub-major group 23, Teaching professionals. For instance, the group includes those who provide private tuition in subjects other than foreign languages and the arts, and those who provide educational counselling to students.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assessing students’ level of ability and determining learning needs;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: planning, preparing and delivering programs of study, lessons and workshops for individual students and groups;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing and presenting material on the theory of the subject area being studied;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: instructing and demonstrating practical aspects of the subject area being studied;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: assigning exercises and work relevant to students’ level of ability, interests and aptitude;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assessing students and offering advice, criticism and encouragement;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: revising curricula, course content, course materials and methods of instruction;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing students for examinations and assessments;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: counselling students regarding educational issues such as course and program selection, class scheduling, school adjustment, truancy, study habits, and career planning;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: counselling students to help them understand and overcome personal, social, or behavioral problems affecting their education; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: preparing students for later educational experiences by encouraging them to explore learning opportunities and to persevere with challenging tasks.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Business and administration professionals perform analytical, conceptual and practical tasks to provide services in financial matters, human resource development, public relations and marketing, sales in the technical, medical, information and communication technology areas and conduct, reviews of organizational structures, methods and  systems as well as quantitative analyzes of information affecting investment programs.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include: collecting, analyzing and interpreting information on the financial viability, cost structures and trading effectiveness of organizations; conducting audits, preparing financial statements and controlling treasury systems for organizations; developing and reviewing financial plans and strategies, executing buy and sell orders, and negotiating the purchase and sale of commodities; developing, implementing and evaluating staff recruitment, training and development programs; researching, developing and implementing marketing and public relations campaigns; studying and developing methods and policies to improve and promote government and business operations and effectiveness; acquiring and updating knowledge of employers’ and competitors’ goods and services, and market conditions; assessing customers’ needs and explaining and demonstrating goods and services to them.

definition_paragraphs.text: Finance professionals plan, develop, organize, administer, invest, manage and conduct quantitative analyses of either financial accounting systems or funds for individuals, establishments and public or private institutions.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: preparing and organizing financial statements for an organization; reviewing financial materials of an organization; providing financial advice to individuals and organizations; preparing analytic reports concerning segments of the economy and the economy as a whole.

definition_paragraphs.text: Accountants plan, organize and administer accounting systems for individuals and establishments. Some occupations classified here examine and analyze the accounting and financial records of individuals and establishments to ensure accuracy and compliance with established accounting standards and procedures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising on, planning and installing budgetary, accounts controlling and other accounting policies and systems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing and certifying financial statements for presentation to management, shareholders and statutory or other bodies;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing tax returns, advising on taxation problems and contesting disputed claims before tax officials;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing or reporting on profit forecasts and budgets;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: conducting financial investigations in such matters as suspected fraud, insolvency and bankruptcy;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: auditing accounts and bookkeeping records;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: conducting investigations and advising management on financial aspects of productivity, stockholdings, sales, new products, etc.; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: devising and controlling a system to determine unit cost of products and services.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Financial and investment advisers develop financial plans for individuals and organizations, and invest and manage funds on their behalf.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: building and maintaining a client base;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: interviewing clients to determine financial status and objectives, risk tolerance and other information needed to develop financial plans and investment strategies;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: setting financial objectives, and developing and implementing strategies for achieving the financial objectives;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: arranging to buy and sell stocks and bonds for clients;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: monitoring investment performance, and reviewing and revising investment plans based on modified needs and changes in markets; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: recommending and arranging insurance cover for clients.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Financial analysts conduct quantitative analyses of information affecting investment programs of public or private institutions.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: analyzing financial information to produce forecasts of business, industry, and economic conditions for use in making investment decisions;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: maintaining knowledge and staying abreast of developments in the fields of industrial technology, business, finance, and economic theory;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: interpreting data affecting investment programs, such as price, yield, stability, future trends in investment risks, and economic influences;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: monitoring economic, industrial, and corporate developments through analysis of information obtained from  financial publications and services, investment banking firms, government agencies, trade publications, company sources, and personal interviews;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: recommending investments and investment timing to companies, investment firm staff, or the investing public;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: determining the prices at which securities should be syndicated and offered to the public;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: preparing plans of action for investment based on financial analyses;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: evaluating and comparing the relative quality of various securities in a given industry; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: presenting oral and written reports on general economic trends, individual corporations, and entire industries.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Administration professionals apply various concepts and theories related to improving the effectiveness of organizations and the individuals within the organization.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include:  evaluating the structure of organizations and suggesting areas of improvement; ensuring that the operational activities of an organization are consistent with the policy objectives of the organization; recruiting, training, developing, and counselling personnel within an organization.

definition_paragraphs.text: Management and organization analysts assist organizations to achieve greater efficiency and solve organizational problems. They study organizational structures, methods, systems and procedures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assisting and encouraging the development of objectives, strategies and plans aimed at achieving customer satisfaction and the efficient use of organizations’ resources;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: analyzing and evaluating current systems and structures;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: discussing current systems with staff and observing systems at all levels of organization;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: directing clients towards more efficient organization and developing solutions to organizational problems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: undertaking and reviewing work studies by analyzing existing and proposed methods and procedures such as administrative and clerical procedures;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: recording and analyzing organizations’ work flow charts, records, reports, manuals and job descriptions;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: preparing and recommending proposals to revise methods and procedures, alter work flows, redefine job functions and resolve organizational problems;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: assisting in implementing approved recommendations, issuing revised instructions and procedure manuals, and drafting other documentation; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: reviewing operating procedures and advising of departures from procedures and standards.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Policy administration professionals develop and analyze policies guiding the design, implementation and modification of government and commercial operations and programs.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: liaising and consulting with program administrators and other interested parties to identify policy needs;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: reviewing existing policies and legislation to identify anomalies and out-of-date provisions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: researching social, economic and industrial trends, and client expectations of programs and services provided;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: formulating and analyzing policy options, preparing briefing papers and recommendations for policy changes, and advising on preferred options;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: assessing impacts, financial implications, interactions with other programs and political and administrative feasibility of policies;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: conducting threat and risk assessments and developing responses; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: reviewing operations and programs to ensure consistency with policies of the organization.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Personnel and careers professionals provide professional business services related to personnel policies such as employee recruitment or development, occupational analyzes and vocational guidance.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising on and performing personnel functions relating to employee recruitment, placement, training, promotion, compensation, and employee-management relations or other areas of personnel policy;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: studying and analyzing jobs performed in an establishment by various means, including interviews with workers, supervisors and management, and writing detailed position, job or occupation descriptions from information obtained;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing occupational information or working on occupational classification systems;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: advising and working on the foregoing and other aspects of job and occupation analyzes in such fields as personnel administration, workforce research and planning, training, or occupational information and vocational guidance; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: studying and advising individuals on employment opportunities, career choices and further education or training that may be desirable.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Training and staff development professionals plan, develop, implement and evaluate training and development programs to ensure management and staff acquire the skills and develop the competencies required by organizations to meet organizational objectives.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: identifying training needs and requirements of individuals and organizations;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: setting human resource development objectives and evaluating learning outcomes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing and developing instructional training material and aids such as handbooks, visual aids, online tutorials, demonstration models, and supporting training reference documentation;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: designing, coordinating, scheduling and conducting training and development programs that can be delivered in the form of individual and group instruction, and facilitating workshops, meetings, demonstrations and conferences;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: liaising with external training providers to arrange delivery of specific training and development programs;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: promoting internal and external training and development, and evaluating these promotional activities;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring and performing ongoing evaluation and assessment of internal and external training quality and effectiveness, and reviewing and modifying training objectives, methods and course deliverables; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: gathering, investigating and researching background materials to gain an understanding of various subject matters and system.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: SALES, MARKETING AND PUBLIC RELATIONS PROFESSIONALS

definition_paragraphs.text: Sales, marketing and public relations professionals plan, develop, coordinate and implement programs of information dissemination to promote organizations, goods and services, and represent companies in selling a range of technical, industrial, medical, pharmaceutical and ICT goods and services.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: commissioning and undertaking market research, analyzing the findings, and planning advertising marketing and public relations activities; supporting business growth and development through the preparation and execution of marketing objectives, policies and programs; planning and organizing publicity campaigns; appraising and selecting material submitted by writers, photographers, illustrators and others to create favorable publicity; acquiring and updating knowledge of employers’ and competitors’ goods and services, and market conditions; assessing customers’ needs and explaining and demonstrating goods and services to them; visiting regular and prospective client businesses to establish and act on marketing opportunities; quoting and negotiating prices and credit terms, and completing contracts.

definition_paragraphs.text: Advertising and marketing professionals develop and coordinate advertising strategies and campaigns, determine the market for new goods and services, and identify and develop market opportunities for new and existing goods and services.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning, developing and organizing advertising policies and campaigns to support sales objectives;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: advising managers and clients on strategies and campaigns to reach target markets, creating consumer awareness and effectively promoting the attributes of goods and services;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: writing advertising copy and media scripts, and arranging television and film production and media placement;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: analyzing data regarding consumer patterns and preferences;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: interpreting and predicting current and future consumer trends;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: researching potential demand and market characteristics for new goods and services and collecting and analyzing data and other statistical information;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: supporting business growth and development through the preparation and execution of marketing objectives, policies and programs;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: commissioning and undertaking market research to identify market opportunities for new and existing goods and services; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: advising on all elements of marketing such as product mix, pricing, advertising and sales promotion, selling, and distribution channels.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Public relations professionals plan, develop, implement and evaluate information and communication strategies that create an understanding and a favorable view of businesses and other organizations, their goods and services, and their role in the community.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning and organizing publicity campaigns and communication strategies;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: advising executives on the public relations implications of their policies, programs and practices preparing and controlling the issue of news and press releases;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: undertaking and commissioning public opinion research, analyzing the findings and planning public relations and promotional campaigns;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: organizing special events, seminars, entertainment, competitions and social functions to promote goodwill and favorable publicity;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: representing organizations and arranging interviews with publicity media;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: attending business, social and other functions to promote the organization;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: commissioning and obtaining photographs and other illustrative material; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: selecting, appraising and revising material submitted by publicity writers, photographers, illustrators and others to create favorable publicity.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: TECHNICAL AND MEDICAL SALE PROFESSIONALS (Excluding ICT)

definition_paragraphs.text: Technical and medical sales professionals (excluding ICT) represent companies in selling a range of industrial, medical and pharmaceutical goods and services to industrial, business, professional and other establishments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: compiling lists of prospective client businesses using directories and other sources;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: acquiring and updating knowledge of employers’ and competitors’ goods and services, and market conditions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: visiting regular and prospective client businesses to establish and act on selling opportunities;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assessing clients' needs and resources and recommending appropriate goods or services;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: providing  input to product design where goods or services must be tailored to suit clients’ needs;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: developing reports and proposals as part of sales presentation to demonstrate benefits from use of good or service;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: estimating costs of installing and maintaining equipment or service;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: monitoring customers’ changing needs and competitor activity, and reporting these developments to sales management;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: quoting and negotiating prices and credit terms, and preparing and administering sales contracts;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: arranging delivery of goods, installation of equipment and the provision of services;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: reporting to sales management on sales made and the marketability of goods and services; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: consulting with clients after sale to ensure satisfaction resolve any problems and provide ongoing support.

examples.title: Medical and pharmaceutical products sales representative

related_occupations.title: Information and communications technology sales representative
related_occupations.raw: Information and communications technology sales representative - 2434

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY SALE PROFESSIONALS

definition_paragraphs.text: Information and communications technology (ICT) sales professionals sell, at the wholesale level, a range of computer hardware, software and other information and communications technology goods and services including installations and provide specialized information as required.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: soliciting orders and selling goods to retail, industrial, wholesale and other establishments;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: selling technical equipment, supplies and related services to business establishments or individuals;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: discussing the needs of new and existing customers and providing specialized information about how particular equipment, supplies and services meet those needs;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: quoting and negotiating prices and credit terms, and completing contracts and recording orders;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: updating customer records and preparing sales reports;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: arranging delivery of goods, installation of equipment and the provision of services; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: reporting customers' reactions and requirements to manufacturers.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Information and communications technology professionals conduct research, plan, design, write, test, provide advice and improve information technology systems, hardware, software and related concepts for specific applications; develop associated documentation including principles, policies and procedures; and design, develop, control, maintain and support databases and other information systems to ensure optimal performance and data integrity and security.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: researching information technology use in business functions; identifying areas for improvement and researching the theoretical aspects and operational methods for the use of computers; evaluating, planning and designing hardware or software configurations for specific applications including for Internet, Intranet and multimedia systems; designing, writing, testing and maintaining computer programs; designing and developing database architecture and database management systems; developing and implementing security plans and data administration policy, and administering computer networks and related  computing environments; analyzing, developing, interpreting and evaluating complex system design and  architecture specifications, data models and diagrams in the development, configuration and integration of computer systems.

records.title: SOFTWARE AND APPLICATIONS DEVELOPERS AND ANALYST

definition_paragraphs.text: Software and applications developers and analysts conduct research, plan, design, write, test, provide advice on and improve information technology systems, such as hardware, software and other applications to meet specific requirements.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: researching information technology use in business functions and identifying areas in which improvements could be made to maximize effectiveness and efficiency;  conducting research into the theoretical aspects of and operational methods for the use of computers; evaluating, planning and designing hardware or software configurations for specific applications; designing, writing, testing and maintaining computer programs for specific requirements; evaluating, planning and designing Internet, Intranet and multimedia systems.

definition_paragraphs.text: Systems analysts conduct research, analyze and evaluate client information technology requirements, procedures  or problems, and develop and implement proposals, recommendations, and plans to improve current or future information systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: consulting with users to formulate and document requirements and with management to ensure agreement on systems principles;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: identifying and analyzing business processes, procedures and work practices;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: identifying and evaluating inefficiencies and recommending optimal business practices, and system functionality and behavior;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: taking responsibility for deploying functional solutions, such as creating, adopting and implementing system test plans;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: developing functional specifications for use by systems developers;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: expanding or modifying systems to improve work flow or serve new purposes; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: coordinating and linking the computer systems within an organization to increase compatibility.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Software developers research, analyze and evaluate requirements for existing or new software applications and operating systems, and design, develop, test and maintain software solutions to meet these requirements.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: researching, analyzing and evaluating requirements for software applications and operating systems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: researching, designing, and developing computer software systems;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: consulting with engineering staff to evaluate interface between hardware and software;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: developing and directing software testing and validation procedures;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: modifying existing software to correct errors, to adapt it to new hardware or to upgrade interfaces and improve performance;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: directing software programming and development of documentation;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: assessing, developing, upgrading and documenting maintenance procedures for operating systems, communications environments and applications software; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: consulting with customers concerning maintenance of software system.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Web and multimedia development professionals combine design and technical knowledge to research, analyze, evaluate, design, programme and modify websites, and applications that draw together text, graphics, animations, imaging, audio and video displays, and other interactive media.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: analyzing, designing and developing Internet sites applying a mixture of artistry and creativity with software programming and scripting languages and interfacing with operating environments;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: designing and developing digital animations, imaging, presentations, games, audio and video clips, and Internet applications using multimedia software, tools and utilities, interactive graphics and programming languages;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: communicating with network specialists regarding web-related issues, such as security and hosting web sites, to control and enforce Internet and web server security, space allocation, user access, business continuity,  web site backup and disaster recovery planning;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: designing, developing and integrating computer code with other specialized inputs, such as image files, audio files and scripting languages, to produce, maintain and support web sites; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: assisting in analyzing, specifying and developing Internet strategies, web-based methodologies and development plans.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Applications programmers write and maintain programmable code outlined in technical instructions and specifications for software applications and operating systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: writing and maintaining program code outlined in instructions and specifications in accordance with quality accredited standards;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: revising, repairing or expanding existing programs to increase operating efficiency or adapt to new requirements;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: conducting trial runs of programs and software applications to confirm that they will produce the desired information;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: compiling and writing documentation of program development; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: identifying and communicating technical problems, processes and solutions.

records.title: SOFTWARE AND APPLICATIONS DEVELOPERS AND ANALYST NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers software and applications developers and analysts not classified elsewhere in minor group 251, Software and applications developers and analysts. For instance the group includes those professionals specializing in quality assurance including software testing.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: developing and documenting software testing plans;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: installing software and hardware and configuring operating system software in preparation for testing;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: verifying that programmes function according to user requirements and established guidelines;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: executing, analyzing and documenting results of software application tests and information and telecommunication systems tests; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: developing and implementing software and information system testing policies, procedures and scripts.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Database and network professionals design, develop, control, maintain and support the optimal performance and security of information technology systems and infrastructure, including databases, hardware and software, networks and operating systems.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: designing and developing database architecture, data structures,  dictionaries and naming conventions for information systems projects; designing, constructing, modifying, integrating, implementing and testing database management systems; developing and implementing security plans, data administration policy, documentation and standards; maintaining and administering computer networks and related computing environments; analyzing, developing, interpreting and evaluating complex system design and architecture specifications, data models and diagrams in the development, configuration and integration of computer systems.

definition_paragraphs.text: Database designers and administrators design, develop, control, maintain and support the optimal performance and security of databases.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: designing and developing database architecture, data structures, tables, dictionaries and naming conventions for information systems projects;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: designing, constructing, modifying, integrating, implementing and testing database management systems;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: conducting research and providing advice on the selection, application and implementation of database management tools;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: developing and implementing data administration policy, documentation, standards and models;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: developing policies and procedures for database access and usage and for the backup and recovery of data; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: performing the operational establishment and preventive maintenance of backups, recovery procedures, and enforcing security and integrity controls.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Systems administrators develop, control, maintain and support the optimal performance and security of information technology systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: maintaining and administering computer networks and related computing environments including computer hardware, systems software, applications software and all configurations;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: recommending changes to improve systems and network configurations, and determining hardware or software requirements related to such changes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: diagnosing hardware and software problems;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing data backups and disaster recovery operations; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating master consoles to monitor the performance of computer systems and networks, and to coordinate computer network access and use.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Computer network professionals research, analyze and recommend strategies for network architecture and development, implement, manage, maintain and configure network hardware and software, and monitor, troubleshoot and optimize performance.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: analyzing, developing, interpreting and evaluating complex system design and architecture specifications, data models and diagrams in the development, configuration and integration of computer systems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: researching, analyzing, evaluating and monitoring network infrastructure to ensure networks are configured to operate at optimal performance;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assessing and recommending improvements to network operations and integrated hardware, software, communications and operating systems;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing specialist skills in supporting and troubleshooting network problems and emergencies;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: installing, configuring, testing, maintaining and administering new and upgraded networks, software database applications, servers and workstations;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: preparing and maintaining procedures and documentation for network inventory, and recording diagnosis and resolution of network faults, enhancements and modifications to networks, and maintenance instructions; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring network traffic, and activity, capacity and usage to ensure continued integrity and optimal network performance.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: DATABASE AND NETWORK PROFESSIONALS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers database and network professionals elsewhere in Minor group 252, Database and network professionals.  For instance, the group includes information and communications technology security specialists.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: developing plans to safeguard computer files against accidental or unauthorized modification, destruction, or disclosure and to meet emergency data processing needs;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: training users and promoting security awareness to ensure system security and to improve server and network efficiency;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: conferring with users to discuss issues such as computer data access needs, security violations, and programming changes;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: monitoring current reports of computer viruses to determine when to update virus protection systems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: modifying computer security files to incorporate new software, correct errors, or change individual access status;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: monitoring use of data files and regulate access to safeguard information in computer files;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: performing risk assessments and executing tests of data processing system to ensure functioning of data processing activities and security measures; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: encrypting data transmissions and erecting firewalls to conceal confidential information as it is being transmitted and to keep out tainted digital transfers.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Legal, social and cultural professionals conduct research, improve or develop concepts,  theories and operational methods, or apply knowledge relating to the law,  storage and retrieval of information and artefacts, psychology, social welfare, politics, economics, history, religion, languages, sociology, other social sciences, and to arts and entertainment.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include: conducting research on legal problems; drafting laws and regulations; advising clients on legal cases; pleading and conducting cases in a court of law; presiding over judicial proceedings in a court of law; developing and maintaining library and gallery collections of archives; conducting research, improving or developing concepts, theories and operational methods or applying knowledge relating to the field of social sciences; conceiving, creating and performing in literary and artistic works; interpreting and communicating news, ideas, impressions and facts.

definition_paragraphs.text: Legal professionals conduct research on legal problems, advise clients on legal aspects of problems, plead cases or conduct prosecutions in courts of law, preside over judicial proceedings in courts of law, and draft laws and regulations.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: giving clients legal advice, undertaking legal business on clients’ behalf, and conducting litigation when necessary, or presiding over judicial proceedings- and pronouncing judgement in courts of law. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Lawyers give clients legal advice on a wide variety of subjects, draw up legal documents, represent clients before administrative boards or tribunals and plead  cases or conduct prosecutions in courts of justice, or instruct barristers to plead in higher courts of justice.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: giving clients legal advice on a wide variety of subjects and undertaking legal business on clients’ behalf;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: researching legal principles, statutes and previous court decisions related to specific cases;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: gathering evidence to formulate a defense or to initiate legal actions, by such means as interviewing clients and witnesses to ascertain the facts of a case;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: evaluate findings and develop strategies and arguments in preparation for presentation of cases;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: pleading clients’ cases before courts of law, tribunals and administrative boards or instructing barristers to plead in higher courts of justice;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: accepting briefs and pleading in the higher court;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: acting as prosecutor on behalf of the Government;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: negotiating settlements in matters which involve legal disputes;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: drafting legislation and preparing government regulations based on existing laws; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: drawing up legal documents such as contracts, real estate transactions and wills and preparing statements of legal opinions.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Judges preside over civil and criminal proceedings in courts of law.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: presiding over trials and hearings;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: interpreting and enforcing rules of procedure and making rulings regarding the admissibility of evidence;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: determining the rights and obligations of the parties involved, and, in cases tried by jury;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: instructing the jury on points of law that are applicable to the case;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: weighing and considering evidence in non-jury trials and deciding legal guilt or innocence or degree of liability of the accused or defendant;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: passing sentence on persons convicted in criminal cases, determining damages or other appropriate remedy in civil cases and issuing court orders; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: researching legal issues and writing opinions on the issues.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers legal professionals not classified elsewhere in Minor group 261, Legal professionals. For instance, the group includes those who perform legal functions other than pleading or prosecuting cases or presiding over judicial  proceedings.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: giving advice on legal aspects of various personal, business and administrative problems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: drawing up legal documents and contracts; and

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: determining, by inquest, the causes of any death not obviously due to natural causes.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Librarians, archivists and curators develop and maintain the collections of archives, libraries, museums, art galleries, and similar establishments.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: appraising or developing and organizing the contents of archives and artefacts of historical, cultural and artistic interest, and ensuring their safe-keeping and preservation; organizing the collections of and exhibitions at museums, art galleries and similar establishments; developing and the collections of and exhibitions at museums, art galleries and similar establishments; developing and maintaining the systematic collection of recorded and published material and making it available to users in libraries and related institutions; preparing scholarly papers and reports; conducting research.

definition_paragraphs.text: Archivists and curators collect, appraise and ensure the safekeeping and preservation of the contents of archives, artefacts and records of historical, cultural, administrative and artistic interest, and of art and other objects. They plan, devise and implement systems for the safekeeping of records and historically valuable documents.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: evaluating and preserving records for administrative, historical, legal, evidential and other purposes;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: directing or carrying out the preparation of indexes, bibliographies, microfilm copies and other reference aids to the collected material and making them available to users;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: researching the origin, distribution and use of materials and objects of cultural and historical interest;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: organizing, developing and maintaining collections of artistic, cultural, scientific or historically significant;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: directing or undertaking classification and cataloguing of museum and art gallery collections and organizing exhibitions;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: researching into, appraising, and developing, organizing and preserving historically significant and valuable documents such as government papers, private papers, photographs, maps, manuscripts audio-visual materials;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: preparing scholarly papers and reports;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: planning and implementing the computerized management of archives and electronic records;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: organizing exhibitions at museums and art galleries, publicizing exhibits and arranging special displays for general, specialized or educational interest; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: appraising and acquiring archival materials to build and develop an archival collection for research purposes.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Librarians and related information professionals collect, select, develop, organize and maintain library collections and other information repositories, organize and control other library services and provide information for users.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: organizing, developing and maintaining a systematic collection of books, periodicals and other printed, audio-visually and digitally recorded material;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: selecting and recommending acquisitions of books and other printed or audio-visually and digitally recorded material;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: organizing, classifying and cataloguing library material;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: managing library borrowing and inter-library loan facilities and information networks;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: retrieving material and providing information to business and other users based on the collection itself or on library and information-network systems;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: conducting research and analyzing or modifying library and information services in accordance with changes in users' needs;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: devising and implementing schemes and conceptual models for the storage, organization, classification and retrieval of information;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing scholarly papers and reports; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: performing manual, on-line and interactive media reference searches, making interlibrary loans and performing other functions to assist users in accessing library materials.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Social and related professionals conduct research, improve or  develop concepts, theories and operational methods, or apply knowledge  relating to philosophy, politics, economics, sociology, anthropology, history, philology, languages, psychology, and other social sciences, or they provide  social services to meet the needs of individuals and families in a community.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: formulating and applying solutions to  present or projected economic, political or social problems; researching into  and analyzing past events and activities and tracing the origin and evolution  of the human race; studying the origin and development of languages, or translating or interpreting them; studying mental processes and behavior of  individuals and groups; providing social services; preparing scholarly papers  and reports.  Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Economists conduct research, monitor data, analyze information and prepare reports and plans to resolve economic and business problems and develop models to analyze, explain and forecast economic behavior and patterns. They provide advice to business, interest groups and governments to formulate solutions to present or projected economic and business problems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: forecasting changes in the economic environment for short-term budgeting, long-term planning and investment evaluation;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: formulating recommendations, policies and plans for the economy, corporate strategies and investment, and undertaking feasibility studies for projects;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: monitoring  economic data to assess the effectiveness, and advise on the appropriateness, of monetary and fiscal policies;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: forecasting production and consumption of specific products and services based on records of past production and consumption and general economic and industry-specific conditions;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: preparing forecasts of income and expenditure, interest rates and exchange rates;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: analyzing factors that  determine labor force participation, employment, wages, unemployment and other labor market outcomes;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: applying mathematical formulae and statistical techniques and apply to test economic theories and devise solutions to economic problems;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: compiling, analyzing and interpreting economic data using economic theory and a variety of statistical and  other techniques;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: evaluating the outcome of political decisions concerning public economy and finances and advising on economic policy and possible courses of action in the light of past, present and projected economic factors and trends;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: preparing scholarly papers and reports;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: examining problems related to the economic activities of individual companies; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: conducting research on market conditions in local, regional or national areas to set sales and pricing levels for goods and services, to assess market potential and future trends and to develop business strategies.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Sociologists, anthropologists and related professionals investigate and describe the structure of societies, the origin and evolution of societies, and the interdependence between environmental conditions and human activities. They provide advice on the practical application of their findings in the formulation of economic and social policies.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: conducting research on the origin, development, structure, social patterns, organizations and inter-relationships of human society;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: tracing the origin and evolution of humanity through the study of changing characteristics and cultural and social institutions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: tracing the development of humanity through the material remains of its past, such as dwellings, temples, tools, pottery, coins, weapons, or sculpture;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: studying physical and climatic aspects of areas and regions, and correlating these findings with economic, social and cultural activities;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: developing theories, models and methods to interpret and describe social phenomena;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: evaluating the outcome of political decisions concerning social policy;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: analyzing and evaluating social data;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: advising on the practical application of  findings in the formulation of economic and social policies for population groups and regions, and for the development of markets; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: preparing scholarly papers and reports.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Philosophers, historians and political scientists conduct research into the nature of human experience and existence, phases or aspects of human history, and political structures, movements and behavior. They document and report on findings to inform and guide political and individual actions.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: researching, mostly by reasoning, into the general causes, principles and meanings of the world, human actions, experience and existence, and interpreting and developing philosophical concepts and theories;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: consulting and comparing primary sources, such as original or contemporary records of past events, and secondary sources such as archaeological or anthropological findings;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: extracting relevant material, checking its authenticity, and researching into and describing the history of a particular period, country or region, or a particular facet - for example economic, social or political - of its history;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: conducting research in such fields as political philosophy, or past and present theory and practice of political systems, institutions or behavior;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: observing contemporary political institutions and opinions, collecting data on them from various sources, including interviews with government and political party officials and other relevant persons;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: developing theories, models and methods to interpret and describe the nature of human experience and historical and political events and behavior ;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: presenting findings and conclusions for publication or use by government, political parties or other organizations and interested persons; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing scholarly papers and reports.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Psychologists research into and study the mental processes and behavior of human beings as individuals or in groups, and apply this knowledge to promote personal, social, educational or occupational adjustment and development.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning and carrying out tests to measure mental, physical and other characteristics such as intelligence, abilities, aptitudes, potentialities, etc., interpreting and evaluating results, and providing advice;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: analyzing the effect of heredity, social, occupational and other factors on individual thought and behavior;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: conducting counselling or therapeutic interviews with individuals and groups, and providing follow-up services;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: maintaining required contacts, such as those with family members, educational authorities or employers, and recommending possible solutions to, and treatment of, problems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: studying psychological factors in the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of mental illnesses and emotional or personality disorders, and conferring with related professionals;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: preparing scholarly papers and reports;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: formulating achievement, diagnostic and predictive tests for use by teachers in planning methods and content of instruction;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: conducting surveys and research studies on job design, work groups, morale, motivation, supervision and management; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: developing theories, models and methods to interpret and describe human behavior.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Social work and counselling professionals provide advice and guidance to individuals, families, groups, communities and organizations in response to social and personal difficulties.  They assist clients to develop skills and access resources and support services needed to respond to issues arising from unemployment, poverty, disability, addiction, criminal and delinquent behavior, marital and other problems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: interviewing  clients individually, in families, or in groups, to assess their situation and problems and determine the types of services required;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: analyzing the client's situation and presenting alternative approaches to resolving problems;
