tasks.text: providing fluoride treatments, cleaning and removing deposits from teeth, preparing cavities and placing fillings, administering local anesthesia, and performing other types of basic or routine clinical dental procedures;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: preparing, cleaning and sterilizing dental instruments, equipment and materials used in the examination and treatment of patients;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: getting patients ready for examination or treatment including explaining procedures and correct positioning;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: taking impressions of the mouth and dental radiographs to support diagnosis and fitting of dental prosthetics.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: MEDICAL RECORDS AND HEALTH INFORMATION TECHNICIANS

definition_paragraphs.text: Medical records and health information technicians develop, maintain and implement health records processing, storage and retrieval systems in medical facilities and other health care settings to meet the legal professional, ethical and administrative records-keeping requirements of health services delivery.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning, developing, maintaining  and operating a variety of health record indexes and storage and retrieval systems to collect, classify, store and analyze information;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: transcribing, compiling and processing patient medical records, admission and discharge documents, and other medical reports into records-keeping systems to provide data for patient monitoring and referral, epidemiological monitoring, research, billing, cost control and care improvement;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: reviewing records for completeness, accuracy and compliance with regulations;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: translating narrative descriptions and numeric information from medical records and other documents on health services delivery into codes associated with standard classification systems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: protecting the security of medical records to ensure that confidentiality is maintained and releasing information to authorized persons and agencies in accordance with regulations; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: supervising clerical and administrative workers involved in the maintenance of medical records.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Community health workers provide health education, referral and follow up, case management, and basic preventive health care and home visiting services to specific communities. They provide support and assistance to individuals and families in navigating the health and social services system.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: providing  information to families and communities on a range of health issues including nutrition, hygiene, infant and child care, immunizations, family planning,  risk factors and prevention of common infectious diseases, poisoning prevention, first aid for treatment of simple and common ailments, substance abuse, domestic violence, and other topics;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: visiting families in their homes to provide information on the health, social and other services available and support them in gaining access to these services;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: visiting families who do not usually access medical establishments to monitor on a regular basis certain conditions, such as progress with pregnancy, child growth and development, and environmental sanitation;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: distributing to households medical supplies for the prevention and treatment of endemic diseases such as malaria, pneumonia and diarrhea diseases, and instructing family and community members in the use of these products;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: conducting outreach efforts to groups who do not usually access medical establishments with information and basic medical supplies for prevention and management of certain health conditions for which they are most at risk, such as HIV/AIDS and other communicable diseases; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: collecting data from households and communities who do not usually access medical establishments for purposes of patient monitoring and referral and reporting to meet health regulations.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Dispensing opticians design, fit and dispense optical lenses based on a prescription from an ophthalmologist or optometrist for the correction of reduced visual acuity. They service corrective eyeglasses, contact lenses, low-vision aids and other optical devices.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: examining and taking facial and eye measurements of clients for fitting of eyeglasses and other optical devices;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: providing advice to clients with selection and maintenance of eyeglasses and frames, types of contact lenses  and other optical devices for performance, safety, comfort and lifestyle;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: interpreting optical prescriptions and preparing work order for optical laboratory for grinding  and mounting of lenses in frames, preparation of contact lenses and other required work; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: verifying exactness of finished optical appliances and devices to the original prescription and  fit of clients.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Physiotherapy technicians and assistants provide physical therapeutic treatments to patients in circumstances where functional movement is threatened by injury, disease or impairment. Therapies are usually provided as per rehabilitative plans established by a physiotherapist or other health professional.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: administering manual treatments such as massage therapy or pressure point therapy;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: administering electrical modality treatments, ultrasound, and other physical therapies using specialized techniques and equipment, including infra-red lamps, wet compresses, and herbal and mineral therapies;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: instructing, motivating, safeguarding and assisting patients as they practice physical exercises, relaxation techniques and functional activities;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: conferring with physiotherapists or other health care providers to evaluate patient information for planning, modifying, and coordinating treatment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: monitoring and recording patients' progress during treatments, including measuring their range-of-joint motion and vital signs; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: fitting patients for orthopedic braces, prostheses, and other physical supportive devices such as crutches, and instructing patients in the use of such devices.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Medical assistants perform basic clinical and administrative tasks to support patient care under the direct supervision of a medical practitioner or other health professional.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: interviewing patients and their families to obtain information on their health status and medical history;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: assisting medical doctors and other health professionals to examine and treat patients, including measuring and recording vital signs, administering medications, and performing routine clinical procedures such as giving injections and removing sutures ;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: getting patients ready for examination and treatment, including explaining procedures and showing them to examination rooms;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing and handling medical instruments and supplies, including sterilizing instruments and disposing of contaminated supplies in accordance with safety procedures;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: collecting blood, tissue or other specimens, and preparing them for laboratory testing;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: providing information to patients and families on health care topics including medications prescribed by a medical doctor or other health professional;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: providing prescription and drug refill information to pharmacies;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: maintaining cleanliness of patient waiting and examination rooms;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: recording information on patients' medical history, diagnostic testing and treatment procedures and results, and other information in medical records-keeping systems; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: scheduling appointments with patients, and preparing documentation required for billing, reporting and insurance purposes.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: ENVIRONMENTAL AND OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH INSPECTORS AND ASSOCIATES

definition_paragraphs.text: Environmental and occupational health inspectors and associates investigate the implementation of rules and regulations relating to environmental factors that may affect human health, safety in the workplace, and safety of processes for the production of goods and services. They may implement and evaluate programs to restore or improve safety and sanitary conditions under the supervision of a health professional.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising employers’ and workers’ representatives on the  implementation of government and other rules and regulations concerning occupational safety and the working environment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: inspecting places of work to ensure that the working environment, machinery and equipment conform to government and other rules, regulations and standards related to sanitation and/or occupational and environmental health and safety;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: giving advice on environmental sanitary problems and techniques;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: inspecting places of work and, by interviews, observations and other means, obtaining information about work practices and accidents to determine compliance with safety rules and regulations;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: inspecting areas of production, processing, transport, handling, storage and sale of products to ensure conformity with government and other rules, regulations and standards;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: advising enterprises and the general public on the  implementation of government and other rules and regulations concerning hygiene, sanitation, purity and grading of primary products, food, drugs, cosmetics and similar goods;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: inspecting establishments to ensure that they conform to government and other rules and regulations concerning emission of pollutants and disposal of dangerous wastes;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: initiating action to maintain or improve hygiene and prevent pollution of water, air, food or soil;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: promoting preventive and corrective measures such as control of disease carrying organisms and of harmful substances in the air, hygienic food handling, proper disposal of waste and cleaning of public places; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: estimating quantities and costs of materials and labor required for health, safety and sanitation remediation projects;

examples.title: Electric vehicle (EV) fleet and depot safety officer

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Ambulance workers provide emergency health care to patients who are injured, sick, infirm, or otherwise physically or mentally impaired prior to and during transport to medical facilities.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assessing health status of persons involved in accidents, natural disasters and other emergency situations, and determining needs for immediate and specialized medical assistance;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: performing medical procedures and administering drugs and other therapies according to protocol for emergency medical treatment, including resuscitating and defibrillating patients and operating life-support equipment;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: monitoring changes in health status of patients during transport to and from medical, rehabilitation and other health care facilities;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing information and training to community groups and essential service workers in first aid for initial care of an illness or injury;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: attending and/or patrolling large-scale public gatherings and other events where health emergencies are more  likely to occur; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: recording information on patients' conditions and treatments provided in medical records-keeping systems.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: HEALTH ASSOCIATE PROFESSIONALS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers health associate  professionals not classified elsewhere in Sub-major group 32, Health associate professionals. For instance the group includes occupations such as chiropractor, osteopath and other health associate professionals.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: interviewing and examining patients to obtain information on their health status and the nature and extent of injury, illness or other physical or mental health problem;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: administering therapeutic care and treatment to patients, including the manual and physical chiropractic an osteopathic techniques;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: monitoring patients' progress through treatment plans, and identifying signs and symptoms requiring referral to a medical doctor or other health professional;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: recording information on patients' health status and responses to treatment in medical records-keeping systems; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: sharing information with other health care providers when required to ensure continuing and comprehensive care.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Business and administration associate professionals perform mostly technical tasks connected with the practical application of knowledge relating to financial accounting and transaction matters, mathematical calculations, human resource development, selling and buying financial instruments, specialized secretarial tasks, and enforcing or applying relevant government rules.  Also included are workers who provide business services such as customs clearance, conference planning, job placements, buying and selling real estate or bulk commodities, and serving as agents for performers such as athletes and artists.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include recording and transmitting buy and sell orders for securities, stocks, bonds or other financial instruments and for foreign exchange for future or immediate delivery; submitting credit and loan applications to management with recommendations for approval or rejection; approving or rejecting applications within authorized limits ensuring that credit standards of the institution are respected; maintaining complete records of all financial transactions of an undertaking according to general bookkeeping principles, with guidance from Accountants; assisting in planning and performing mathematical, statistical, actuarial, accounting and related calculations; selling and buying financial instruments.

definition_paragraphs.text: Financial and mathematical associate professionals place a value on various items and property, maintain records of financial transactions, analyze loan application information and render a decision, buy and sell financial instruments, and perform mathematical and related calculations.

Recording and transmitting buy and sell orders for securities, stocks, bonds or other financial instruments and for foreign exchange for future or immediate delivery; submitting credit and loan applications to management with recommendations for approval or rejection; or approve or reject applications within authorized limits ensuring that credit standards of the institution are respected; maintaining complete records of all financial transactions of an undertaking according to general bookkeeping principles, with guidance from Accountants; assisting in planning and performing mathematical, statistical, actuarial, accounting and related calculations.

records.title: SECURITIES AND FINANCE DEALERS AND BROKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Securities and finance dealers and brokers buy and sell securities, stocks, bonds and other financial instruments, and deal on the foreign exchange, on spot, or on futures markets, on behalf of their own company or for customers on a commission basis. They recommend transactions to clients or senior management.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: obtaining information about the financial circumstances of customers and companies in which investments may be made;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: analyzing market trends for securities, bonds, stocks and other financial instruments, including foreign exchange;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: informing prospective customers about market conditions and prospects;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: advising on and participating in the negotiation of terms for, and organization of, loans and placement of stocks and bonds in the financial market to raise capital for customers; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: recording and transmitting buy and sell orders for securities, stocks, bonds or other financial instruments and for foreign exchange for future or immediate delivery.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Credit and loan officers analyze and evaluate financial information on applications for credit and loans and determine approval or disapproval of the client for the credit or loan or recommend to management approval or disapproval.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: interviewing applicants for personal, mortgage, student and business loans;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: researching and evaluating loan applicant’s financial status, references, credit and ability to repay the loan;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: submitting credit and loan applications to management with recommendations for approval or rejection;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: approving or rejecting loan applications within authorized limits ensuring that credit standards of the institution are respected;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: keeping records of payments, and preparing routine letters requesting payment for overdue accounts and forwarding these for legal action; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: completing credit and loan documentation.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Accounting associate professionals maintain complete records of financial transactions of an undertaking and verify accuracy of documents and records relating to such transactions.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: maintaining complete records of all financial transactions of an undertaking according to general bookkeeping principles, with guidance from Accountants;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: verifying accuracy of documents and records relating to payments, receipts and other financial transactions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing financial statements and reports for specified periods;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: applying knowledge of bookkeeping principles and practices in order to identify and solve problems arising in the course of their work;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: using standard computer software packages to perform accounting and related calculations; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: supervising the work of accounts and bookkeeping clerks.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: STATISTICAL, MATHEMATICAL AND RELATED ASSOCIATE PROFESSIONALS

definition_paragraphs.text: Statistical, mathematical and actuarial associate professionals assist in planning the collection, processing and presentation of statistical, mathematical or actuarial data and in carrying out these operations, usually working under the guidance of statisticians, mathematicians and actuaries.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assisting in planning and performing statistical, mathematical, actuarial, and related calculations;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing detailed estimates of quantities and costs of materials and labor required for statistical census and survey operations;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: performing technical tasks connected with establishing, maintaining and using registers and sampling frames for census and survey operations;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing technical tasks connected with data collection and quality control operations in censuses and surveys;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: using standard computer software packages to perform mathematical, actuarial, statistical, accounting and related calculations;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: preparing statistical, mathematical, actuarial, accounting and other results for presentation in graphical or tabular form;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: applying knowledge of statistical, mathematical, actuarial, accounting and related principles and practices in order to identify and solve problems arising in the course of their work; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: supervising the work of statistical clerks.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Valuers and loss assessors value property and various goods and assess losses covered by insurance policies.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining the quality or value of raw materials, real estate, industrial equipment, personal and household effects, works of art, gems and other objects;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: assessing the extent of damage or loss and liabilities of insurance companies and underwriters for losses covered by insurance policies;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: obtaining records of sales and value of similar items or property;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: inspecting items or property to evaluate condition, size, and construction; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: preparing reports of value, outlining the estimation factors and methods used.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: SALES AND PURCHASING AGENTS AND BROKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Sales and purchasing agents and brokers represent companies, governments and other organizations to  buy and sell commodities, goods, insurance, shipping and other services to industrial, professional, commercial or other establishments, or act as independent agents to bring together buyers and sellers of commodities and services.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include obtaining information about,  monitoring and analyzing market trends and conditions and employer’s and competitors goods and services; obtaining information about clients’ needs and identifying suitable products and services; explaining and demonstrating products and services to clients; negotiating prices, contracts, terms, conditions and shipping arrangements for purchase or sale of goods, services or commodities.

definition_paragraphs.text: Insurance representatives advise on and sell life, accident, automobile, liability, endowment, fire, marine and other types of insurance to new and established clients.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: obtaining information about customers’ circumstances necessary to determine appropriate type of insurance and conditions;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: negotiating with customers to determine type and degree of risk for which insurance is required;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: explaining details of insurance and conditions, risk coverage premiums and benefits to customers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assisting clients to determine the type and level of coverage required, calculating premiums and establishing method of payment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: negotiating and placing reinsurance contracts; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: advising on, negotiating terms for and placing insurance contracts for large or special types of projects, installations or risks.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Commercial sales representatives represent companies to sell various goods and services to businesses and other organizations and provide product specific information as required.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: soliciting orders and selling goods to retail, industrial, wholesale and other establishments;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: selling equipment, supplies and related services to business establishments or individuals;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: obtaining and updating knowledge of market conditions and of employer’s and competitors’ goods and services;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing prospective customers with information about the characteristics and functions of the products and equipment for sale, and demonstrating its use or qualities;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: reporting customers’ reactions and requirements to suppliers and manufacturers; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: following up clients to ensure satisfaction with products purchased.

related_occupations.title: Information and communications technology sales professional
related_occupations.raw: Information and communications technology sales professional - 2434

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Buyers buy goods and services for use or resale on behalf of industrial, commercial, government or other establishments and organizations.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining or negotiating contract terms and conditions, awarding supplier contracts or recommending contract awards for the purchase of equipment, raw materials products, services  and the purchasing of merchandise for resale;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: obtaining information about requirements and stock and developing specifications for quantity and quality to be purchased, costs, delivery dates and other contract conditions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: purchasing general and specialized equipment, materials or business services for use or for further processing by their establishment;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: inviting tenders, consulting with suppliers and reviewing quotations;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: purchasing merchandise for resale by retail or wholesale establishments;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: studying market reports, trade periodicals and sales promotion materials and visiting trade shows, showrooms, factories and product design events;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: interviewing  suppliers and negotiating prices, discounts, credit terms and transportation arrangements;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: overseeing distribution of merchandise to outlets and maintaining adequate stock levels; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: establishing delivery schedules, monitoring progress and contacting clients and suppliers to resolve problems.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Trade brokers buy and sell commodities and shipping services, usually in bulk, on behalf of their own company or for customers on a commission basis.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: establishing contact between buyers and sellers of commodities;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: discussing buying or selling requirements of clients and giving advice accordingly;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: buying  and selling cargo space on ships;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: negotiating purchase or sale of commodities and commodity futures;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: finding cargo and/or storage space for commodities and negotiating freight, shipping and storage charges; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: monitoring and analyzing market trends and other factors affecting the supply and demand for commodities and shipping services.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Business service agents establish contacts to sell various business services such as advertising space in the media, carry out customs clearance activities ensuring that necessary documents are in order, match jobseekers with vacancies, find workers for employers, arrange contracts for the performance of athletes, entertainers and artists, as well as for the publication of books, the production of plays, or the recording, performing and sale of music, plan and organize conferences and similar events.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: Carrying out customs clearing procedures for exports or imports; arranging and coordinating conference and event services, such as conference facilities, catering, signage, displays, audiovisual and computer equipment, accommodation, transport and social events, for participants; matching jobseekers with vacancies; finding workers for vacant posts for employers; showing real estate properties to be sold or leased to prospective buyers or tenants and explaining terms of sale or conditions of rent or lease; selling by auction various kinds of property, cars, commodities, livestock, art, jewelry and other objects; arranging contracts for performers and performances.

definition_paragraphs.text: Clearing and forwarding agents carry out customs clearing procedures and ensure that insurance, export/import licenses and other formalities are in order.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: carrying out customs clearing procedures for exports or imports;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: ensuring that insurance is in order;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: ensuring that export/import licenses and other formalities are in order;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: signing and issuing bills of lading; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: checking import/export documentation to determine cargo contents, and classifying goods into different fee or tariff groups, using a tariff coding system.

definition_paragraphs.text: Conference and event planners organize and coordinate services for conferences, events, functions, banquets and seminars.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: promoting conferences, conventions and trade shows to potential customers;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: responding to inquiries concerning services provided and costs for room and equipment hire, catering and related services;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: meeting with clients to discuss their needs and outlining package options to meet these needs;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: arranging and coordinating services, such as, conference facilities, catering, signage, displays, audiovisual and computer equipment, accommodation, transport and social events, for participants, logistical arrangements for presenters;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: organizing registration of participants;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: negotiating the type and costs of services to be provided within budget; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: overseeing work by contractors and reporting on variations to work orders.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Employment agents and contractors match jobseekers with vacancies, find workers for employers and contract labor for particular projects at the request of enterprises and other organizations including government, institutions, or find places for jobseekers for a commission.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: matching jobseekers with vacancies;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: finding workers for vacant posts against a commission from the employer or worker;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: discussing with enterprises/organizations the needed skills and other characteristics of the workers to be employed or contracted;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: finding workers with appropriate skills, etc., and undertaking the necessary formalities according to national or international regulations and requirements;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: ensuring that the employment contracts meet legal requirements and signing them; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: advising on training schemes.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: REAL ESTATE AGENTS AND PROPERTY MANAGERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Real estate agents and property managers arrange the sale, purchase, rental and lease of real property, usually on behalf of clients and on a commission basis.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: obtaining information about properties to be sold or leased, the circumstances of their owner and the needs of prospective buyers or tenants;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: showing properties to be sold or leased to prospective buyers or tenants and explaining terms of sale or conditions of rent or lease;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: facilitating negotiations with tenants and owners on rents and fees;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: drawing up leasing and sale agreements and estimating costs;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: arranging signing of lease agreements and transfer of property rights;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: collecting rent and bond monies on behalf of owner and inspecting properties before, during and after tenancies; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: ensuring the availability of workers to perform maintenance of the properties.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: BUSINESS SERVICES AGENTS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers business services agents not classified elsewhere in Minor group 333, Business services agents. For instance, the group includes those who establish business  contacts, sell business services such as advertising space in the media, arrange contracts for performances of athletes, entertainers and  artists, for the publication of books, the production of plays, or the recording, performance and sale of music and who sell property and goods by auction.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: obtaining information about services to be sold and needs of prospective buyers;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: negotiating contracts on behalf of seller or buyer and explaining terms of sale and payment to client;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: signing agreements on behalf of seller or buyer and ensuring that contract is honored;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: making sure that the business service purchased is made available to the buyer in the agreed format at the agreed time; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: selling by auction various kinds of property, cars, commodities, livestock, art, jewelry and other objects.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Administrative and specialized secretaries provide organizational, communication and documentation support services, utilizing specialized knowledge of the business activity of the organization in which they are employed.  They take supervisory responsibility for office clerks in the organization.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: coordinating, assigning and reviewing the work of clerical support workers; desktop publishing; preparing and processing legal documents and papers, such as deeds, wills, affidavits and briefs; implementing and supporting the communication, documentation and internal managerial coordination activities of an organizational unit, on some occasions utilizing specialized knowledge of the business activity of  the organization; scheduling and confirming meetings and appointments and communicating messages for clients; compiling, recording and reviewing legal and medical records, reports, documents and correspondence.

definition_paragraphs.text: Office supervisors supervise and coordinate the activities of workers in major group 4, Clerical support workers.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: coordinating, assigning and reviewing the work of clerks engaged in the following duties: word processing, record keeping and filing, operating telephones and switchboards; data entry, desktop publishing and other activities involving general office and administrative skills;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: establishing work schedules and procedures and co-coordinating activities with other work units or departments;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: resolving work-related problems and preparing and submitting progress and other reports;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: training and instructing employees in job duties, safety procedures and company policies, or arranging for training to be provided;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: evaluating employees’ job performance and conformance to regulations, and recommending appropriate personnel action; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assisting in recruitment, interviewing, and selection of employees.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Legal secretaries apply specialized knowledge of legal terminology and procedures in providing support to legal professionals with communication, documentation and internal managerial coordination activities, in law offices, legal departments of large firms and governments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: preparing and processing legal documents and papers, such as deeds, wills, affidavits and briefs;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: reviewing and proofreading documents and correspondence to ensure compliance with legal procedures;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: mailing, faxing, or arranging for delivery of legal correspondence to clients, witnesses, and court officials;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: organizing and maintaining documents, case files and law libraries;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: screening requests for meetings, scheduling and organizing meetings;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assisting in the preparation of budgets, monitoring of expenditures, drafting of contracts and purchasing or acquisition orders; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: supervising the work of office support workers.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Administrative and executive secretaries perform liaison, coordination and organizational tasks in support of managers and professionals and/or prepare correspondence, reports and records of proceedings and other specialized documentation.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: drafting administrative correspondence and minutes;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: obtaining, proposing and monitoring deadlines and follow-up dates;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: screening requests for meetings, scheduling and organizing meetings and travel arrangements;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assisting in the preparation of budgets, monitoring of expenditures, drafting of contracts and purchasing or acquisition orders;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: liaising with other staff about a range of matters relating to the organization’s operations;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: writing and answering business or technical letters and other similar correspondence;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: preparing verbatim reports of proceedings in legislative assemblies, courts of law or other places  using shorthand or  specialized office equipment;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: supervising the work of  clerical support workers.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Medical secretaries, using specialized knowledge of medical terminology and health care delivery procedures, assist health professionals and other workers by performing a variety of communication, documentation, administrative and  internal coordination functions, to support health workers in medical facilities and other health-care related organizations.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: scheduling and confirming medical appointments and communicating messages for medical staff; and patients;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: compiling, recording and reviewing medical charts, reports, documents and correspondence;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: interviewing patients to complete forms, documents and case histories;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: completing insurance and other claims forms;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: maintaining medical files and records and technical library;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: preparing financial statements and billing procedures;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: assisting in the preparation of budgets, drafting of contracts and purchasing or acquisition orders; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: supervising the work of office support workers and other office staff.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Regulatory government associate professionals administer, enforce or apply relevant government rules and regulations relating to national borders,  taxes, social benefits, and issue or examine applications for licenses or authorizations in connection with travel, exports and imports of goods, establishment of businesses, erection of buildings and other activities subject to government regulations.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include:  patrolling national borders and  checking persons and vehicles, travel and transport documents and goods transported across the border to ensure enforcement of government rules and regulations; examining tax returns to determine taxes payable by persons and businesses; examining and deciding on applications for social benefits, examining and deciding on applications for government authorizations and licenses necessary to travel, export or import goods, erect buildings, establish businesses or undertake other activities subject to government regulations; monitoring the application of price, wage or weights and measures regulations. They may receive guidance from senior government officials or Managers. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Customs and border inspectors check persons and vehicles crossing national borders to administer and enforce relevant government rules and regulations.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: patrolling national borders and coastal waters to stop persons from illegally entering or leaving the country and from illegally importing or exporting currency or goods;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: checking travel documents of persons crossing national borders to ensure that they have the necessary authorizations and certificates;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: inspecting the luggage of persons crossing national borders to ensure that it conforms to government rules and regulations concerning import or export of goods and currencies;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: examining transport documents and freight of vehicles crossing national borders to ensure conformity with government rules and regulations concerning goods in transit and the import and export of goods, and to verify that necessary payments have been made;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: detaining persons and seizing prohibited and undeclared goods found to be in violation of immigration and customs laws;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: coordinating and cooperating with other agencies involved in law enforcement, deportation and prosecution;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: performing related administrative tasks to record findings, transactions, violations and determinations; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: when necessary, testifying in a court of law about the  circumstances and results of investigations carried out.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Government tax and excise officials examine tax returns, bills of sale  and other documents to determine the type and amount of taxes, duties and  other types of fees to be paid by individuals or businesses, referring exceptional or important cases to accountants, senior government officials or Managers.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising organizations, enterprises and the public on government laws, rules and regulations concerning the determination and payment of taxes, duties and other government fees, and on the public’s rights and obligations;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: examining tax returns, bills of sale and other relevant documents to determine type and amount of taxes, duties and other types of fees to be paid;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: investigating filed tax returns and accounting records, systems and internal controls of organizations to ensure compliance with taxation laws and regulations; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing related administrative tasks to document findings, maintain records and report on actions taken for cases.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Government social benefits officials examine applications for government, financial or service programs to determine eligibility and amount of benefit or appropriate services, referring exceptional or important cases to senior government officials or managers.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising individuals and organizations on government laws, rules and regulations concerning government benefit programs and the determination and disbursement of payments or referral to services, as well as on the public’s rights and obligations;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: examining applications and other relevant documents to determine type and amount of benefit which individuals are eligible to receive;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assessing documentation and interviewing benefit recipients to ensure eligibility for continuing benefits or services; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing related administrative tasks to maintain client records and prepare reports on determinations regarding eligibility, referral decisions, termination of benefits and abuse or fraud.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Government licensing officials examine applications for licenses to export or import goods, set up businesses, build houses or other structures, or to obtain passports, determine eligibility of applications for issuing licenses or passports, and identify specific conditions or restrictions to be attached to licenses issued, referring exceptional or important cases to Senior government officials or Managers.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: advising individuals on government laws and regulations concerning the type of license required and the conditions attached to such licenses, and on the public's rights and obligations;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: examining applications and relevant documents and determining whether a license can be granted and the conditions which should be attached;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: examining applications and approving the issue of passports;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing related administrative tasks to process applications, document activities, evaluations and determinations, and to prepare correspondence to inform applicants of licensing decisions; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: administering and scoring tests required to license applicants.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Police inspectors and detectives investigate facts and circumstances relating to crimes committed in order to identify suspected offenders and obtain information not readily available or apparent concerning establishments or the circumstances and behavior of persons, mostly in order to prevent crimes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: establishing contacts and sources of information about crimes planned or committed, in order to prevent crimes or identify suspected offenders;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: obtaining and verifying evidence by examining crime and accident scenes for clues and physical evidence, interviewing witnesses and suspects and analyzing documents and computer files;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: analyzing  evidence in order to solve crimes, identify criminal activity and gather information for court cases;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: establishing contacts and sources of information not readily available or apparent concerning establishments or the circumstances and behavior of persons, usually with the aim of preventing a crime;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: making arrests; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: testifying in courts of law or reporting to superiors about circumstances and results of investigations.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: GOVERNMENT REGULATORY ASSOCIATE PROFESSIONALS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers government regulatory associate professionals not classified elsewhere in Major group 3, Technicians and associate professionals. For instance the group includes agricultural, fisheries, forestry, prices, wages and weights and measures inspectors.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: examining places of business to ensure the use of correct weights and measures in trade;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: monitoring price regulations to assess appropriateness of costs for goods and services to protect consumer interests;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: monitoring wage regulations to ensure appropriate levels of pay for work performed and to assess compliance with employment standards legislation; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing related investigative and administrative tasks to record findings, document compliance problems or inappropriate business practices and to prepare reports and correspondence.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: LEGAL, SOCIAL, CULTURAL AND RELATED PROFESSIONALS

definition_paragraphs.text: Legal, social, cultural and related associate professionals perform technical tasks connected with the practical application of knowledge relating to legal services, social work, culture, food preparation, sport and religion.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed in this sub-major group usually include: providing technical and practical services and support functions in legal processes and investigations, social and community assistance programs, and religious and cultural activities; participating and adjudicating in sporting events; developing and delivering sports coaching, fitness and recreational programmes;  combining creative and technical skills in a variety of artistic, cultural and culinary activities; creating dishes and menus and overseeing the preparation of meals.

records.title: LEGAL, SOCIAL AND RELIGIOUS ASSOCIATE PROFESSIONALS

definition_paragraphs.text: Legal, social and religious associate professionals provide technical and practical services and support functions in legal processes and investigations, social and community assistance programs and religious activities.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: assisting and supporting legal, social work and religious professionals; obtaining and analyzing evidence, preparing legal documents and serving court orders; administering and implementing social assistance programs and community services; assisting clients to deal with personal and social problems; providing practical assistance, guidance and moral support to individuals and  communities.

definition_paragraphs.text: Legal and related associate professionals perform support functions in courts of law or in law offices, provide services related to such legal matters as  insurance contracts, the transferring of property and the granting of loans and other financial  transactions or conduct investigations for clients.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: documenting court proceedings and judgements;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: serving statements of claims, summonses, warrants, subpoenas and other court orders;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: maintaining order in court and hearing rooms;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing legal documents including trial briefs, pleadings, appeals, wills and contracts and preparing, papers summarizing legal positions, or setting out conditions of loans or insurance;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: investigating facts, assembling evidence and researching relevant statutes, decisions and other legal documents to prepare cases;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: advising clients on legal matters;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: examining documentation such as mortgages, liens, judgements, easements, contracts and maps in order to verify properties’ legal descriptions and ownership;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing documents relating to transfer of real estate, stocks or other matters requiring formal registration;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: investigating possible cases of theft of goods, money or information from business establishments and of other possible cases of unlawful behavior by customers or employees; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: investigating establishments or the circumstances and behavior of persons on behalf of clients.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Social work associate professionals administer and implement social assistance programs and community services and assist clients to deal with personal and social problems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: collecting information relevant to clients’ needs and assessing their relevant skills, strengths and deficits;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: helping persons with disabilities or the elderly to obtain services and to improve their ability to function in society;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assisting clients to identify options and develop plans of action while providing necessary support and assistance;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assisting clients to identify and access community resources including legal, medical and financial assistance, housing, employment, transportation, assistance with moves, day care and other referral services;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: counselling clients living in group homes and half-way houses, supervising their activities and assisting in pre-release and release planning;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: participating in the selection and admission of clients to appropriate programs;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: providing crisis intervention and emergency shelter services;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: implementing life skills workshops, substance abuse treatment programs, behavior management programs, youth services programs and other community and social service programs under the supervision of social work or health care professionals;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: assisting in evaluating the effectiveness of interventions and programs by monitoring and reporting on clients' progress; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: maintaining contact with other social service agencies, schools and health care providers involved with clients to provide information and obtain feedback on clients' overall situation and progress.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Religious associate professionals provide support to ministers of religion or to a religious community, undertake religious works,  preach and propagate the teachings of a particular religion and endeavor to improve well-being through the power of faith and spiritual advice.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: undertaking religious works;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preaching and propagating the teachings of a particular religious faith;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assisting at services of public worship and religious rites;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing religious education, spiritual guidance and moral support to individuals and  communities;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: administering and participating in programs to provide food, clothing and shelter to those in need; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: advising communities and individuals on proper behavior and faith to preserve or improve well-being.

examples.title: Tribal Ritualists (e.g. Mambunong, Mumbaki, Mabaki, Mensapo and Anituwan in Cordilleras)

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Sports and fitness workers prepare for and compete in sporting events for financial gain, train amateur and professional sportsmen and women to enhance performance, promote participation and standards in sport, organize and officiate sporting events, and provide instruction, training and supervision for various forms of exercise and other recreational activities.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: participating in competitive sporting events; conducting sports training to develop ability in and knowledge of the sport; compiling rules concerning the conduct of sporting competitions, and controlling the progress of these events; planning, organizing and conducting practice sessions; developing and designing fitness programmes; delivering group exercise classes and personal tuition in a variety of fitness activities; promoting sports and sports skills development, and overseeing the participation of young people in sport.

definition_paragraphs.text: Athletes and sport players participate in competitive sporting events. They train and compete, either individually or as part of a team, in their chosen sport.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: participating in competitive sporting events;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: participating in regular practice and training sessions and undertaking private training to maintain the required standard of fitness and skill;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: undertaking sports promotional activities and media interviews;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: maintaining a high degree of expertise in a particular sport;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: deciding on strategies in consultation with coaches;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assessing other competitors and conditions at venues;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: competing in sporting events; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: adhering to the rules and regulations associated with a specific sport.

definition_paragraphs.text: Sports coaches, instructors and officials work with amateur and professional sportspersons to enhance performance, encourage greater participation in sport, and organize and officiate in sporting events according to established rules.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: identifying strengths and weaknesses of athletes or teams;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: planning, developing and implementing training and practice sessions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: developing, planning and coordinating competitive schedules and programs;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: motivating and preparing athletes or teams for competitive events or games;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: formulating competitive strategy, developing game plans and directing athletes and players during games or athletic events;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: analyzing and evaluating athletes' or teams' performances and modifying training programs;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring and analyzing technique and performance, and determining how future improvements can be made;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: officiating at sporting events or athletic competitions to maintain standards of play and to ensure that game rules and safety regulations are observed;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: recording lapsed time and keeping scores during events or competitions;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: judging the performance of competitors, awarding points, imposing penalties for infractions and determining results; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: compiling scores and other athletic records.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: FITNESS AND RECREATION INSTRUCTORS AND PROGRAM LEADERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Fitness and recreation instructors and program leaders lead, guide and instruct groups and individuals in recreational, fitness or outdoor adventure activities.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning and carrying out recreational and fitness activities;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: monitoring recreational, sports or fitness activities to ensure safety and provide emergency or first aid assistance when required;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: evaluating and monitoring clients’ abilities and fitness and recommending activities;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: demonstrating and teaching body movements, concepts and skills used in fitness routines and recreational activities;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: instructing in the use of equipment; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: explaining and enforcing safety procedures, rules and regulations.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Esports players and athletes participate in competitive esport tournaments, events and leagues. They train and compete, either individually or as part of a team, in their chosen esports tournaments, events and leagues.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: participating in competitive e-sports tournaments, events and leagues;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: participating in regular practice and training sessions and undertaking private training to maintain the required skill;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: undertaking promotional activities;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: maintaining a high degree of expertise in a particular e-sport;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: deciding on strategies in consultation with coaches;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assessing other competitors and conditions at venues;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: competing in esports tournaments, events and leagues; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: adhering to the rules and regulations associated with a specific esport.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: ARTISTIC, CULTURAL AND CULINARY ASSOCIATE PROFESSIONALS

definition_paragraphs.text: Artistic cultural and culinary associate professionals combine creative skills and technical and cultural knowledge in taking and processing still photographs; design and decoration of theatre sets, shop displays and the interiors of homes; preparation of objects for display; maintenance of library and gallery collections, records and cataloguing systems; creation of menus and preparation and presentation of food; provision of support for stage, film and television production; and in other areas of artistic and cultural endeavor.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: operating still cameras to photograph people, events, scenes, materials, products and other subjects; applying artistic techniques to product design, interior decoration and sales promotion; mounting and preparing objects for display; designing and arranging exhibit furnishings, display cases and display areas; designing menus and overseeing the preparation of food; assisting directors and performers with the staging of theatrical, motion picture, television or commercial productions.

definition_paragraphs.text: Photographers operate still cameras to photograph people, events, scenes, materials, products and other subjects.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: taking photographs for advertising, or other commercial, industrial or scientific purposes and to illustrate stories and articles in newspapers, magazines and other publications;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: taking portrait photographs of persons and groups of persons;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: studying requirements of a particular assignment and decide on type of camera, film, lighting and background accessories to be used;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: determining picture composition, making technical adjustments to equipment and photograph subject;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating scanners to transfer photographic images to computers;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating computers to manipulate photographic images;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: adapting existing photographic images to create new digitized images to be included in multimedia products; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: using airbrush, computer or other techniques to create the desired visual effect.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Interior designers and decorators plan and design commercial, industrial, public, retail and residential building interiors to produce an environment tailored to a purpose, taking into consideration factors that enhance living  and working environments and sales promotion. They coordinate and participate in their construction and decoration.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining the objectives and constraints of the design brief by consulting with clients and stakeholders;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: researching and analyzing spatial, functional, efficiency, safety and aesthetic requirements;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: formulating design concepts for the interiors of buildings;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing sketches, diagrams, illustrations and plans to communicate design concepts;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: negotiating design solutions with clients, management, suppliers and construction staff;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: selecting, specifying and recommending functional and aesthetic materials, furniture and products for interiors;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: detailing and documenting selected design for construction;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: coordinating the construction and the decoration of interiors;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: designing and painting stage scenery; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: designing and decorating show windows and other display areas to promote products and services.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Gallery, museum and library technicians prepare artworks, specimens and artefacts for collections, arrange and construct gallery exhibits, and assist librarians to organize and operate systems for handling recorded material and files.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: mounting and preparing objects for display;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: designing and arranging exhibit furnishings, display cases and display areas;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assisting in setting up lighting and display equipment;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: receiving, shipping, packing and unpacking exhibits;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: ordering new library materials and maintaining library records and circulation systems;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: cataloguing printed and recorded material;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: entering data into databases and editing computer records;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: operating audiovisual and reprographic equipment; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: searching and verifying bibliographic data.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Chefs design menus, create dishes and oversee the planning, organization preparation and cooking of meals in hotels, restaurants and other eating places, on board ships, on passenger trains and in private households.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning and developing recipes and menus, estimating food and labor costs, and ordering food supplies;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: monitoring quality of dishes at all stages of preparation and presentation;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: discussing food preparation issues with managers, dieticians, kitchen and waiting staff;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: supervising and coordinating the activities of cooks and other workers engaged in food preparation;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: inspecting supplies, equipment, and work areas to ensure conformance to established standards;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: determining how food should be presented, and creating decorative food displays;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: instructing cooks and other workers in the preparation, cooking, garnishing, and presentation of food;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: participating on the recruitment of kitchen staff and monitoring their performance;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: preparing, seasoning and cooking specialty foods and complex dishes; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: explaining and enforcing hygiene and food safety regulations.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: ARTISTIC AND CULTURAL ASSOCIATE PROFESSIONAL NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers artistic and cultural associate professionals not classified elsewhere in Minor Group 344, Artistic, cultural and culinary associate professionals. For instance those who assist directors or actors with staging of theatrical, motion picture, television or commercial productions are classified here.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Information and communications technicians provide support for the day-to-day running of computer systems, communications systems and networks and perform technical tasks related to telecommunications, broadcast of image and sound as well as other types of telecommunications signals on land, sea or in aircraft.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include: providing assistance to information and communications systems users ; installing new programs and equipment; establishing, operating and maintaining  network and other data communications systems; installing, monitoring and supporting Internet and Intranet websites or web server hardware or software; modifying web pages; and performing web server backup and recovery operations; controlling equipment to record sound, edit and mix image and sound recordings; controlling and maintaining transmitting and broadcast systems and satellite systems for radio and television programmes; controlling and maintaining radio communications systems, satellite services, and multiplex systems on land, sea or in aircraft; providing technical assistance connected with research and the development of computer systems and telecommunications equipment, or testing prototypes; designing and preparing blueprints of circuitry according to the specifications given; providing technical supervision of the manufacture, utilization, maintenance and repair of telecommunications systems.

records.title: INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY OPERATIONS AND USER SUPPORT TECHNICIANS

definition_paragraphs.text: Information technology operations and user support technicians provide support for the day-to-day running of communications systems, computer systems and networks and provide technical assistance to users.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: operating and controlling peripheral and related computer equipment; monitoring systems for equipment failure or errors in performance; loading peripheral equipment, such as printers, with selected materials for operating runs, or oversee loading of peripheral equipment by peripheral equipment operators; answering user inquiries regarding software or hardware operation to resolve problems; installing and performing minor repairs to hardware, software, or peripheral equipment, following design or installation specifications; overseeing the daily performance of systems; setting up equipment for employee use, performing or ensuring proper installation of cables, operating systems, or appropriate software; establishing, operating and maintaining network and other data communications systems; installing, monitoring and supporting the reliability and usability of Internet and Intranet websites or web server hardware or software; modifying web pages; and performing web server backup and recovery operations.

records.title: INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY OPERATIONS TECHNICIANS

definition_paragraphs.text: Information and communications technology operations technicians support the day-to-day processing, operation and monitoring of information and communications technology systems,  peripherals, hardware, software and related computer equipment to ensure optimal performance, and identify any problems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and controlling peripheral and related computer equipment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: entering commands, using computer terminal, and activating controls on computer and peripheral equipment to integrate and operate equipment;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: monitoring systems for equipment failure or errors in performance;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: notifying supervisor or maintenance technician of equipment malfunctions;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: responding to program error messages by finding and correcting problems, escalating the problem to other staff or terminating the program;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: reading job set-up instructions to determine equipment to be used, order of use, material such as disks and paper to be loaded, and control settings;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: retrieving, separating and sorting program output as needed, and sending data to specified users; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: loading peripheral equipment, such as printers, with selected materials for operating runs, or oversee loading of peripheral equipment by peripheral equipment operators.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY USER SUPPORT TECHNICIANS

definition_paragraphs.text: Information and communications technology user support technicians provide technical assistance to  users, either directly or by telephone, e-mail or other electronic means, including diagnosing and resolving issues and problems with software, hardware, computer peripheral equipment, networks, databases and the Internet, and providing guidance and support in the deployment, installation and maintenance of systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: answering user inquiries regarding software or hardware operation to resolve problems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: entering commands and observing system functioning to verify correct operations and detect errors;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: installing and performing minor repairs to hardware, software, or peripheral equipment, following design or installation specifications;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: overseeing the daily performance of communications and computer systems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: setting up equipment for employee use, performing or ensuring proper installation of cables, operating systems, or appropriate software;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: maintaining records of daily data communication transactions, problems and remedial actions taken, or installation activities;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: emulating or reproducing technical problems encountered by users; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: consulting user guides, technical manuals and other documents to research and implement solutions.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Computer network and systems technicians establish, operate and maintain network and other data communications systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating, maintaining and troubleshooting network systems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and maintaining data communications systems other than networks;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assisting users with network and data communications problems;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: identifying areas needing upgraded equipment and software;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: installing computer hardware, network software, operating system software and applications software; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: performing start up and close down as well as backup and disaster recovery operations for computer networks.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Web technicians maintain, monitor and support the optimal functioning of Internet and Intranet websites and web server hardware and software.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: installing, monitoring and supporting the reliability and usability of Internet and Intranet websites or web server hardware or software;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: developing and maintaining documentation, policies and instructions, recording operational procedures and system logs;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: developing, coordinating, implementing and monitoring security measures;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: analyzing and making recommendations to enhance performance, including upgrading and acquiring new systems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: liaising with, and providing guidance to, clients and users;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: modifying web pages; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: performing web server backup and recovery operations.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Telecommunications and broadcasting technicians control technical functioning of equipment to record and edit images and sound and for transmitting radio and television broadcasts of images and sounds, as well as other types of telecommunication signals on land, sea or in aircraft, perform technical tasks connected with telecommunications engineering research and with the design, manufacture, assembly, construction, operation, maintenance and repair of telecommunications systems.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: controlling equipment to record sound, edit and mix image and sound recordings; controlling and maintaining transmitting and broadcast systems and satellite systems for radio and television programmes; controlling and maintaining radio communications systems, satellite services, and multiplex systems on land, sea or in aircraft; providing technical assistance connected with research and the development of telecommunications equipment, or testing prototypes; designing and preparing blueprints of circuitry according to the specifications given; providing technical supervision of the manufacture, utilization, maintenance and repair of telecommunications systems.

definition_paragraphs.text: Broadcasting and audio-visual technicians control technical functioning of equipment to record and edit images and sound and for transmitting radio and television broadcasts of images and sounds, as well as other types of telecommunication signals on land, sea or in aircraft.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: controlling equipment to record sound;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: controlling equipment to edit and mix image and sound recordings to ensure satisfactory quality and to create special image and sound effects;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: applying knowledge of principles and practices of image and sound recording and editing in order to identify and solve problems;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: controlling transmitting and broadcast systems and satellite systems for radio and television programmes;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: controlling radio communications systems, satellite services, and multiplex systems on land, sea or in aircraft;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: applying knowledge of principles and practices of broadcasting, telecommunications terminals and transmissions systems, in order to identify and solve problems; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: making emergency repairs to equipment.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Telecommunications engineering technicians perform technical tasks connected with telecommunications engineering research, as well as with the design, manufacture, assembly, construction, operation, maintenance and repair of telecommunications systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: providing technical assistance connected with research and the development of telecommunications equipment, or testing prototypes;

tasks.label: b
