tasks.text: studying technical material such as blue prints and sketches to determine the method of work to be adopted;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing detailed estimates of quantities and costs of materials and labor required for the manufacture and  installation of telecommunications equipment, according to the specifications given;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing technical supervision of the manufacture, utilization, maintenance and repair of telecommunications systems to ensure satisfactory performance and compliance with specifications and regulations; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: applying technical knowledge of telecommunications engineering principles and practices in order to identify and solve problems arising in the course of their work.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Clerical support workers record, organize, store, compute and retrieve information-related; and perform a number of clerical  duties in connection with money-handling operations, travel arrangements, requests for information, and appointments. Most occupations in this Major Group require skills at the second ISCO skill level.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by clerical support workers usually include: stenography, typing, and operating word processors and other office machines; entering data into computers; carrying out secretarial duties; recording and computing numerical data; keeping records relating to stocks, production and transport; keeping  records relating to passenger and freight transport; carrying out clerical duties in libraries; filing documents; carrying out duties in connection with mail services; preparing and checking material for printing; writing on behalf of illiterate persons; performing money-handling operations; dealing with travel arrangements; supplying information requested by clients and making appointments; and operating a telephone switchboard. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: General and keyboard clerks record, organize, store and retrieve information; and perform a range of clerical and administrative tasks according to established procedures.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this Sub-Major Group usually include: operating personal computers, word-processors or typewriters; recording, inputting and processing data using computers; recording input and processing text; calculating; bookkeeping and similar office machines to input and process text and data; and performing a wide range of general clerical duties including preparing invoices, checking figures, filing, faxing or processing mail.

definition_paragraphs.text: General office clerks perform a range of clerical and administrative tasks according to established procedures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: recording, preparing, sorting, classifying and filing information;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: sorting, opening and sending mail;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: photocopying and sending  documents;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing reports and correspondence of a routine nature;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: recording issue of equipment to staff;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: responding to telephone or electronic enquiries or forwarding to appropriate person;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: checking figures, preparing invoices and recording details of financial transactions made; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: transcribing information into computers, and proof-reading and correcting copy.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Secretaries (general) use typewriters, personal computers or other word-processing equipment to transcribe correspondence and other documents; check and format documents prepared by other staff; deal with incoming and outgoing mail; screen requests for meetings or appointments; and perform a variety of administrative support tasks.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: checking, formatting and transcribing correspondence, minutes and reports from dictation, electronic documents or written drafts to conform to office standards, using typewriter, personal computer or other word processing equipment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: using various computer software packages, including spreadsheets, to provide administrative support;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: dealing with incoming or outgoing mail;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: scanning, recording and distributing mail, correspondence and documents;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: screening requests for meetings or appointments and helping to organize meetings;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: screening and recording leave and other staff-members' entitlements;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: organizing and supervising filing systems; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: dealing with routine correspondence on their own initiative.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Keyboard operators input and process text and data; and prepare, edit and generate documents for storage, processing, publication and transmission.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: entering data and codes required to process information; retrieving, confirming and updating data in storage and keeping records of data input; taking records of proceedings in rapid shorthand using computerized equipment and shorthand-writing machines; transcribing information recorded in shorthand and on sound recording equipment, and proofreading and correcting copy; and reproducing the spoken word, environmental sounds and song lyrics as captions for cinema and television programming.

definition_paragraphs.text: Typists and word processing operators type, edit and print using typewriter, personal computer or word processor; and record oral or written matter in shorthand.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: typing written material from rough drafts, corrected copies, voice recordings, or shorthand using a computer, word processor or typewriter;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: checking completed work for proper spelling, grammar, punctuation and formatting;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: gathering and arranging the material to be typed, following instructions;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: filing and storing completed documents on computer hard drive or disk, or maintaining a computer filing system to store, retrieve or update documents;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: taking dictation and recording other matter in shorthand;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: reproducing the spoken word, environmental sounds and song lyrics as captions for cinema and television programming; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: transcribing information recorded in shorthand and on sound recording equipment.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Data entry clerks enter coded, statistical, financial and other numerical data into electronic equipment, computerized databases, spreadsheets or other data repositories using a keyboard, mouse, or optical scanner, speech recognition software or other data entry tools. They enter data into mechanical and electronic devices to perform mathematical calculations.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: receiving and registering invoices, forms, records and other documents for data capture;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: entering numerical data, codes and text from source material into computer-compatible storage and processing devices;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: verifying accuracy and completeness of data and correcting entered data, if needed;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating bookkeeping and calculating machines; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: importing and exporting data between different database systems and software.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Customer service clerks deal with clients in connection with money-handling operations, travel arrangements, requests for information, making appointments, operating telephone switchboards; and interviewing for surveys or to complete applications for eligibility for services.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this Sub-Major Group include: performing money-handling operations in banks, post offices, betting and gambling establishments; or dealing with travel arrangements; supplying information requested by clients and making appointments; operating telephone switchboards; greeting and receiving visitors; interviewing survey respondents; and interviewing applicants for services.

records.title: TELLERS, MONEY COLLECTORS AND RELATED CLERKS

definition_paragraphs.text: Tellers, money collectors and related clerks perform money-handling operations in establishments relating to banking, postal services, betting or gambling, pawning and debt-collecting.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: dealing with clients of banks or post offices in connection with money operations or postal services; receiving and paying off bets on results of sporting events; conducting gambling games; lending money against articles deposited or other securities; and collecting debts and other payments.

definition_paragraphs.text: Bank tellers and related clerks deal directly with clients of banks or post offices in connection with receiving, changing and paying out money; or providing mail services.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: processing customer cash deposits and withdrawals, cheques, transfers, bills, credit card payments, money orders, certified cheques and other related banking transactions;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: crediting and debiting clients' accounts;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: paying bills and making money transfers on clients' behalf;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: receiving mail, selling postage stamps and conducting other post office counter business such as bill payments, money transfers and related business;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: changing money from one currency to another, as requested by clients; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: making records of all transactions and reconciling them with cash balance.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: BOOKMAKERS, CROUPIERS/DEALERS AND RELATED GAMING WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Bookmakers, croupiers/dealers and related gaming workers determine odds and receive and pay off bets on results of sporting or other events; or conduct games of chance in gambling establishments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining risks to decide odds and to hedge or refuse bets;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing and issuing lists of approximate odds;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: distributing cards, rolling dice or spinning a roulette wheel;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: explaining and interpreting operating rules of a gambling establishment; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: announcing winning numbers, paying winners and collecting payments from losers.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Pawnbrokers and money lenders lend money against articles deposited as pledges, or against property or other security.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: evaluating articles offered as pledges, calculating interest, and lending money;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: returning articles when the loan is paid or, in the event of non-payment, selling pledged articles;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: lending money as personal loans against success of future harvest and other similar undertakings;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: collecting loans when the pledge involved the success of future harvest and other similar undertakings; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: keeping a record of items received and money distributed and received.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Debt collectors and related workers collect payments on overdue accounts and bad cheques and collect charity payments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: tracing and locating debtors;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: telephoning, visiting, or writing to customers to collect money or arrange for later payments;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing reports including amounts collected and maintain records and files related to collection work;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: recommending legal action or discontinuation of service when payment cannot be otherwise obtained; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: asking for and collecting charity payments.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Client information workers provide or obtain information in person, by telephone or electronic means such as e-mail in connection with making travel arrangements; describing the products or services of an organization; registering and greeting guests and visitors; making appointments; connecting telephone calls; and collecting information from survey respondents or applicants for services.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: preparing itineraries and making travel and hotel reservations for clients; greeting and receiving clients and visitors; registering accommodation guests; providing information concerning the goods, services or policies of an organization; making appointments; operating a telephone switchboard; and interviewing survey respondents and applicants for eligibility.

definition_paragraphs.text: Travel consultants and clerks provide information about travel destinations, arrange travel itineraries, obtain travel and accommodation reservations and register passengers at check-in and departure.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: obtaining information about the availability, cost and convenience of different types of transport and accommodation, ascertaining customer’s requirements and advising them on travel arrangements;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: providing information about local and regional attractions, sightseeing tours, restaurants, arts and entertainment, and providing maps and brochures;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing itineraries;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: making and confirming reservations for travel, tours and accommodation;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: issuing tickets, boarding passes and vouchers;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: verifying travel documentation and registering passengers and luggage at check-in and departure;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: helping customers in obtaining necessary travel documents such as visas;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing bills and receiving payments; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: organizing group tours for business or vacation travel and selling them to groups or individuals.

related_occupations.title: Entertainment and sporting events ticket issuing clerk
related_occupations.raw: Entertainment and sporting events ticket issuing clerk - 5230

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Contact center information clerks provide advice and information to clients; respond to queries regarding a company’s or an organization’s goods, services or policies; and process financial transactions using the telephone or electronic communications media, such as email. They are located in premises that may be remote from clients or other operations of the organizations or companies about whom information is provided.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: dealing with incoming calls and messages from clients, whether to answer queries, handle calls for service or sort out complaints;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: identifying requirements and entering events into a computer system;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: dispatching tasks to other units, when relevant;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: invoicing or handling payments, where necessary;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: sending letters, information sheets and other documents to clients; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: advising clients of additional products or services.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Telephone switchboard operators operate telephone communications switchboards and consoles to establish telephone connections; receive caller inquiries and service problem reports; and record and relay messages to staff or clients.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating switchboards and consoles to connect, hold, transfer, and disconnect telephone calls;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making connections for outgoing calls;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: dealing with telephone inquiries and recording messages;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: forwarding messages to staff or clients; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: investigating operating system problems and informing repair services.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Hotel receptionists register guests; assign rooms; issue keys; provide information concerning the hotel services; make room reservations; keep a record of rooms available for occupancy; and present statements of charges to departing guests and receive payment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: maintaining an inventory of rooms available for occupancy, reservations and room assignments;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: registering arriving guests, assigning rooms; verifying customer’s credit and issuing room keys;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: providing information regarding hotel services and services available in the community;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing information about availability of accommodation and making room reservations;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: responding to guests’ requests for housekeeping and maintenance services as well as complaints;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: contacting housekeeping or maintenance services when guests report problems;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: compiling and checking guest accounts for charges using computerized or manual systems;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: receiving and forwarding messages in person or using telephone or telephone switchboard; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: reviewing statements of charges to departing guests and receiving payment.

definition_paragraphs.text: Inquiry clerks respond to personal, written, electronic mail, and telephone inquiries and complaints about the organization’s goods, services and policies, provide information and refer people to other sources. They are employed in locations which put them in direct contact with clients or with the production of the goods and services provided.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: answering inquiries about goods, services and policies, and providing information about their availability, location, price and related issues;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: responding to enquiries about problems and providing advice, information and assistance;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: recording information about inquiries and complaints;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: referring complex enquiries to team leaders or expert advisers; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: issuing relevant forms, information kits and brochures to interested parties.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Receptionists (general) receive and welcome visitors, clients, or guests; and respond to inquiries and requests, including arranging for appointments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: receiving and welcoming visitors, guests or clients;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making appointments for clients;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: dealing with telephone requests for information or appointments;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: directing clients to appropriate location or person; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: supplying information pamphlets, brochures or forms.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Survey and market research interviewers interview people and record their responses to survey and market research questions on a range of topics.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: contacting individuals by telephone or in person and explaining the purpose of the interview;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: asking questions following the outlines of questionnaires and surveys;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: recording responses on paper or entering responses directly into a computer database through computer-assisted interviewing systems;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: identifying and resolving inconsistencies in responses; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: providing feedback to survey sponsors concerning problems in obtaining valid data.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: CLIENT INFORMATION WORKERS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This Unit Group includes client information workers not elsewhere classified in Minor Group 422. Client information workers. For instance, it includes workers who obtain and process information from clients needed to determine eligibility for services.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: interviewing patients to obtain and process information required to provide hospital services;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: interviewing applicants for public assistance to gather information pertinent to their application;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: verifying the accuracy of information provided;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: initiating procedures to grant, modify, deny or terminate assistance;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: providing information and answering questions concerning benefits and claims procedures; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: referring patient or applicant to other organizations if they are ineligible for services.

section_markers.text: In such cases, tasks would include:
Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Numerical and material recording clerks obtain, compile and compute accounting, bookkeeping, statistical, financial and other numerical data; and take charge of cash transactions incidental to business matters. Some occupations classified here keep records of goods produced, purchased, stocked, dispatched and of materials needed at specified production dates; or keep records of operational aspects; and coordinate the timing of passenger and freight transport.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this Sub-Major Group usually include: helping with accounting and bookkeeping records and computations; calculating unit production costs; calculating wages and in some cases preparing wage packets and paying wages; taking charge of cash transactions incidental to the business; obtaining, compiling and computing statistical or actuarial data; performing clerical tasks relating to the financial transactions of an insurance establishment, bank or similar establishment; recording produced, stocked, ordered and  dispatched goods; recording production materials received, put into stock or issued; computing quantities of the production materials required at specified dates; and helping with preparation and checking of production operation schedules; keeping records of operational aspects; and coordinating the timing of passenger and freight transport.

definition_paragraphs.text: Numerical clerks obtain, compile and compute accounting, bookkeeping, statistical, financial and other numerical data; and take charge of cash transactions incidental to business matters.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: helping with accounting and bookkeeping records and computations; calculating unit production costs; calculating wages and in some cases, preparing wage pockets and paying wages; taking charge of cash transactions incidental to the business; obtaining, compiling and computing statistical or actuarial data; and performing clerical tasks relating to the financial transactions of an insurance establishment, bank or similar establishment.

definition_paragraphs.text: Accounting and bookkeeping clerks compute, classify and record numerical data to keep financial records complete. They perform any combination of routine calculating, posting and verifying duties to obtain primary financial data for use in maintaining accounting records.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: checking figures, postings and documents for correct entry, mathematical accuracy and proper codes;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating computers programmed with accounting software to record, store and analyze information;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: classifying, recording and summarizing numerical and financial data to compile and keep financial records using journals and ledgers or computers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: calculating, preparing and issuing bills, invoices, account statements and other financial statements according to established procedures; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: compiling statistical, financial, accounting or auditing reports and tables pertaining to such matters as cash receipts, expenditures, accounts payable and receivable, and profits and losses.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Statistical, finance and insurance clerks obtain, compile and compute statistical or actuarial data or perform clerical tasks relating to the transactions of insurance establishments, banks and other financial establishments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: processing insurance enrolments, cancellations, claims transactions, policy changes and payments;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: obtaining and compiling statistical or actuarial data based on routine or special sources of information;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: calculating totals, averages, percentages and other details and presenting them in the required tabular form;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing financial documents, and calculating interest or brokerage charges and stamp duties payable; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: maintaining records of bonds, shares and other securities bought or sold on behalf of clients or employer.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Payroll clerks collect, verify and process payroll information and compute pay and benefit entitlements for employees within a department, company or other establishment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: maintaining records of employee attendance, leave and overtime to calculate pay and benefit entitlements, using manual or computerized systems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing and verifying statements of earnings for employees, indicating gross and net salaries and deductions such as taxes, union dues, garnishments and insurance and pension plans;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing employee payments and benefit payments by cheque or electronic transfer;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: reviewing time sheets, work charts, wage computation and other information to detect and reconcile payroll discrepancies; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: verifying attendance, hours worked and pay adjustments, and posting information onto designated records.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Material recording and transport clerks keep records of goods produced, purchased, stocked, dispatched and of materials needed at specified production dates, or keep records of operational aspects and coordinate the timing of passenger and freight transport.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: recording produced, stocked, ordered and dispatched goods; recording production materials received, put into stock or issued; computing quantities of the production materials required at specified dates; and helping with preparation and checking of production operation schedules; keeping records of operational aspects; and coordinating the timing of passenger and freight transport.

definition_paragraphs.text: Stock clerks maintain records of goods produced and production materials received, weighed, issued, dispatched or put into stock.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: arranging and controlling receipt and dispatch of goods and keeping relevant records;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: maintaining stock records, verifying issue of goods, estimating needs and making requisitions of new stocks;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: receiving, storing and issuing tools, spare parts, or various equipment and maintaining relevant records;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: weighing goods received, issued, produced, or dispatched and maintaining relevant records; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: compiling inventories of furniture and other items received for storage.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Production clerks compute quantities of materials required at specified dates for manufacturing, construction and similar production programmes; and prepare and check production operation schedules.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: computing quantities, qualities and types of materials required by production programme;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing production requirements schedules, ensuring that materials are available when needed, and keeping relevant records;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing or assisting in the preparation of production operation schedules on the basis of customers' orders and production capacity and performance;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: verifying stocks, arranging deliveries and investigating delays; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: recording and coordinating the flow of work and materials between departments.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Transport clerks keep records of operational aspects and coordinate the timing of train, road and air passenger and freight transport; and prepare reports for management.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: keeping records of operational aspects and coordinating the timing of passenger and freight transport;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: directing train routings within a division or zone of a railway system and keeping related records;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: directing, controlling and keeping records of freight handling at a railway yard;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: coordinating and keeping records of operational activities concerning road transport, such as allocation and scheduling of vehicles and drivers, loading and unloading of vehicles and storage of goods in transit;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: coordinating and keeping records of operational activities concerning air transport of passengers and freight, such as passenger lists and freight manifests; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: preparing reports for management.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Other clerical support workers perform clerical duties in newspapers, courts, libraries and post offices; file documents; prepare information for processing; maintain personnel records; check material for consistency with original source material; and write on behalf of illiterate persons.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this Sub-Major Group usually include: recording information regarding acquisition, issue and return of library books; maintaining personnel records; classifying and filing various documents and other records; sorting, recording and delivering mail from post offices, as well as from or within an enterprise; coding; correcting proofs; performing a number of miscellaneous clerical duties; and writing on behalf of persons who are unable to read and write.

definition_paragraphs.text: Other clerical support workers perform clerical duties in newspapers, courts, libraries and post offices; file documents; prepare information for processing; maintain personnel records; check material for consistency with original source material; and write on behalf of illiterate persons.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this Minor Group usually include: recording information regarding acquisition, issue and return of library books; maintaining personnel records; classifying and filing various documents and other records; sorting, recording and delivering mail from post offices, as well as from or within an enterprise; coding; correcting proofs; performing a number of miscellaneous clerical duties; and writing on behalf of persons who are unable to read and write.

definition_paragraphs.text: Library clerks issue and receive library materials; sort and shelve books, sound and vision recordings, periodicals, journals, magazines and newspapers; and provide general library information to library users.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: issuing and receiving library books and other materials;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: reshelving books and other library materials;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: performing clerical activities such as manual and electronic filing, word processing and occasional typing;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: maintaining journal subscriptions;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: assisting library users in accessing basic library materials and making inter-library loans; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: maintaining library records relating to the acquisition, issue and return of books and other materials.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Mail carriers and sorting clerks perform sorting, recording, delivery and other duties in connection with mail services from post offices or related organizations, as well as from or within an establishment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: performing mail-handling duties in public post offices or privately-owned delivery establishments;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: sorting and delivering mail to private houses and businesses;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: providing delivery confirmation records when requested by the client; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: sorting and keeping simple records of incoming and outgoing correspondence and dispatching outgoing mail in various establishments.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Coding, proof-reading and related clerks convert information into codes; verify and correct proofs; and perform a number of miscellaneous clerical duties.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: converting information into codes and classifying information by codes for data-processing purposes;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: comparing proofs of texts and related material prepared for printing with original material; correcting errors; and marking texts for printer according to the established rules;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: sorting forms and marking them with identification numbers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: sorting documents for filing or to collate sets of pages; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: addressing circulars and envelopes by hand.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Scribes and related workers write letters and complete forms on behalf of  persons who are unable to read and write, e.g.,  illiterate persons, not  physically  present, etc.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: reading letters and other written matter to persons who are unable to read or write and providing necessary interpretation and information;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: writing letters and completing forms on behalf of others; and

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: offering advice to individuals and interpreting and helping with the completion of government and other official forms.

definition_paragraphs.text: Filing and copying clerks file correspondence, cards, invoices, receipts and other records in alphabetical or numerical order or according to the filing system used. They locate and remove material from file when requested; and photocopy, scan or fax documents.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: sorting or classifying materials according to guidelines such as content, purpose, user criteria, or chronological, alphabetical, or numerical order;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: filing material in drawers, cabinets and storage boxes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: locating and removing materials from files when requested;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: keeping records of materials filed and removed; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: photocopying, scanning or faxing documents.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Personnel clerks maintain and update personnel records such as information on transfers and promotions, performance evaluations, employee leave taken and accumulated, salaries, qualifications and training.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: updating information on employment history, salaries, performance evaluations, qualifications and training, and leave taken and accumulated;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: initiating records for newly-appointed workers and checking records for completeness;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: processing applications for employment and promotions and advising applicants of results;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: receiving and answering inquiries about employment entitlements and conditions;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: sending out job applications and announcements of job openings and job examinations;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: maintaining and updating manual and computerized filing and registration systems; and compiling and preparing reports and documents relating to personnel activities; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: storing and retrieving personnel records and files on request.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: CLERICAL SUPPORT WORKERS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This Unit Group covers clerical support workers not classified elsewhere in Major Group 4. Clerical support workers. For instance, the group includes correspondence clerks, press clippers and publication clerks.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: receiving customers' orders for classified advertising; writing and editing copy; calculating advertising rates; and billing customers;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: writing business and government correspondence such as replies to requests for information and assistance, damage claims, credit and billing enquiries and service complaints;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assisting in the preparation of periodicals, advertisements, catalogues, directories and other material for publication; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: reading newspapers, magazines, press releases and other publications to locate and file articles of interest to staff and clients.

section_markers.text: In such cases, tasks would include:
Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Service and sales workers provide personal and  protective services related to travel, housekeeping, catering, personal care,  or protection against fire and unlawful acts, or demonstrate and sell goods in wholesale or retail shops and similar establishments, as well as at stalls and on markets.  Most occupations in this Major Group require skills at the second PSOC skill level.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by service and sales workers usually include: organizing and providing services during travel; housekeeping; preparing and serving of food and beverages; caring for children;  providing personal and basic health care at homes or in institutions, as well as hairdressing, beauty treatment and companionship; telling fortunes; embalming and arranging funerals; providing security services and protecting individuals and property against fire and unlawful acts; enforcing of law and order;  posing as models for advertising, artistic creation and display of goods;  selling goods in wholesale or retail establishments, as well as at stalls and on markets; and demonstrating goods to potential customers.  Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Personal service workers provide personal services related to travel, housekeeping, catering, child and personal care.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this Sub-Major Group usually include: organizing and providing of services during travel; housekeeping; preparing and serving food and beverages; providing personal and basic health care at homes or institutions, as well as hairdressing, beauty treatment and companionship; telling fortunes; and embalming and arranging funerals.  Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Travel attendants, conductors and guides provide various personal services in connection with travelling by aircraft, train, ship, bus or other vehicle; and escorting individuals and groups on travel tours, sightseeing visits and excursions.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: ensuring the comfort and safety of passengers; serving food and refreshments; providing information and answering questions in connection with travel; collecting or issuing tickets on board public transport; and accompanying individuals or groups on sightseeing tours or excursions and describing points of interest.

definition_paragraphs.text: Travel attendants and travel stewards ensure the comfort and safety of passengers; serve meals and beverages; and render personal services, usually on aircraft and on board ships.  They may plan and coordinate housekeeping and social activities on ships.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: greeting passengers entering aircraft or ship; checking tickets or boarding passes; and directing them to their seats or berths;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: announcing, explaining and demonstrating safety and emergency procedures, such as the use of oxygen masks, seat belts, and life jackets;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assembling and serving pre-prepared meals and beverages;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: selling duty-free and other goods;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: taking care of general needs and comfort of passengers, answering inquiries, and keeping cabins clean and tidy;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: directing and assisting passengers and following prescribed procedures in the event of an emergency, such as evacuating a plane following an emergency landing;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: verifying that first aid kits and other emergency equipment are in working order;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: administering first aid to passengers in distress;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: attending pre-flight briefings concerning weather, altitudes, routes, emergency procedures, crew coordination, lengths of flights, food and beverage services offered, and numbers of passengers;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: preparing passengers and aircraft for take-off and landing; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: determining special assistance needs of passengers such as small children, the elderly, or disabled persons.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Transport conductors check and issue tickets; and ensure the safety and comfort of passengers on trains, trams, buses and other public transport vehicles.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: collecting and issuing tickets, passes or fares, and checking the validity of tickets issued previously;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: attending to sleeping-cars and their occupants on passenger trains;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: providing assistance with boarding, seating and luggage as required, especially to elderly, sick, or injured people;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: opening and closing doors for passengers;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: performing equipment safety checks prior to departure;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: signaling to drivers to stop or proceed;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: greeting passengers, boarding transportation equipment, and announcing routes and stops;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: ensuring that safety regulations are respected;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: responding to passengers requests and complaints and providing information about stops and connections; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: taking appropriate action in case of emergencies or accidents.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Travel guides accompany individuals or groups on trips, sightseeing tours and excursions and on tours of places of interest such as historical sites, industrial establishments and theme parks.  They describe points of interest and provide background information on interesting features.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: escorting and guiding tourists on cruises and sightseeing tours;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: escorting visitors through places of interest such as museums, exhibitions, theme parks, factories and other industrial establishments;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: describing and providing information on points of interest and exhibits, and responding to questions;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: conducting educational activities for school children;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: monitoring visitors' activities to ensure compliance with establishment or tour regulations and safety practices;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: greeting and registering visitors and tour participants, and issuing any required identification badges or safety devices;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: distributing brochures, showing audio-visual presentations, and explaining procedures and operations at tour sites;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: providing for physical safety of groups, and performing activities such as providing first aid and directing emergency evacuations; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: resolving any problems with tour itineraries, service, or accommodation.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Cooks plan, organize, prepare and cook meals in hotels, restaurants and other eating places, on board ships, on passenger trains and in private households.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning meals, preparing and cooking foodstuffs;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: planning, supervising and coordinating the work of kitchen helpers;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: checking the quality of food;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: weighing, measuring and mixing ingredients according to recipes and personal judgement;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: regulating the temperature of ovens, grills, roasters and other cooking equipment; inspecting and cleaning the kitchen, kitchen equipment, serving areas, etc. to ensure safe and sanitary food handling practices; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating large-volume cooking equipment such as grills, deep-fat fryers, or griddles.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Waiters and bartenders serve food and beverages in commercial dining and drinking places, clubs, institutions and canteens, on board ships and on passenger trains.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: assisting in keeping bar properly stocked; washing used glassware and cleaning bar area; serving alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks at a bar; setting tables with clean linen, cutlery, crockery and glassware; serving food and beverages; advising on the choice of wines and serving them; taking orders for food and/or drinks and passing order to kitchen; presenting bill; and accepting payment.

definition_paragraphs.text: Waiters serve food and beverages at tables in dining and drinking places, clubs, institutions and canteens, on board ships and on passenger trains.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting tables with clean linen, cutlery, crockery and glassware;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: greeting customers and presenting them with menus and beverage lists;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: advising on food and beverage choices;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: taking orders for food and drinks and passing order to kitchen or bar staff;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: serving food and beverages to clients at tables;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: clearing tables and returning dishes and cutlery to kitchen; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: presenting bills, accepting payment and operating point of sales machines and cash registers.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Bartenders prepare, mix and serve alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks directly to customers over a bar or counter, or through waiters.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: taking beverage orders from serving staff or directly from patrons;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing and serving alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks at a bar;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: washing used glassware, cleaning and maintaining bar service areas, tea and coffee-making areas and equipment such as espresso machines;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: collecting payment for sales, operating cash registers and balancing cash receipts;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: tapping kegs and attaching supply lines;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assisting in keeping bar properly stocked and arranging bottles and glasses;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: checking identification of customers to verify age requirements for purchase of alcohol;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: taking steps to limit problems related to excessive drinking such, as persuading customers to stop drinking, declining further service and ordering transportation;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: mixing ingredients to prepare cocktails and other drinks; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: serving snacks or other food items to customers at the bar.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Hairdressers, beauticians and related workers cut and dress hair; shave and trim beards; give beauty treatment; apply cosmetics and make-up; and give other kinds of treatment to individuals in order to improve their appearance.

Their tasks include: discussing customers’ requirements; cutting and dressing hair; shaving and trimming beards; giving beauty treatment, and applying cosmetics and make up; shaping and polishing finger and toe nails and treating minor ailments of the human foot; and attending clients taking bath and administering elementary massage.
Hairdressers cut, style, color, straighten and permanently wave hair; shave or trim facial hair; and treat scalp conditions.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: cutting, washing, tinting and waving hair;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: shaving or trimming beards and moustaches;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: giving scalp treatment;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: fitting wigs according to customers’ requirements;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: providing advice on hair care, beauty products and hairstyles;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: styling hair into dreadlocks and braids and adding hair extensions;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: arranging appointments and collecting payments; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: cleaning work areas and sanitizing instruments.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Beauticians and related workers give facial and body beauty treatments; apply cosmetics and make-up; and give other kinds of treatment to individuals in order to improve their appearance.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: cleaning and applying creams, lotions and related products to face and parts of body;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: giving facial and body massage;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: applying make-up to clients of a beauty parlor or to actors and other performers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: cleaning, shaping and polishing finger- and toe-nails; and treating minor ailments of the human foot such as corns, calluses or deformed toe-nails;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: attending to clients taking bath and administering elementary massage;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: using waxing, sugaring and depilation techniques to remove unwanted bodily hair;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: advising clients on diet and exercise to assist in weight loss and slimming; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: arranging appointments and collecting payments.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Building and housekeeping supervisors coordinate, schedule, and supervise the work of cleaners and other housekeeping staff in commercial, industrial and residential premises.  They take responsibility for housekeeping and caretaking functions in hotels, offices, apartments, houses and private dwellings.

Tasks usually include: assigning tasks and inspecting building areas to see that cleaning, housekeeping and maintenance work has been done properly; issuing of supplies and equipment and inventory stocks to ensure that the supplies on hand are adequate; screening and hiring job applicants; training both new and experienced employees; recommending promotions, transfers or dismissals; and performing some cleaning, housekeeping and maintenance tasks.

records.title: CLEANING AND HOUSEKEEPING SUPERVISORS IN OFFICES, HOTELS AND OTHER ESTABLISHMENTS

definition_paragraphs.text: Cleaning and housekeeping supervisors in offices, hotels and other establishments organize, supervise and carry out housekeeping functions in order to keep clean and tidy the interiors, fixtures and facilities in these establishments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: engaging, training, discharging, organizing and supervising helpers, cleaners and other housekeeping staff;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: purchasing or controlling the purchase of supplies;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: controlling storage and issue of supplies;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: supervising general welfare and conduct of individuals in institutions;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: sweeping or vacuum-cleaning, washing and polishing floors, furniture and other fixtures;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: making beds, cleaning bathrooms, supplying towels, soap and related items;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: cleaning kitchens and generally helping with kitchen work, including dishwashing; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: restocking mini-bars and replenishing items such as drinking glasses and writing equipment.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Household service providers organize, supervise and carry out housekeeping functions in private households with or without the support of subordinate staff.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: supervising workers employed in households as domestic staff;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: purchasing or controlling the purchase of supplies;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: controlling storage and issue of supplies;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assisting in cases of minor injury or illness by performing tasks such as taking temperature, giving medicine, putting on bandages;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: sweeping or vacuum-cleaning, washing and polishing floors, furniture and other fixtures;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: making beds, cleaning bathrooms, supplying towels, soap and related items;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: taking care of household pets and plants, receiving visitors, answering telephones, delivering messages and shopping for groceries;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing and cooking meals, setting and clearing tables and serving food and beverages; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: cleaning kitchens and generally helping with kitchen work, including dishwashing.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Building caretakers take care of apartment houses, hotels, offices, churches and other buildings and maintain them and associated grounds in a clean and orderly condition.  They may supervise other workers and contractors depending on the size and nature of the building concerned.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: supervising the work of cleaning, housekeeping and building maintenance staff and contractors;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: participating in cleaning, simple repairs and maintenance of building interiors;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: tending furnaces and boilers to ensure provision of heat and hot water;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: regulating conduct of tenants and visitors in such matters as noise abatement or misuse of property;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: providing small services to absent tenants such as accepting deliveries on their behalf or providing requested information to callers;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: notifying management and owners of buildings of the need for major repairs;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: patrolling buildings to ensure security is maintained; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: filling out registration forms and providing tenants with copies of rules.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Other personal services workers recount past and predict future events in persons’ lives; provide companionship and other personal services; groom, train and care for animals; provide embalming and funeral services; and train people to drive vehicles.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: casting horoscopes; providing companionship or valet services and other personal services to clients; providing embalming and funeral services; feeding, handling, training and grooming animals; and instructing students under actual driving conditions.

definition_paragraphs.text: Astrologers, fortune-tellers and related workers recount past and predict future events in persons’ lives by practicing astrology, on the basis of characteristics of the clients’ palms, samples of playing cards drawn or other techniques.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: casting horoscopes of individuals at birth or later to recount past and forecast future events and conditions of their lives;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: interpreting characteristics of clients’ palms, samples of playing cards, position of tea leaves or coffee remnants in a cup, shapes and patterns of bones of dead animals, etc.;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: forecasting future events on the basis of these interpretations;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: determining auspicious times for various human activities such as inaugurations, marriages, journeys and religious and other ceremonies;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: giving warnings and advice on possible courses of action; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: advising individuals on precautions to be taken to avoid evil influences.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Companions and valets provide companionship and attend to various needs of the employer.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: providing companionship to employer by accompanying him/her to various places, reading, conversing and participating in activities such as sports;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: assisting in entertaining visitors in employer's home; and

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: keeping wardrobe and personal effects of the employer in good order.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Undertakers and embalmers perform various tasks in the disposal of dead human bodies.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: making arrangements for, and conducting, funerals, cremations and burials;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: embalming human bodies to retard or arrest the process of decay;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: conforming to health and sanitation and ensuring that legal requirements concerning embalming are met;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: incising and closing incisions on various parts of the body and reshaping or reconstructing disfigured or maimed bodies when necessary;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: dressing bodies and placing them in caskets; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: conducting interviews to arrange for preparation of obituary notices, to assist with the selection of caskets or urns, and to determine the location and time of burials or cremations.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: PET GROOMERS AND ANIMAL CARE WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Pet groomers and animal care workers feed, handle, train and groom animals; and assist veterinarians, animal health technologists and technicians in veterinary facilities, animal shelters, breeding and boarding kennels, zoos, laboratories, retail pet shops, riding schools, dog training schools, pet grooming and similar establishments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: bathing and feeding animals;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: leading or carrying animals to treatment room and holding them during treatment;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: cleaning and sterilizing veterinary surgical instruments;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: labelling drugs, chemicals and other pharmaceutical preparations and replenishing stock;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: sterilizing bottles, beakers and other equipment;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: cleaning, organizing, and disinfecting animal quarters such as pens, stables, cages, and yards, and animal equipment such as saddles and bridles;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: collecting and recording animal information such as weight, size, physical condition and treatments received, medications given, and food intake;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: training animals to develop and maintain desired animal behaviors for competition, entertainment, obedience, security, riding and other activities; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: grooming animals by performing tasks such as washing, brushing, clipping, and trimming coats, cutting nails and cleaning ears.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Driving instructors teach people how to drive motor vehicles.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: instructing students under actual driving conditions; and explaining and demonstrating the operation of brakes, clutch, gear selection, automatic transmission, signals and lights;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: teaching road traffic regulations;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: teaching road craft and road safety;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: advising students when they are ready to undergo driving examination;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: advising on and teaching advanced driving techniques required for emergency situations; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: illustrating and explaining handling and mechanical operation of motor vehicles and driving techniques using blackboard diagrams and audio-visual aids.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: PERSONAL SERVICES WORKERS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This Unit Group covers personal services workers not elsewhere classified in Sub-Major Group 51. Personal Services Workers.  For instance, those who provide services and companionship as dancing partners, social escorts, and night club hostesses or hosts are classified here.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Sales workers sell and demonstrate goods in wholesale or retail shops, at stalls and markets, door-to-door, via telephone or customer contact centers. They may record and accept payment for goods and services purchased, and may operate small retail outlets.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this Sub-Major Group may include the following: selling goods in wholesale or retail establishments or at street or market stalls, door-to- door, via telephone or customer contact centers; demonstrating and displaying goods to potential customers; selling and serving food for immediate consumption at counters and in the street; buying or contracting a regular supply of products to be sold; stacking and displaying goods for sale, and wrapping and packing goods sold; determining product mix, stock  and price levels for goods to be sold; operating cash registers, optical price scanners, computers or other equipment to record and accept payment for the purchase of goods and  services.  Supervision of other workers may be required in some occupations classified  here.

definition_paragraphs.text: Street and market salespersons sell goods from stalls on markets or in streets and prepare and sell hot or cold food and beverages ready for immediate consumption in streets and public places.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: obtaining permission to set up a stand at a particular place in streets, markets or other open spaces or to sell food and drinks on the streets; buying or contracting a regular supply of products to be sold; erecting and dismantling stalls and stands; transporting, storing, loading and unloading products for sale; stacking, displaying and selling goods, food and drinks  and accepting payment; wrapping and packing goods sold;  preparing food and drinks for sale; pushing, pedaling or carrying hand-cart, truck, tray or basket to bring food and drinks to the desired place in the street, or to public places such as stations or cinemas; and keeping accounts and maintaining a record of stock levels.

definition_paragraphs.text: Stall and market salespersons sell various goods from stalls on open-air or covered markets or from stalls in streets or other open spaces.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: obtaining permission to set up a stand at a particular place in streets, markets or other open spaces;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: determining product mix, stock and price levels for goods to be sold;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: buying or contracting a regular supply of goods to be sold from wholesale suppliers or directly from producers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: erecting and dismantling stalls and stands; and transporting, storing, loading and unloading goods for sale;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: demonstrating and selling goods and accepting payment;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: stacking and displaying goods for sale; and wrapping and packing goods sold; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: keeping accounts and maintaining a record of stock levels.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Street food salespersons prepare and sell, or sell previously prepared, hot or cold food and beverages ready for immediate consumption in streets and public places such as stations, cinemas, or theaters.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: obtaining permission or a license,  where required, to sell food and drinks on the street or in a public place;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: obtaining food and drinks for sale;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing, either beforehand or on the spot, food and drinks for sale;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: loading and unloading, pushing, pedaling or carrying hand-cart, truck, tray or basket to bring food and drinks to the desired place in the streets, or to public places such as stations or cinemas; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: displaying and selling food and drinks and accepting payment.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Shop salespersons sell a range of goods and services directly to the public or on behalf of retail and wholesale establishments.  They explain functions and qualities of these goods and services; and may operate small shops or supervise the activities of shop sales assistants and cashiers.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: determining customer requirements and advising on product range, price, delivery, warranties and product use and care; demonstrating and explaining and selling goods and services to customers; accepting payment for by a variety of payment methods and preparing sales invoices; undertaking or assisting with the ongoing management of stock such as product inventories and participating in stock takes; tacking and displaying goods for sale, and wrapping and packing goods sold; determining product mix, stocks and price levels for goods to be sold; and supervising and coordinating the activities of shop sales assistants, checkout operators and other workers in supermarkets and department stores.

definition_paragraphs.text: Shopkeepers operate small retail shops either independently or with support from a small number of others.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining product mix, stock  and price levels for goods to be sold;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: purchasing and ordering goods for sale from markets, wholesalers and other suppliers;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: budgeting and maintaining records of stock levels and financial transactions;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: determining prices and displaying goods for sale;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: selling goods to customers and advising them on product use;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: examining returned goods and deciding on appropriate action; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: taking inventory of goods in stock.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Shop supervisors supervise and coordinate the activities of shop sales assistants, checkout operators and other workers in retail and wholesale shops such as supermarkets and department stores.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: planning and preparing work schedules and assigning staff to specific duties;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: instructing staff on sales procedures, including how to handle difficult or complex cases;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: ensuring that customers receive prompt service;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: participating in and providing advice to managers on interviewing, hiring, training, evaluating, promoting and dismissing staff, and resolving staff grievances;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: examining returned goods and deciding on appropriate action;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: taking inventory of goods for sale and ordering new stock;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: ensuring that goods and services are correctly priced and displayed; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: ensuring that safety procedures are enforced.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Shop sales assistants sell a range of goods and services directly to the public or on behalf of retail and wholesale establishments, and explain the functions and qualities of these goods and services.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining customer requirements and advising on product range, price, delivery, warranties and product use and care;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: demonstrating and explaining to customers the establishment's goods and services;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: selling goods and services; accepting payment by a variety of payment methods; preparing sales invoices; and recording sales using cash registers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assisting with the ongoing management of stock such as product inventories and participating in stock takes; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: stacking and displaying goods for sale, and wrapping and packing goods sold.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Cashiers and ticket clerks operate cash registers, optical price scanners, computers or other equipment to record and accept payment for the purchase of goods, services and admissions in settings such as stores, restaurants and ticket offices.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: receiving and verifying payment by cash, check, credit card or automatic debit in stores, ticket offices, or similar establishments;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: giving change and issuing receipts;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: issuing tickets for attendance at sporting and cultural events;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: counting and recording money received or paid out and balancing against cash register sales records;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: receiving incoming cash, checking it against sales slips and other documents, and preparing it for deposit at bank;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating cash register to calculate total to be paid from or to clients;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: scanning, weighing and recording prices of goods; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: wrapping and placing merchandise in bags.

examples.title: Entertainment and sporting event ticket issuing clerk

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Other sales workers display, demonstrate, display and sell goods, food and services, usually to the general public, in context other than sales in markets, streets and shops.  It includes sales workers not classified in Minor Groups 521. Street and Market Salespersons; 522. Shop Salespersons; and 523. Cashiers and Ticket Clerks.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed may include: displaying and demonstrating items for sale; posing for photographs, film and video, advertising, still photography or for artistic creation; answering questions and offering advice on the use of goods and services; taking orders and making arrangements for payment, delivery and collection of goods or for  provision of services; selling goods and services; and soliciting business by approaching potential customers by going from door-to-door or using the telephone or other electronic communications media; selling fuel, lubricants and other automotive products at service stations; and providing services such as fueling, cleaning, lubricating and performing minor repairs to motor vehicles.

definition_paragraphs.text: Fashion and other models wear and display clothing and accessories and pose for photographs, film and video, advertising, still photography or for artistic creation.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: dressing in sample apparel of new or current styles or of type wanted by customer;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: walking, turning and posing to demonstrate style and characteristics of garments, fashion accessories and other merchandise to best advantage;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: posing as subject for sculpture, painting and other types of visual art;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: posing for still photography for magazines and other advertising media; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: posing for television, video and cinema commercials and other productions.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Sales demonstrators demonstrate goods at commercial premises, exhibitions and private homes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting up displays and demonstrating articles for sale to inform customers about their characteristics and mode of use, as well as to stimulate buying interest;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: answering questions and offering advice on the use of goods;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: selling goods or directing customers to sales staff;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: taking orders and making arrangements for payment, delivery and collection of goods; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: offering sample goods and distributing catalogues and advertising material.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Door-to-door salespersons sell goods and services and solicit business for an establishment, by approaching or visiting potential customers, usually residents in private homes, by going from door to door.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: giving details of various goods or services and of terms of sale by visiting clients and potential clients door-to-door;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: demonstrating or describing goods or services on offer;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: recording orders and transactions and placing orders received with suppliers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing invoices and sales contracts and accepting payment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: distributing letters, information sheets and other documents to clients;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: compiling lists of prospective clients and calling on them to obtain new business; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: travelling between sales areas and clients and transporting samples or goods for sale.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Contact center salespersons contact existing and prospective customers, using the telephone or other electronic communications media, to promote goods and services, obtain sales and arrange sales visits.  They may work from a customer contact center or from non-centralized premises.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: promoting goods and services by telephone or electronic mail, following scripts and working form lists of contacts;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: creating interest in goods and services, and seeking a sale or agreement to see sales representatives;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: arranging processing and dispatch of goods and services, information kits and brochures to customers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: arranging appointments for sales representatives;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: recording notes for follow up action and updating marketing databases to reflect changes to the status of each customer;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: reporting competitor activities and issues raised by contacts for attention by managers;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: maintaining statistics of calls made and successes achieved; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: submitting periodic reports on telemarketing activities and results.

examples.title: Sales and marketing call center agent

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Service station attendants sell fuel, lubricants and other automotive products; and provide services such as fueling, cleaning, lubricating; and performing minor repairs to motor vehicles.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: filling fuel tanks and containers to level specified by customer;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: checking and replenishing air pressure in vehicle tires, and oil and other vehicle fluid levels;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: washing vehicle windscreens and windows;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing minor repair work to vehicles such as replacing tires, light bulbs and windscreen wiper blades;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: maintaining and operating automatic car wash facilities;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: collecting payments from customers for purchases;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: cleaning petrol pumps and surrounding driveway, shop and facilities; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: undertaking stock control; and preparing reports on fuel, oil, accessories and other items sold.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Food service counter attendants serve customers at food counters and finish preparation of simple food items in restaurants, cafes, hotels, fastfood outlets, cafeterias, hospitals and other settings.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: serving food to customers at counters;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: ascertaining the products desired by the customer, assisting customer in making a choice and taking orders;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: cleaning, peeling, slicing and trimming foodstuffs using manual and electric appliances;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing simple food items and reheating prepared meals;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: portioning and wrapping food or placing it directly on plates for service to patrons;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: packaging take-away food;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: stocking refrigerators, salad and buffet bars and keeping records of the quantities of food used; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: receiving payment for food items purchased.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:
