definition_paragraphs.text: Online-selling salespersons sell goods and services via internet. They fill orders and document for shipping to customers. They work for companies that typically sell their products online.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: filling customer orders by packaging sold items and documentation for shipping to customers;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: building relationship with clients or customers in order to convince them to buy the products;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: purchasing and ordering goods for sale from markets, wholesalers and other suppliers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: budgeting and maintaining records of stock levels and financial transactions;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: composing description of products, determining their prices and shipping costs;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: advertising products on different social media platforms to attract customers;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: examining returned goods and deciding on appropriate action; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: taking inventory of goods in stock.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations included here:

definition_paragraphs.text: This Unit Group includes sales workers not classified elsewhere in Sub-Major Group 52. Sales Workers.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Personal care workers provide care, supervision and assistance for children, patients and elderly, convalescent or disabled persons in institutional and residential settings.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this Sub-Major Group usually include: assisting with mobility, washing and other personal needs; assisting children individually to learn social skills; supervising and participating in activities that enhance the child's physical, social, emotional and intellectual development in schools and pre-school; and observing and reporting concerns to appropriate medical or social service worker.

records.title: CHILD CARE WORKERS AND TEACHERS' AIDES

definition_paragraphs.text: Child care workers and teachers' aides provide care and supervision for children in schools, residential homes and child care facilities.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: assisting children individually to learn social skills; demonstrating, supervising and participating in activities that enhance the physical, social, emotional and intellectual development of children in schools and pre-schools; assisting in preparation of materials and equipment for children's education and recreational activities before-school, after-school, during vacation and in day care centers.

definition_paragraphs.text: Child care workers provide care and supervision for children in residential homes and in before-school, after-school, vacation and day care centers.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assisting children to wash, dress and feed themselves;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: taking children to and from school or outdoors for recreation;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: playing games with children, or entertaining them by reading or storytelling;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assisting in the preparation of materials and equipment for children's education and recreational activities;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: managing children's behavior and guiding their social development;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: disciplining children and recommending or initiating other measures to control behavior, such as caring for own clothing and picking up toys and books;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: observing and monitoring children's play activities; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: keeping records on individual children, including daily observations and information about activities, meals served, and medications administered.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Teachers' aides perform non-teaching duties to assist teaching staff, and provide care and supervision for children in schools and pre-schools.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: demonstrating, supervising and participating in activities that enhance the physical, social, emotional and intellectual development of children in schools and preschools;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing indoor and outdoor areas for learning and recreational activities;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assisting children with intellectual, physical, behavioral and other  learning difficulties with their studies;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assisting children individually to learn social skills;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: assisting with preparing teaching materials, and copying and collating written and printed material;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating audio-visual equipment, computers and other teaching aides; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: distributing and collecting lesson material.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: PERSONAL CARE WORKERS IN HEALTH SERVICES

definition_paragraphs.text: Personal care workers in health services provide personal care and assistance with mobility and activities of daily living to patients, and elderly, convalescent and disabled people in health care and residential settings.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: assisting patients with mobility, personal care and communication needs; sterilizing surgical and other instruments and equipment; observing and reporting concerns to the appropriate medical or social service workers, preparing patients for examination and treatment; and participating in planning the care of individuals.

definition_paragraphs.text: Health care assistants provide direct personal care and assistance with activities of daily living to patients and residents in a variety of health care settings such as hospitals, clinics, and residential nursing care facilities. They generally work in implementation of established care plans and practices, and under the direct supervision of medical, nursing or other health professionals or associate professionals.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: providing care, support and treatment to patients and residents of medical, rehabilitative and residential care facilities as per treatment plans established by medical, nursing and other health professionals;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: assisting patients with personal and therapeutic care needs such as personal hygiene, feeding, dressing, physical mobility and exercise, communication; taking oral medications; and changing dressings;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: positioning, lifting and turning patients and transporting them in wheelchairs or on movable beds; maintaining patients' environmental hygiene standards, such as cleaning patient rooms and changing bed-linen;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing massage and other non-pharmacological pain relief measures, such as during pregnancy and labor; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: observing patients’ condition, responses and behavior and reporting changes to a health professional.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Home-based personal care workers provide routine personal care and assistance with activities of daily living  to persons who are in need of such care due to effects of ageing, illness, injury, or other physical or mental condition  in  private homes and other independent residential settings.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: assisting clients with personal and therapeutic care needs such as personal hygiene, feeding, dressing, physical mobility and exercise, communication, taking oral medications and changing dressings, usually as per care plans established by a health professional;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: maintaining records of client care, changes in condition and responses to care and treatment, and reporting concerns or providing referrals to a health or social services professional;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: positioning and lifting clients with physical mobility challenges, and helping transport them in wheelchairs and motor vehicles;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing clients and families with emotional support and information and advice on topics such as nutrition, hygiene, exercise, caring for infants, or adapting to disability or illness;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: maintaining clients' environmental hygiene standards, such as changing bed linen, washing clothes and dishes, and cleaning living quarters;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: providing psychological support to clients such as through conversation or reading aloud;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: planning, purchasing, preparing, or serving meals to meet nutritional requirements and prescribed diet;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: providing support to parents and care for newborns during the post-partum period; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: scheduling and accompanying clients for appointments with medical doctors and other health professionals; or performing other errands.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: PERSONAL CARE WORKERS IN HEALTH SERVICES NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This Unit Group covers personal care workers in health services not elsewhere classified in Minor Group 532. Personal Care Workers in Health Services.  For instance the group includes occupations such as dental aid, sterilization aid, hospital orderly, medical imaging assistant, and pharmacy aide.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: cleaning and sterilizing surgical, dental and pharmaceutical instruments, bottles, beakers and other equipment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: labelling drugs, chemicals and other pharmaceutical preparations and replenishing stock on shelves;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: lifting, turning, and moving patients and transporting them in wheelchairs or on moveable beds;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing patients for examination or treatment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: setting  up instrument trays, preparing materials, and assisting dentists or radiographers during  procedures; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: exposing diagnostic X-rays.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Protective services workers protect individuals and property against fire and other hazards; maintain law and order; and enforce laws and regulations.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: preventing, fighting and extinguishing fires; rescuing people from burning buildings and accident sites and those trapped in dangerous situations; maintaining law and order, enforcing laws and regulations, patrolling public areas and arresting suspected offenders; directing traffic and assuming authority in the event of accidents; watching over and maintaining order among inmates of  prisons, reformatories or penitentiaries; patrolling or monitoring premises to guard property against theft and vandalism, controlling access to establishments and maintaining order and enforcing regulations at public events and within establishments. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Firefighters prevent, fight and extinguish fires and assist in other emergencies; protect life and property; and conduct rescue efforts.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: responding to fire alarms and other calls for assistance, such as automobile and industrial accidents, bomb threats and other emergencies;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: controlling and extinguishing fires using manual and power equipment and firefighting chemicals;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: fighting special types of fires and using special equipment in industrial establishments;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: rescuing people from burning buildings and accident sites and those trapped in dangerous situations;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: preventing or limiting the spread of dangerous substances in case of fires or accidents; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: informing the public about fire prevention.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Police officers maintain law and order; patrolling public areas; enforcing laws and regulations; and arresting suspected offenders.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: patrolling a specific area to maintain public order; respond to emergencies; protect people and property; and enforce laws and regulations;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: identifying, pursuing and arresting suspects and perpetrators of criminal acts;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: directing traffic and assuming authority in the event of accidents; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing emergency assistance to victims of accidents, crimes and natural disasters.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Prison guards watch over and maintain order among inmates of prisons, reformatories or penitentiaries.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: searching arriving prisoners, putting their valuables in safekeeping, escorting prisoners to cells and locking them in;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making periodic inspection tours of cells; and inspecting and maintaining the security of locks, windows, doors and gates;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: supervising prisoners at work, meals, or during recreation periods;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: observing the conduct and behavior of prisoners to prevent disturbances and escapes;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: patrolling prison areas to prevent escape;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assisting with the implementation of rehabilitation programs; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: escorting prisoners in transit and during temporary leaves.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Security guards patrol or monitor premises to guard property against theft and vandalism.  They control access to establishments and maintain order; and enforce regulations at public events and within establishments.

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: controlling access to establishments; monitoring and authorizing the entrance or departure of employees and  visitors; checking identification; and issuing security passes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: circulating among visitors, patrons, or employees to preserve order; protect property from theft or vandalism; and enforce the regulations of the establishment;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: responding to alarms; investigating disturbances; and contacting superiors, police or firefighters as appropriate;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: performing security checks of passengers and luggage at airports; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: picking up and ensuring the safe delivery of cash and valuables to banks, automated teller machines and retail establishments.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: PROTECTIVE SERVICES WORKERS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This Unit Group covers protective services workers not elsewhere classified in Minor Group 541. Protective Services Workers.  For instance, the group includes lifeguards, crossing guards and animal control officers.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: patrolling beaches and swimming pools to prevent accidents; and to rescue bathers from drowning;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: monitoring traffic flow to locate safe gaps through which pedestrians can cross streets;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: responding to citizen complaints concerning stray domestic animals, livestock and wildlife; issuing warnings and citations to owners; and impounding lost, homeless and dangerous animals;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: patrolling an assigned area to enforce parking regulations; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: directing traffic.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: SKILLED AGRICULTURAL, FORESTRY AND FISHERY WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Skilled agricultural, forestry and fishery workers grow and harvest field or tree and shrub crops, gather wild fruits and plants, breed, tend or hunt animals, produce a variety of animal husbandry products, cultivate, conserve and exploit forests, breed or catch fish and cultivate or gather other forms of aquatic life in order to provide food, shelter and income for themselves and their households. Most occupations in this major group require skills at the second ISCO skill level.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by skilled agricultural, forestry and fishery workers usually include: preparing the soil; sowing, planting, spraying, fertilizing and harvesting field crops; growing fruit and other tree and shrub crops; growing garden vegetables and horticultural products; gathering wild fruits and plants; breeding, raising, tending or hunting animals mainly to obtain meat, milk, hair, fur, skin, sericultural, apiarian or other products; cultivating, conserving and exploiting forests; breeding or catching fish; cultivating or gathering other forms of aquatic life; storing and carrying out some basic processing of their produce; selling their products to purchasers, marketing organizations or at markets. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Market-oriented skilled agricultural workers plan, organize and perform farming operations to grow and harvest field or tree and shrub crops and produce a variety of animals and animal products for sale or delivery on a regular basis to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include: preparing the soil; sowing, planting, spraying, fertilizing and harvesting field crops, growing fruit and other tree and shrub crops; growing garden vegetables and horticultural products; raising, breeding and tending animals mainly to obtain meat, milk, hair, fur, skin, sericultural, apiarian or other products; storing and carrying out some processing of their produce; selling their products to purchasers, marketing organizations or at markets. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Market gardeners and crop growers plan, organize and perform operations to grow and harvest field crops, to grow fruit and other tree and shrub crops, to grow garden vegetables and medicinal and other plants, and to produce horticultural and horticultural nurseries products, for sale or delivery on a regular basis to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: monitoring market activity and conditions, determining types and quantities of crops to be grown, and planning and coordinating production accordingly; purchasing seeds, bulbs and fertilizer; investing in land and land improvements; preparing land, sowing, planting, cultivating and harvesting various crops; tending working animals and maintaining farm buildings, machinery and equipment; producing saplings, bulbs and seeds; storing and carrying out some processing of produce; delivering or marketing farm products. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Workers in this unit group plan and carry out the necessary operations to grow and harvest rice for sale or delivery on a regular basis to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets. They may grow other secondary crops.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: determining the kinds and amounts of rice to be grown;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: purchasing seeds, fertilizer and other supplies;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: renting or investing in land and land improvements, buildings, working animals, equipment and machinery;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: performing farm operations such as land preparation, sowing, planting, cultivating and harvesting rice;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: storing and carrying out some basic processing of rice;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: tending working animals and maintaining farm buildings, machinery and equipment; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: delivering or marketing farm products.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Tree and shrub crop growers plan organize and perform farming operations to grow and harvest trees and shrubs, such as fruit trees, tree nuts, coffee and cacao and other tree and shrub crop growers for sale or delivery on a regular basis to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: monitoring market activity and conditions, determining types and quantities of crops to be grown, and planning and coordinating production accordingly;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing soil by hand or machine, and spreading fertilizers and manure;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: selecting and sowing seeds, and planting seedlings;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: maintaining crops by cultivating soil, by transplanting, pruning or thinning trees and shrubs, and by setting up and operating irrigation equipment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: controlling weeds, pests and diseases, by applying herbicides and pesticides;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: tending trees or bushes, collecting sap and harvesting crops;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: inspecting, cleaning, grading, packaging, storing and loading crops for sale or delivery to market;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: tending working animals and maintaining farm buildings, structures, equipment and water supply systems;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: inspecting, cleaning, grading, packaging, storing and loading crops for sale or delivery to market;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: storing and carrying out some processing of produce;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: promoting and marketing products, arranging the sale, purchase and transportation of produce and supplies and maintaining and evaluating records of farm activities and transactions; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: training and supervising workers in crop production, maintenance duties, and health and safety precautions and hiring and discharging workers and contractors.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Animal producers plan, organize and perform farming operations to breed and raise domesticated animals, poultry, insects and non-domesticated animals for the production of meat, dairy products, honey, skins, textiles and other products or for use as working, sporting or recreational animals, for sale or delivery to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets.

Task performed usually include: monitoring market activity and conditions, determining kinds and amounts of products to produce, planning and coordinating production accordingly; raising, feeding and tending animals; preparing animals or animal products for market; monitoring and examining animals to detect illness, injury, or disease, and to check physical condition such as rate of weight gain; performing duties related to animal reproduction, such as breeding, artificial insemination, and helping with animal births; renting or investing in and maintaining and cleaning buildings, machinery, equipment, and structures; storing and carrying out some processing of produce; promoting and marketing products, arranging the sale, purchase and transportation of stock, produce and supplies and maintaining and evaluating records of activities and transactions; training and supervising workers in animal care procedures, maintenance duties, and health and safety precautions and hiring and discharging workers and contractors.

definition_paragraphs.text: Market-oriented skilled forestry, fishery and hunting workers plan, organize and perform operations to cultivate, conserve and exploit natural and plantation forests, breed and raise fish, harvest and catch fish and hunt and trap animals, for sale or delivery on a regular basis to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major groups usually include: renting or investing, equipment and machinery and purchasing supplies; planning and undertaking forestry, aquaculture, fishery and hunting operations; maintaining buildings, tanks, machinery, and other equipment; delivering or marketing products; supervising and training other workers.

definition_paragraphs.text: Forestry and related workers plan, organize and perform operations to cultivate, conserve and exploit natural and plantation forests.

Tasks usually include: assessing sites for reforestation, selecting seedlings and planting trees using manual planting tools and establishing and caring for forest stands; young forest stands, trim, top and fell trees and saw them into logs; shaping rough wooden products from logs at felling site; stacking logs and loading them in chutes or floating them down rivers; keeping watch to detect forest fires, participating in fire fighting operations complete fire fighting reports and maintaining fire fighting equipment; controlling weeds and undergrowth in regenerating forest stands using manual tools and chemicals; operating and maintaining a skidder, bulldozer or other prime mover to pull a variety of scarification or site preparation equipment over areas to be regenerated; collecting seed cones, pruning trees, assisting in planting surveys and marking trees for subsequent operations; training and supervising other workers in forestry procedures, including forestry laborers and plant operators.

Workers in this unit group plan and manage the necessary operations to cultivate trees for sale or delivery of forest products on a regular basis to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets.

tasks.text: herding or leading livestock to pastures, grazing land and water supplies;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: raising, tending, feeding and milking animals or draining blood from them;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: breeding animals and helping with animal births;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: slaughtering and skinning animals and preparing them and their products for consumption or sale;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: carrying out some processing of animal products;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: building and maintaining makeshift houses and other shelters for own use;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: making tools, clothes and utensils for use by the household;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: fetching water and gathering firewood; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: buying, bartering and selling animals and some products.

records.title: SUBSISTENCE MIXED CROP AND LIVESTOCK FARMERS
SUBSISTENCE MIXED CROP AND LIVESTOCK FARMERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Subsistence mixed crop and livestock farmers grow and harvest field or tree and shrub crops, vegetables and fruit, gather wild fruits, medicinal and other plants, tend or hunt animals, and/or catch fish and gather various forms of aquatic life in order to provide food, shelter and a minimum of cash income for themselves and their households.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: preparing the soil, sowing, planting, tending and harvesting field crops;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: growing vegetables, fruit and other tree and shrub crops;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: gathering wild fruits, medicinal and other plants;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: breeding, tending and feeding animals and poultry mainly to obtain meat, eggs, milk, hair, skin or other products;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: fetching water and gathering firewood;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: storing produce for later use and carrying out some processing of produce;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: building and maintaining makeshift houses and other shelters for own use;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: making tools, clothes and utensils for use by the household;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: selling or bartering some products at local markets.

records.title: SUBSISTENCE FISHERS, HUNTERS, TRAPPERS AND GATHERERS
SUBSISTENCE FISHERS, HUNTERS, TRAPPERS AND GATHERERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Subsistence fishers, hunters, trappers and gatherers gather wild fruits medicinal and other plants; hunt and trap animals; and catch fish and gather various forms of aquatic life in order to provide food, shelter, and a minimum of cash income for themselves and their households.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: gathering wild fruits, roots, medicinal and other plants;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: hunting or trapping animals mainly to obtain meat, milk, hair, skin or other products;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: fetching water and gathering firewood;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: catching fish and gathering other forms of aquatic life;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: storing or carrying out some processing of their produce;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: building and maintaining houses and other shelters;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: making tools, clothes and utensils for use by the household; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: selling or bartering some products at local markets.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Craft and related trades workers apply specific knowledge and skills in the fields to construct and maintain buildings, form metal, erect metal structures, set machine tools, or make, fit, maintain and repair machinery, equipment or tools, carry out printing work produce or process foodstuffs, textiles, or wooden, metal and other equipment or tools, carry out printing work produce or process foodstuffs, textiles, or wooden, metal and other articles, including handicraft goods.

The work is carried out by hand and by hand-powered and other tools which are used to reduce the amount of physical effort and time required for specific tasks, as well as to improve the quality of the products. The tasks call for an understanding of all stages of the production process, the materials and tools used, and the nature and purpose of the final product. Most occupations in this major group require skills at the second ISCO skill level.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by craft and related trades workers usually include: constructing, maintaining and repairing buildings and other structures; casting, welding and shaping metal; installing and erecting heavy metal structures, tackle and related equipment; making machinery, tools, equipment, and other metal articles; setting for operators, or setting and operating various machine tools; fitting, maintaining and repairing industrial machinery, including engines and vehicles, as well as  electrical and electronic instruments and other equipment; making precision instruments, jewelry, household and other precious-metal articles, pottery, glass and related products; producing handicrafts; executing printing work; and  producing and processing foodstuffs and various articles made of wood, textiles, leather and related materials. Supervision of other workers may be included.

records.title: BUILDING AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS, EXCLUDING ELECTRICIANS

definition_paragraphs.text: Building and related trades workers construct, maintain and repair buildings, erect and repair foundations, walls and structures of brick, stone and similar materials, shape and finish stone for building and other purposes, and extract and work solid minerals from underground or surface mines or quarries. The work is carried out by hand and by hand-powered and other tools which are used to reduce the amount of physical effort and time required for specific tasks, as well as to improve the quality of the products. The tasks call for an understanding of the work organization, the materials and tools used, and the nature and purpose of the final product.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group include: constructing, maintaining and repairing buildings and other structures using traditional and/or modern building techniques; constructing and repairing foundations, walls and structures of brick, stone and similar materials; breaking quarried stone into slabs or blocks; cutting, shaping and finishing stone for building, ornamental, monumental and other purposes; erecting reinforced concrete frameworks and structures as well as finishing and repairing cement surfaces; cutting, shaping, assembling and maintaining wooden structures and fittings; and performing miscellaneous construction and building maintenance tasks.

records.title: BUILDING FRAME AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Building frame and related trades workers construct, maintain and repair buildings, erect and repair foundations, walls and structures of brick, stone and similar materials, shape and finish stone for building and other purposes, and perform miscellaneous construction and building maintenance tasks.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this minor group include: constructing, maintaining and repairing buildings and other structures by using traditional and/or modern building techniques; constructing and repairing foundations, walls and structures of brick, stone and similar materials; breaking quarried stone into slabs or blocks; cutting, shaping and finishing stone for building, ornamental, monumental and other purposes; erecting reinforced concrete frameworks and structures as well as finishing and repairing cement surfaces; cutting, shaping, assembling and maintaining wooden structures and fittings; and performing miscellaneous construction and building maintenance tasks. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: House builders erect, maintain and repair houses and similar small buildings using either traditional or modern techniques and materials.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: preparing ground for erecting building or other structures;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: erecting structures to support roof, and building and covering walls with appropriate materials;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: fixing rafters to roof and covering with roofing material;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: levelling floor to make it smooth and serviceable;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: maintaining and repairing existing structures;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: arranging for specialized work such as bricklaying, painting, plumbing and electrical wiring to be done by subcontractors; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: coordinating and supervising the activities of subcontractors, laborers and other workers.

definition_paragraphs.text: Bricklayers and related workers lay bricks, pre-cut stones and other types of building blocks in mortar to construct and repair walls, partitions, arches and other structures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: laying stone, brick and similar building blocks to construct or repair walls, partitions, fireplaces and other structures such as smokestacks, furnaces, converters, kilns and ovens, piers and abutments;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: laying footpaths, kerbs and pavements; and

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: laying bricks or other masonry to build patios, garden walls and other decorative installations.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: STONEMASONS, STONE CUTTERS, SPLITTERS AND CARVERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Stonemasons, stone cutters, splitters and carvers cut and shape hard and soft stone blocks and slabs for the construction and maintenance of stone structures and monumental masonry, and carve designs and figures in stone.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: driving wedges into quarried stone to break it into slabs or blocks;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: selecting and grading slabs and blocks of granite, marble, and other stone;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: cutting, shaping and finishing building and monumental stone such as granite or marble by using hand or hand-powered tools;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: making patterns and marking shapes on stone for subsequent sawing, planing, drilling and other dressing and cutting operations;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: cutting and carving characters, figures or designs on stone blocks used for monuments or memorials;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: setting stone in the erection of monuments and memorials; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: repairing and replacing stonework on old buildings, churches and monuments.

related_occupations.title: Stone cutting or processing machine operator
related_occupations.raw: Stone cutting or processing machine operator - 8112

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: CONCRETE PLACERS, CONCRETE FINISHERS AND RELATED WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Concrete placers, concrete finishers and related workers erect reinforced concrete frameworks and structures, make forms for molding concrete,  reinforce concrete surfaces, cement openings in walls or casings for wells, finish and repair cement surfaces and carry out terrazzo work.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: constructing and repairing reinforced concrete floors, walls, tanks, silos and other concrete structures;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making shuttering or assembling prefabricated forms for molding concrete;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: cementing openings in walls or casings for wells;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: finishing and smoothing surfaces of concrete structures; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: applying a durable, smooth surfacing composed of cement, sand pigment and marble particles to floors, known as a terrazzo finish.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Carpenters and joiners cut, shape, assemble, erect, maintain and repair various types of structures and fittings made from wood and other materials.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: making, altering and repairing structural and other woodwork at a work-bench and on a construction site;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: constructing, erecting and installing heavy-framed wooden structures on building sites;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: fitting, assembling and altering internal and external fixtures of buildings, such as walls, doors, door and window frames, facings and paneling;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: making, repairing and fitting scenic equipment for theatrical performances, motion picture or television productions; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: constructing, assembling, altering and repairing wooden fixtures and fittings in train coaches, aircraft, ships, boats, floats, and other vehicles.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: BUILDING FRAME AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers building frame and related trades workers not classified elsewhere in Minor group 711, Building frame and related trades workers. For instance the group includes steeplejacks, scaffolders and demolition workers.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: climbing and performing miscellaneous construction and building maintenance work on tall structures such as towers, chimneys and spires;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: erecting temporary metal or wooden scaffolding on building sites; and

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: demolishing buildings and other structures.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: BUILDING FINISHERS AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Building finishers and related trades workers cover, apply or install, maintain and repair roofs, floors, walls, insulation systems, glass in windows or other frames, as well as plumbing, piping and electrical systems in buildings and other structures.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: covering roof frameworks with one or more kinds of material; installing parquet and other kinds of flooring or covering floors and walls with tiles or mosaic panels; applying plaster to walls and ceilings; applying insulating material to walls, floors and ceilings; cutting, fitting and setting glass in windows and similar openings; and installing plumbing and pipeline systems; installing electrical wiring and related equipment. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Roofers build and repair roofs on all types of buildings using one or more kinds of materials.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: studying drawings, specifications and construction sites to determine materials required;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: covering roof frameworks with slate and pre-fabricated tiles to cover pitched roofs;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: laying a waterproof shield and fixing metallic or synthetic materials to a building’s frame;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: sizing and cutting roofing materials to fit around edges corners and protuberances such as chimney;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: using natural materials such as thatching to provide roof coverings; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: creating temporary structures such as scaffolding and ladders.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Floor layers and tile setters install, maintain and repair flooring, and cover floors, walls and other surfaces with tiles or mosaic panels for decorative or other purposes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: preparing floor areas for covering with a variety of materials;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: assembling carpet, tiles or other materials and laying them on floors according to design and other specifications;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing wall areas for covering with tiles or other materials for decorative or other purposes such as acoustic insulation; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: setting tiles and constructing and laying mosaic panels to walls, floors and other surfaces.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Plasterers install, maintain and repair plasterboard in buildings, and apply decorative and protective coverings of plaster, cement and similar material to the interiors and exteriors of structures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: applying one or more coats of plaster to interior walls and ceilings of buildings to produce finished surface;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: measuring, marking and installing ornamental plaster panels, and casting and trimming ornamental plaster cornices;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: applying protective and decorative covering of cement, plaster and similar materials to exterior building surfaces; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: making and installing decorative plaster fixtures of fibrous plaster.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Insulation workers apply and repair insulating materials to buildings, boilers, pipes or refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: cutting insulation material by size and shape;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: applying slabs and sheets of insulating or sound-absorbing materials to walls, floors and ceilings of buildings;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: blow and pack insulating or sound-absorbing materials into cavities between walls, floors and ceilings of buildings with power-driven machines;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: examining plans, specifications and work sites to determine the type, quality and quantity of insulation material required;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: applying insulating materials to exposed surfaces of equipment such as boilers, pipes and tanks; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: insulating refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment.

examples.title: Refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment insulation worker

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Glaziers measure, cut, finish, fit and install flat glass and mirrors.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: selecting the type of glass to be used, cutting to right size and shape and installing in windows, doors, showers and partitions of buildings;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: installing glass and mirrors in skylights, display cases, interior walls and ceilings;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: installing or replacing windscreens in vehicles or boats; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: creating decorative glass features such as glass walls, staircases, balustrades and stained-glass windows.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Plumbers and pipe fitters assemble, install, repair and maintain pipe systems, fittings and fixtures for water, gas, drainage, sewerage systems, and hydraulic and pneumatic equipment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: measuring, cutting, threading, bending, jointing, assembling, installing, maintaining and repairing pipes, fittings and fixtures of drainage, heating, water supply and sewerage systems;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: installing gas appliances, dishwashers and water heaters, sinks and toilets using hand and power tools;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: laying clay, concrete or cast-iron pipes in ditches to form sewers, drains or water mains, or for other purposes; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: inspecting, examining and testing installed systems and pipes, using pressure gauge, hydrostatic testing, observation or other methods.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Air conditioning and refrigeration mechanics assemble, install, maintain and repair air conditioning and refrigeration systems and equipment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: interpreting blueprints, drawings or other specifications;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: assembling, installing and repairing components such as compressors, motors, condensers, evaporators, switches and gauges for air conditioning and refrigeration systems;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: connecting piping and equipment by bolting, riveting, welding or brazing; and

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: testing systems, diagnosing faults and performing routine maintenance or servicing.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: PAINTERS, BUILDING STRUCTURE CLEANERS AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Painters, building structure cleaners and related trades workers prepare surfaces and apply paint and similar materials to buildings and other structures, vehicles or various manufactured articles. They cover interior walls and ceilings with wallpaper, clean chimneys and exterior surfaces of buildings and other  structures.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: preparing surfaces and applying paint and similar materials to buildings and other structures; applying paint or varnish to vehicles or various manufactured articles, usually with a hand-spraying device; covering interior walls and ceilings with wallpaper, silk or other fabrics; cleaning chimneys; and cleaning exterior surfaces of buildings and other structures. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Painters and related workers prepare surfaces of buildings and other structures for painting, apply protective and decorative coats of paint or similar materials, or cover interior walls and ceilings of buildings with wallpaper or other finishes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: cleaning and preparing walls and other surfaces of buildings for painting or wallpapering;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: selecting and preparing paints to required colors by mixing pigments and additives;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: applying or spraying paint, varnish, and similar materials to surfaces, fixtures and fittings of buildings;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: measuring and hanging wallpaper or other fabrics on interior walls and ceilings; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: applying paints, varnishes and stains to surfaces using brushes, rollers and sprays.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Spray painters and varnishers operate spray painting and varnishing equipment to apply protective coatings to manufactured items or structures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: preparing surfaces to be coated using a variety of methods to remove grease, dirt and rust;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: painting cars, buses, trucks and other vehicles, and applying varnish and other protective coatings; and

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: applying paint as well as protective coatings of enamel or varnish on metal, wooden and other manufactured products, usually with a hand-spraying device.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Building structure cleaners clean exterior surfaces of buildings and other structures, and remove soot from chimneys.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: cleaning exterior surfaces of stone, brick, metal or similar materials by means of chemicals, or a jet of steam or sand applied under high pressure;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: removing soot from flues, chimneys and connecting pipes; and

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: removing asbestos, mold and fire damaged surfaces from buildings.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: METAL, MACHINERY AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Metal, machinery and related trades workers cast, weld, forge and, by  other methods, form metal, erect, maintain and repair heavy metal structures, engage in machine-tool setting as well as in fitting, maintaining and repairing machinery, including engines, vehicles, or produce tools and various non-precious-metal articles.

The work is carried out by hand and by hand-powered and other tools which  are used to reduce the amount of physical effort and time required for specific tasks, as well as to improve the quality of the products. The tasks call for an understanding of the work organization, the materials and tools used, and the nature and purpose of the final product.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include: making  molds and cores for casting metal; casting, welding and shaping metal; installing, erecting, maintaining and repairing heavy metal structures, tackle  and related equipment; forging and forming steel and other non-precious metals  to make and repair machinery, tools, equipment and other articles; setting for operators or setting and operating various machine tools; and fitting, maintaining  and repairing industrial machinery, including engines and vehicles. Supervision of other workers may be included.

records.title: SHEET AND STRUCTURAL METAL WORKERS, MOLDERS AND WELDERS, AND RELATED WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Sheet and structural metal workers, molders and welders, and related workers, make molds and cores for casting metal, weld and cut metal parts, make and repair articles of sheet metal, and install, erect, maintain and repair heavy metal structures, tackle, cable-cars and related equipment.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: making molds and cores for casting metal; casting, welding and shaping metal parts; making and repairing articles of sheet metal such as sheet steel, copper, tin, or brass; and installing, erecting, maintaining and repairing heavy metal structures, as well as tackle, cable cars and related equipment.

definition_paragraphs.text: Metal molders and coremakers make molds and cores for casting metal.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: making molds by hand or using auxiliary machines on a bench for small metal castings, on the foundry floor, or in a pit for large castings;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making cores for use in metal molds;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: cleaning and smoothing molds, core boxes, and repairing surface imperfections;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: moving and positioning work pieces such as mold sections, patterns, and bottom boards, using cranes, or signaling others to move work pieces;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: positioning patterns inside mold sections and clamping sections together;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: cutting spouts, runner holes and sprue holes into molds; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: lifting upper mold sections from lower sections and remove molded patterns.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Welders and flame cutters weld and cut metal parts using gas flame, electric arc and other sources of heat to melt and cut, or to melt and fuse metal.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: welding metal parts using gas flame, or an electric arc, thermite compound or other methods;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating resistance-welding machines;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: using blowtorch to make and repair lead linings, pipes, floors and other lead fixtures;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: brazing metal parts together;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: cutting metal pieces using gas flame or an electric arc;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: joining metal parts by hand soldering;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring the fitting, burning, and welding processes to avoid overheating of parts or warping, shrinking, distortion, or expansion of material; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: examining work pieces for defects and measuring work pieces with straight edges or templates to ensure conformance with specifications.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Sheet metal workers make, install and repair articles and parts of articles made out of sheet metal such as sheet steel, copper, tin, brass, aluminum, zinc or galvanized iron.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: marking sheet metal for cutting and shaping;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making and repairing household utensils and other articles in tin, copper and light alloys, or ornamental articles and fittings;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: making and repairing boilers, tanks, vats and similar containers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: installing and repairing sheet-metal parts of vehicles and aircraft;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: converting blueprints into shop drawings to be followed in the construction and assembly of sheet metal products;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: determining project requirements, including scope, assembly sequences, and required methods and materials, according to blueprints, drawings, and written or verbal instructions; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: inspecting product quality and installation to ensure conformance to specifications.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Structural metal preparers and erectors assemble, erect and dismantle structural metal frames of buildings and other structures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: marking metal framework as a guide when drilling, cutting, and shaping them for use in buildings, ships and other structures;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: drilling, cutting and shaping structural steel in a workshop;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: erecting steel framework for buildings, bridges and other constructions;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: assembling and erecting the framework and other metal parts of ships' structures;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: shaping and fitting structural-steel plates of ships under construction or repair; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: riveting structural-metal members by hand, machine or pneumatic riveter.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Riggers and cable splicers assemble rigging gear to move and position equipment and structural components, or install and maintain cables, ropes and wires on construction sites, buildings or other structures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: estimating the size, shape and weight of objects to be moved and deciding on the type of equipment to move them;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: installing and repairing cables, ropes, wires, pulleys and other tackle;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: joining, repairing and fitting attachments to wires, ropes and cables;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: working as member of crew erecting and repairing derricks for drilling water, gas and oil-wells;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: lifting and mounting scenery, lighting and other equipment in theatres and on film sets; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: installing and maintaining communication towers, aerial cableways, funicular railways, ski lifts and similar infrastructure.
