section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: BLACKSMITHS, TOOLMAKERS AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Blacksmiths, toolmakers and related trades workers, hammer and forge bars, rods or ingots of iron, steel and other metals to make and repair various kinds of tools, equipment and other articles, set machine tools for operators or set and operate various machine tools, and polish and sharpen surfaces.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: hammering and forging iron, steel and other metals to make and repair various kinds of tools, equipment and other articles; setting machine tools for operators or setting and operating various machine tools working to fine tolerances; and polishing and sharpening metal surfaces and tools.

records.title: BLACKSMITHS, HAMMERSMITHS AND FORGING PRESS WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Blacksmiths, hammersmiths and forging press workers hammer and forge bars, rods, ingots and plates of iron, steel or other metals, and draw wire to make and repair various kinds of tools, metal articles, pieces of equipment, and agricultural and related implements.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: heating metal in forge furnace and manufacturing and repairing articles by drawing, bending;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: cutting, hammering metal on an anvil, punching, shearing, joining and hardening or tempering;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: shaping heated metal into forgings on power hammer equipped with open dies;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating closed-die drop hammer to forge metal articles;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating a power-press machine equipped with closed dies to forge metal articles;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: drawing wire;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: reading work orders or blueprints to determine specified tolerances and sequences of operations for machine setup; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: measuring and inspecting machine parts to ensure conformance to product specifications.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Toolmakers and related workers make and repair custom made and specialized tools, sports guns, locks, dies, patterns machinery components and other metal articles using hand and machine tools to work metal to fine tolerances.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: reading and interpreting engineering drawings and specifications of tools, dies, prototypes or models;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: preparing templates and sketches, and determining work processes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: visualizing and computing dimensions, sizes, shapes, and tolerances of assemblies, based on specifications;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: positioning, securing and measuring metal stock or castings to lay out for machining;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: setting up, operating and maintaining conventional and computer numerically controlled machine tools to cut, turn, mill, plane, drill, bore, grind or otherwise shape workpiece to prescribed dimensions and finish;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: fitting and assembling parts to make and repair jigs, fixtures and gauges;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: repairing and modifying sports guns and other small arms;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: making, fitting, assembling, repairing and installing lock parts and locks;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: making and repairing metal patterns for preparation of foundry molds;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: laying out lines and reference points on metal stock to guide other workers who cut, turn, mill, grind or otherwise shape metal; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: verifying dimensions, alignments, and clearances of finished parts for conformance to specifications, using precision measuring instruments and testing completed items for proper operation.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: METAL WORKING MACHINE TOOL SETTERS AND OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Metal working machine tool setters and operators set and/or operate, various machine tools working to fine tolerances.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting one or more types of machine tool for production of metal articles in standardized series;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and monitoring metalworking machines, such as lathes, milling, planing, boring, drilling, grinding or honing machines, including multi-purpose numerically controlled metalworking machines;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: performing similar tasks when machining plastics and other metal substitutes;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: observing machine operations to detect work piece defects or machine malfunctions, adjusting machines as necessary;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: inspecting work pieces for defects, and measuring work pieces to determine accuracy of machine operation, using rules, templates, or other measuring instruments; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: changing worn machine accessories, such as cutting tools and brushes, using hand tools.

examples.title: Metal working numerical control machine setter-operator

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: METAL POLISHERS, WHEEL GRINDERS AND TOOL SHARPENERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Metal polishers, wheel grinders and tool sharpeners polish and grind metal surfaces and sharpen tools.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating fixed or portable buffing and polishing machines;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: sharpening cutting tools and instruments using grinding wheels or mechanically operated grinding machines;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: repairing, adjusting and sharpening saw blades and metal teeth of cylinders in textile carding machines;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: dressing grinding wheels, according to specifications;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: monitoring machine operations to determine whether adjustments are necessary; stop machines when problems occur;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: inspecting, feeling, and measuring work pieces to ensure that surfaces and dimensions meet specifications; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: selecting and mounting grinding wheels on machines, according to specifications, using hand tools and applying knowledge of abrasives and grinding procedures.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Machinery mechanics and repairers fit, install, maintain and repair engines, vehicles, agricultural or industrial machinery and similar mechanical equipment.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: fitting, installing, maintaining and repairing engines, vehicles, agricultural or industrial machinery and similar mechanical equipment.

definition_paragraphs.text: Motor vehicle mechanics and repairers fit, install, maintain, service and repair engines and the mechanical and related equipment of passenger cars, delivery trucks, motorcycles and other motor vehicles.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: detecting and diagnosing faults in engines and parts;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: fitting, examining, testing and servicing motor vehicle and motorcycle engines;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: replacing engine components or complete engines;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: fitting, examining, adjusting, dismantling, rebuilding and replacing defective parts of motor vehicles;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: installing or adjusting motors and brakes, and adjusting steering or other parts of motor vehicles;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: installing, adjusting, servicing and replacing mechatronics components of motor vehicles;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: performing scheduled maintenance services, such as oil changes, lubrications and engine tune-ups, to achieve smoother running of vehicles and ensure compliance with pollution regulations; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: reassembling engines and parts after being repaired.

examples.title: Motor vehicle engine and fuel systems service technician

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Aircraft engine repairers and mechanics fit, service, repair and overhaul aircraft engines and assemblies, such as airframes, hydraulic, and pneumatic systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: fitting, examining, testing and servicing aircraft engines;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: replacing engine components or complete engines;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: examining  and inspecting airframes and aircraft components, including landing gear, hydraulic systems, and de-icers to detect wear, cracks, breaks, leaks, or other problems;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: maintaining, repairing, overhauling, modifying and testing aircraft structural, mechanical and hydraulic systems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: reading and interpreting manuals, service bulletins, and other specifications to determine the feasibility and method of repairing or replacing malfunctioning or damaged components;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: maintaining, repairing, and rebuilding aircraft structures, functional components, and parts such as wings and fuselage, rigging, hydraulic units, oxygen systems, fuel systems, electrical systems, gaskets, and seals;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: inspecting completed work to certify that maintenance meets standards and the aircraft is ready for operation;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: maintaining repair logs, documenting all preventive and corrective aircraft maintenance;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: installing and testing electrical and electronic components, assemblies, and systems in aircraft; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: connecting components to assemblies such as radio systems, instruments, magnetos, inverters, and in-flight refueling systems.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: AGRICULTURAL AND INDUSTRIAL MACHINERY MECHANICS AND REPAIRERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Agricultural and industrial machinery mechanics and repairers fit, install, examine, service and repair engines, agricultural and industrial machinery and mechanical equipment, except motor vehicle, aircraft and electric motors.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: fitting, installing, examining, servicing and repairing engines, machinery and mechanical equipment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: oiling and greasing stationary engines and machinery;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: inspecting and testing new machinery and mechanical equipment for conformity with standards and specifications;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: disassembling machinery and equipment to remove parts and make repairs;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: examining parts for defects such as breakage and excessive wear;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating newly repaired machinery and equipment to verify the adequacy of repairs; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: recording repairs and maintenance performed.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Bicycle and related repairers fit, maintain, service and repair the mechanical and related equipment of bicycles, rickshaws, baby carriages, wheelchairs and similar non-motorized transport equipment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: examining, servicing and repairing bicycles and other non-motorized transport equipment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: cleaning and lubricating bearings and other moving parts;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: replacing and repairing components and accessories, such as brakes, driving chain mechanism, wheels, handle bars etc.;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: changing tires and controlling air pressure;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: spray painting frames; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assembling new bicycles, wheelchairs and similar non-motorized equipment.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Handicraft and printing workers make and  repair precision instruments, musical instruments, various articles such as  jewelry, precious metalware, ceramics, porcelain ware and glassware, as well  as handicrafts made of wood or textile, leather or related materials, or they perform printing or book-binding tasks.

The work is carried out by hand and by hand-powered and other tools which  are used to reduce the amount of physical effort and time required for specific tasks, as well as to improve the quality of the products. The tasks call for an understanding of the work organization, the materials and  tools used, and the nature and purpose of the final product.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include: making and repairing nautical, meteorological, optical and other precision  instruments and equipment; making and repairing musical instruments; making  jewelry and precious metalware; making pottery, porcelain ware, ceramics and glassware; painting and decorating various articles; producing handicraft  articles in wood or textile, leather and related materials; and performing  printing or book-binding tasks. Supervision of other workers may be included.

definition_paragraphs.text: Handicraft workers combine artistic and manual skills to design, make, repair, adjust, maintain and decorate precision instruments, musical instruments, jewelry and other precious-metals, pottery and porcelain ware. They apply traditional and/or recently developed techniques to carve, mold, assemble, weave and decorate various glass, ceramics, textile, straw, stone, wood and leather articles.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: making, calibrating, repairing, maintaining and installing musical and precision instruments; fabricating, adjusting, repairing, or appraising jewelry, ceremonial or religious items, gold, silver, other precious metals, or gems; cutting, filing, polishing and setting precious and semiprecious stones including gems and diamonds and engraving designs on jewelry and precious metal articles; preparing pottery, porcelain ware, sanitary ware, bricks, tiles and abrasive wheels by hand or by machine; blowing, molding, pressing, cutting, trimming, grinding and polishing glass, shaping molten glass according to patterns; decorating articles made of wood, metal, textiles, glass, ceramics and other materials, and planning, laying out and painting letters, figures, monograms and designs to make signs; applying traditional techniques like seasoning, impregnation to prepare wood, straw, rattan, reeds, stone, clay, shells, and other materials, and carving, molding, assembling, weaving, or painting and decorating various articles for personal or household use, or for decorative purposes; preparing materials to make wicker furniture, brushes and brooms and weaving various kinds of baskets; and applying  traditional techniques and patterns to produce woven fabrics, knitted, embroidered and other garments and household articles.

definition_paragraphs.text: Precision-instrument makers and repairers make, calibrate, repair, maintain, adjust and install mechanical watches, clocks, nautical, meteorological, optical, orthopedic and other precision instruments and equipment and set them for correct performance.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: repairing, cleaning, and adjusting mechanisms of timing instruments, such as watches and clocks;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: adjusting timing regulators, using  calipers, watch-rate recorders, and tweezers;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: cleaning, rinsing, and drying timepiece parts, using solutions and ultrasonic or mechanical watch-cleaning machines;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: testing timepiece accuracy and performance, using meters and other electronic instruments;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: testing accuracy of meters, gauges, indicators, or other recording or controlling instruments to locate defective components and for conformance to standards;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: calibrating instruments or scales, using hand tools, computer, or electronic devices;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: inspecting components, connections, and drive mechanisms to detect defects;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: assembling instruments and devices, such as barometers, control valves, gyroscopes, hygrometers, speedometers, tachometers, and thermostats;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: testing, calibrating, and adjusting electronic, mercurial, aneroid, and other types of meteorological instruments for compliance with printed specifications and schematic diagrams, using voltmeters, oscilloscopes, tube testers, and other test instruments;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: adjusting and repairing masts, supporting structures, clearance lights, control panels, control cabling and wiring, and other electrical and mechanical devices;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: repairing and setting optical instruments such as microscopes, telescopes, theodolites, sextants; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: checking whether assembled units conform to specifications and ensuring stipulated performance and sensitivity by standard tests.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Musical-instrument makers and tuners make, assemble, repair, adjust, restore musical instruments and tune them to the required pitch with hand or power tools. They usually specialize in one type of instrument, such as string instruments, brass instruments pianos, reed instruments or percussion instruments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: fabricating and assembling musical instruments and instrument parts of wood, ebonite, metal, leather and other materials;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: repairing or replacing musical instrument parts and components, such as strings, bridges, felts, and keys, using hand and power tools;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: playing and inspecting instruments to evaluate their sound quality and to locate any defects;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: adjusting string tensions to achieve proper tone or pitch of stringed instruments;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: adjusting lips, reeds, or toe hole of organ pipes, using hand tools, to regulate airflow and loudness of sound;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: tuning and servicing pipe organs by adjusting pitch of organ A pipes to conform with pitch of tuning fork and adjusting pitch of other pipes with references to  pitch of tuned pipes;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: installing new drumheads in percussion instruments;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: tuning accordions by aurally comparing pitch of reeds with master reeds and filing reeds to obtain standard pitch;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: aligning pads and keys on reed or wind instruments;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: tuning percussion instruments to required pitch by tightening or loosening cords holding leather pieces fixed atop or at both ends of instrument; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: assembling and installing new pipe organs and pianos in buildings.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Jewelry and precious metal workers design, fabricate, adjust, repair, or appraise jewelry, ceremonial or religious items, gold, silver, other precious metals, or gems. They cut, file, polish and set precious and semiprecious stones including gems and diamonds and engrave designs on jewelry and precious metal articles. They cut and polish diamonds for industrial purposes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: casting jewelry and other non-ferrous metal articles by hand;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: creating new jewelry designs and modifying existing designs, using computers as necessary;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: cutting designs in molds or other materials to be used as models in the fabrication of metal and jewelry products;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: altering existing jewelry mountings in order to reposition jewels or to adjust mountings;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: repairing, reshaping and restyling old jewelry or precious metal ware following designs or instructions;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: making complete jewelry articles such as rings, necklaces, bangles, brooches and bracelets from materials such as gold, silver, platinum, and precious or semiprecious stones;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: examining gem surfaces and internal structures, using polariscopes, refractometers, microscopes, and other optical instruments, to differentiate between stones, to identify rare specimens, or to detect flaws, defects, or peculiarities affecting gem values;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: cutting and polishing gems and setting them in jewelry articles;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: engraving or embossing letters, designs or decorative lines on jewelry and precious metal ware;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: grinding, drilling and finishing jewel bearings for use in precision instruments such as compasses and chronometers; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: examining assembled or finished products to ensure conformance to specifications, using magnifying glasses or precision measuring instruments.

examples.title: Jewelry caster, by hand and machine
Jewelry finishers, by hand and machine

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Potters and related workers prepare pottery, porcelain ware, sanitary ware, bricks, tiles and abrasive wheels by hand or by machine.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: making articles of pottery and porcelain;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making clay or plaster of Paris molds;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: reading technical drawings to know customer’s requirements;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: forming articles on potter's wheel by pressing thumbs into centers of revolving clay to form hollows, and press on the inside and outside of emerging clay cylinders with hands and fingers, gradually raising and shaping clay to desired forms and sizes;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: adjusting wheel speeds according to the feel of the clay as pieces enlarge and walls become thinner;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating jigger machines to form ceramic ware, such as bowls, cups, plates, and saucers;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: adjusting and setting controls of pug mill that mixes, extrudes, cuts, and deposits clay charges in or over molds as specified;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: smoothening surfaces of finished pieces, using rubber scrapers and wet sponges;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: forming abrasive wheels by molding and pressing an abrasive mixture by hand or by machine;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: examining finished ware for defects, verifying accuracy of shapes and sizes of objects, using calipers and templates; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: preparing work for sale or exhibition, and maintaining relationships with retail, pottery, art, and resource networks that can facilitate sale or exhibition of work.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: GLASS MAKERS, CUTTERS, GRINDERS AND FINISHERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Glass makers, cutters, grinders and finishers blow, mold, press, cut, trim, grind and polish glass, shape molten glass according to patterns.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: heating glass to pliable stage, using gas flames or ovens, and rotating glass to heat it uniformly;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: blowing and bending glass tubing into specified shapes to form scientific apparatus like flasks, retorts, pipettes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: grinding and polishing glass objects or parts to correct defects or to prepare surfaces for further finishing and smoothening and polishing rough edges, using belt sander or polishing wheels;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: examining glass stock and finished products and marking or discarding items with defects such as spots, stains, scars, snags, chips, scratches, or unacceptable shapes or finishes;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: reading work orders to determine dimensions, cutting locations, and quantities to cut;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: observing gauges, computer printouts and video monitors to verify specified processing conditions and make adjustments as necessary ;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: positioning pattern or drawing on glass, measuring dimensions, and marking cutting lines, using glass cutting tools and cutting glass along marked outlines or around pattern;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: setting up, operating and adjusting computerized or robotic glass cutting equipment;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: inspecting, weighing, and measuring products to verify conformance to specifications, using instruments such as micrometers, calipers, magnifiers, and rulers;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: regulating oven temperatures according to glass types to be processed;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: transferring pattern for individual stained glass parts from full size drawing to pattern paper, using stylus to trace drawings;

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: spraying silver solution on glass to provide mirrored surface, using spray gun; and

tasks.label: m
tasks.text: laying out cutting and grinding optical and other glass to specified dimensions and weight for molding into lens blanks and for use as watch crystals.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: SIGN WRITERS, DECORATIVE PAINTERS, ENGRAVERS AND ETCHERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Sign writers, decorative painters, engravers and etchers decorate articles made of wood, metal, textiles, glass, ceramics and other materials. They plan, lay out and paint letters, figures, monograms and designs to make signs and engrave and etch ornamental and floral designs on glass and other articles.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: painting decorative free-hand designs on objects, such as pottery, glass, cigarette cases, lampshades;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: transferring from paper transfers decorative or ornamental designs on articles;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: integrating and developing visual elements, such as line, space, mass, color, and perspective, in order to produce desired effects such as the illustration of ideas, emotions, or moods;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: laying out and painting  in one or more languages letters, figures, monograms and designs to make signs;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: sketching or tracing design or lettering onto work piece or pattern material to prepare pattern or stencil;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: designing pattern or lettering to paint work pieces, such as signs, glassware, pottery, or zinc plates;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: using software and routing equipment to produce 3D Carved images for application onto larger signage as well as engraved and inlaid signs;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: designing and producing normal flat cut lettering or lettering that is shadowed with applied vinyl or lettering that is ready cut for  application;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: writing, painting, or printing signs or show cards used for display or other purposes;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: cutting out letters and signs for display purposes from wallboard or cardboard, by hand or machines, such as electrically powered jigsaw or bandsaw;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: examining sketches, diagrams, samples, blueprints, or photographs to decide how designs are to be etched, cut, or engraved onto work pieces;

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: measuring and computing dimensions of lettering, designs, or patterns to be engraved;

tasks.label: m
tasks.text: engraving and printing patterns, ornamental designs, etchings, trademarks, figures or lettering onto flat or curved surfaces of a wide variety of metal, glass, plastic, or ceramic items; and

tasks.label: n
tasks.text: etching decorative designs, calibration markings and other figures on glass articles.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: HANDICRAFT WORKERS IN WOOD, BASKETRY AND RELATED MATERIALS

definition_paragraphs.text: Handicraft workers in wood and related materials apply traditional techniques like seasoning, impregnation to prepare wood, straw, rattan, reeds, clay, shells, and other materials, and carve, mold, assemble, weave, or paint and decorate various articles for personal or household use, or for decorative purposes. Basketry weavers, brush makers and related workers select and prepare materials like bristles, nylon, fiber, bass, whisker and wire to make wicker furniture, brushes and brooms and weave various kinds of baskets.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: preparing wood, straw, rattan, reeds, shells, or similar materials;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: carving floral and artistic designs on wooden surfaces for decorative purposes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: painting free hand decorative designs on glass and pottery or porcelain ware;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: carving, assembling, weaving, painting and decorating various articles for personal or household use such as salad bowls, serving-spoons, cutting-boards, trays, vases, jugs, baskets, straw hats, straw mats and similar objects;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: carving, assembling, weaving and painting various decorative articles such as statues and other sculptures, chess pieces, jewelry, and similar objects;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: making wicker furniture from peeled and softened rattan, reeds, rushes, willow branches and similar materials;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: making various kinds of baskets by interlacing osier, rattan, reeds, rushes or similar materials;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: forming bottom of basket by interlacing strips of rattan, wood veneer or other material with framework of rods of material such as willow;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: inserting rods around edge of bottom between woven sections of bottom and bending them upright to serve as framework for sides;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: selecting and preparing brush materials, such as bristles, nylon, fibers and wire, and setting them in brush base; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: selecting and preparing materials, such as broom corn, bass, whisker and fiber, and fastening them to broom handles;

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: HANDICRAFT WORKERS IN TEXTILE, LEATHER AND RELATED MATERIALS

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: spinning and dyeing with natural dyestuffs, wool, cotton and other fibers;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: lace-making and weaving, knitting, or embroidering various garments and articles for household use;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing and dyeing hides with natural dyestuffs and making traditional footwear or handbags, belts and other accessories;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: spinning and winding yarn by hand;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: drawing warp threads into loom by hand;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: weaving plain or figured cloth, tapestry, lace, carpet or other fabrics on hand looms;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: making carpets by using a knotting technique;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: knitting garments and other articles on hand-operated machine or by hand;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: crocheting or making braid by hand;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: making nets by hand;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: grading and classifying natural textile fibers;

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: washing wool fibers;

tasks.label: m
tasks.text: cleaning and fluffing textile fibers; and

tasks.label: n
tasks.text: forming fibers into sliver, combing them, combining sliver into sliver laps or forming sliver into rove.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: This unit group covers handicraft workers who perform traditional handicrafts not classified elsewhere. For instance, the group includes traditional handicraft workers in non-precious metals and stone.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Printing trades’ workers compose and set type prior to printing, set up and operate printing presses, bind and finish printed products, and prepare stencils and operate screen printing equipment.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: operating graphic cameras and other photographic equipment to reproduce camera-ready copy onto films, plates and digital output devices; operating computer screen-based equipment for scanning, color separation and correction, retouching and other processes used to transfer copy to film and produce film for plate, cylinder

and digital output productions; setting up, operating and monitoring machines used in typesetting, photographing copy, printing and cutting, folding, collating and binding printed material; performing routine finishing operations and machine maintenance; and preparing stencils and operating screen printing equipment.

definition_paragraphs.text: Pre-press technicians proof, format, set and compose text and graphics into a form suitable for use in various printing processes and representation in other visual media.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating graphic cameras and other photographic equipment to reproduce camera-ready copy onto films, plates and digital output devices;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: using computer applications to generate images, text, layouts and impositions for print and other visual media displays;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating plate making equipment to reproduce images from film to printing plates, digital output devices and presses;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating computer screen-based equipment for scanning, color separation, color correction, masking, creative design, combining, imposing, retouching, and other processes used to transfer copy to film and produce film for plate, digital output and cylinder productions;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: carrying out digital and chemical proofing from digital systems, and negative and positive films;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: evaluating printed proofs, checking and correcting them for quality; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: preparing and exposing carbon tissue for laying on cylinders by transfer method, and developing images.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Printers set up and operate digital, letterpress, lithographic, flexographic, gravure, newspaper and other printing presses.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting, adjusting and monitoring substrate-feed mechanisms, delivery mechanisms, inking systems and other printing machine functions;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: mixing ink and solvents to standard, and regulating paper and ink supply during print runs;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: monitoring, evaluating and determining press to check print quality standards against proofs and detect malfunctions;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: producing a variety of printed products using relief, lithographic, flexographic and gravure printing presses, and in-line finishing systems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: preparing plates, blankets and impression cylinders on small offset lithographic printing presses;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: loading paper into feeding mechanisms;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring machine operations and quality of printing;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: maintaining, adjusting, repairing and cleaning machines; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: producing digital print images, and transferring and outputting images.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Print finishing and binding workers bind books and other publications, and finish printed products by hand or machine.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting up and supervising the operation of automatic binding and finishing equipment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: binding full, half and limp-bound books, and repairing bindings;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: folding, collating and sewing signatures by machine and hand;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating paper guillotines for pre-press and post-press paper cutting and trimming, and programming electronically operated units;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating systems to insert printed material into newspapers, magazines and envelopes;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: embellishing printed products automatically and manually; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: operating photographic and electronic reproduction devices.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Electrical and electronics trades workers install, fit and maintain electrical wiring systems and  machinery and other electrical apparatus, electrical transmission and supply lines and cables, and electronic and telecommunications equipment and systems.

The work is carried out by hand and by hand-powered and other tools which  are used to reduce the amount of physical effort and time required for specific tasks, as well as to improve the quality of the products.  The  tasks call for an understanding of the work organization, the materials and  tools used, and the nature and purpose of the final product.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: installing, maintaining, fitting and adjusting electrical and electronic wiring systems, machinery and equipment; examining blueprints, wiring diagrams and specifications to determine sequences and methods of operation; inspecting and testing electrical and electronic systems, equipment, cables and machinery to identify hazards, defects, and the need for adjustment or repair; installing maintaining and repairing electrical and telecommunications transmission lines; joining electrical, telecommunications and data cables; and maintaining, troubleshooting, fitting, adjusting, testing and repairing electronic equipment such as commercial and office machines and electronic instruments and control systems, computers, telecommunications and data transmission equipment.

definition_paragraphs.text: Electrical equipment installers and repairers install, fit and maintain electrical wiring systems and related equipment, electrical machinery and other electrical apparatus and electrical transmission and supply lines and cables.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: installing, maintaining, fitting and adjusting electrical wiring systems, machinery and equipment; examining blueprints, wiring diagrams and specifications to determine sequences and methods of operation; inspecting and testing electrical systems, equipment, cables and machinery to identify hazards, defects, and the need for adjustment or repair; and installing maintaining and repairing electrical transmission lines; joining electrical cables.

definition_paragraphs.text: Building and related electricians install, maintain and repair electrical wiring systems and related equipment and fixtures.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: installing, maintaining and repairing electrical wiring systems and related equipment in various buildings such as schools, hospitals, commercial establishments, residential buildings and other structures;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: examining blueprints, wiring diagrams and specifications to determine sequences and methods of operation;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: planning layout and installation of electrical wiring, equipment and fixtures, based on job specifications and relevant standards;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: inspecting electrical systems, equipment, and components to identify hazards, defects, and the need for adjustment or repair;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: selecting, cutting and connecting wire and cable to terminals and connectors;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: measuring and laying out installation reference points;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: positioning and installing electrical switchboards; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: testing continuity of circuit.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Electrical mechanics and fitters fit, adjust, install and repair electrical machinery and other electrical apparatus and equipment in buildings, factories, workshops, or other places.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: fitting, adjusting and repairing various kinds of electrical machinery and motors, generators, switchgear and control apparatus, instruments, or electrical parts of elevators and related equipment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: fitting, adjusting and repairing electrical parts in domestic appliances, industrial machines and other appliances;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: inspecting and testing manufactured electrical products;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: installing, testing, connecting, commissioning, maintaining and modifying electrical equipment, wiring and control systems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: designing, installing, maintaining, servicing and repairing electric and hydraulic passenger and freight lifts, escalators, moving walkways and other lift equipment;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: connecting electrical systems to power supply; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: replacing and repairing defective parts.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Electrical line installers and repairers install, repair and join electrical transmission and supply cables and related equipment.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: installing and repairing overhead and underground electrical power and electrical traction lines;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making joints in overhead and underground cables;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: adhering to safety practices and procedures, such as checking equipment regularly and erecting barriers around work areas;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: opening switches or attaching grounding devices to remove electrical hazards from disturbed or fallen lines or to facilitate repairs;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: climbing poles or using truck-mounted buckets to access equipment; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: identifying defective sectionalizing devices, circuit breakers, fuses, voltage regulators, transformers, switches, relays, or wiring, using wiring diagrams and electrical-testing instruments.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Electric vehicle mechanics and repairers are responsible for inspections, maintenance and repair of electric vehicles.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: maintenance and repair, including troubleshooting of power line, as needed; and

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: diagnose, service and repair high voltage EVs and commercial charging stations.
