section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: ELECTRONICS AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS INSTALLERS AND REPAIRERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Electronics and telecommunications installers and repairers fit, maintain, adjust and repair electronic equipment such as commercial and office machines and electronic instruments and control systems and
install, repair and maintain telecommunications equipment, data transmission equipment, cables, antennae and repair, fit and maintain computers.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: examining and testing machines, equipment, instruments and control systems to diagnose faults; adjusting, repairing, and replacing worn and defective parts and wiring, and maintaining machines, equipment and instruments; installing electronic instruments and control systems; fitting and adjusting electronic equipment; maintaining, troubleshooting, fitting, adjusting, testing and repairing computers, data transmission equipment and computer peripherals; installing, maintaining, repairing, and diagnosing malfunctions of microwave, telemetry, multiplexing, satellite and other radio and electromagnetic wave communications systems; providing technical advice and information, and monitoring the performance of complex telecommunications networks and equipment; installing, joining and repairing cabling for computer, radio, telephone and television transmission; and installing, maintaining and repairing antennae used in communications.

definition_paragraphs.text: Electronics mechanics and servicers fit, maintain, adjust and repair electronic equipment such as commercial and office machines and electronic instruments and control systems.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: examining and testing machines, instruments, components, other equipment, instruments and control systems to identify faults;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: adjusting, repairing, and replacing worn and defective parts and wiring, and maintaining machines, equipment and instruments;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: reassembling, test operating and adjusting equipment;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: installing electronic instruments and control systems;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: coordinating work with that of engineers, technicians, and other maintenance personnel;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: interpreting test data to diagnose malfunctions and systemic performance problems;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: installing, adjusting, repairing or replacing electrical and electronic components, assemblies, and systems using hand tools, power tools, or soldering irons;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: connecting components to assemblies such as radio systems, instruments, magnetos, inverters, and in-flight refueling systems; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: keeping records of maintenance and repair work.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY INSTALLERS AND SERVICERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Information and communications technology (ICT) installers and servicers install, repair and maintain telecommunications equipment, data transmission equipment, cables, antennae and conduits and repair, fit and maintain computers.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: maintaining, troubleshooting, testing and repairing computers, data transmission equipment and computer peripherals;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: fitting and adjusting computer hardware;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: installing, maintaining, repairing, and diagnosing malfunctions of microwave, telemetry, multiplexing, satellite and other radio and electromagnetic wave communications systems;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: providing technical advice and information, and monitoring the performance of complex telecommunications networks and equipment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: installing and repairing cabling for computer, radio, telephone and television transmission;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: joining telecommunications and data cables and sealing sheathes; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: installing, maintaining and repairing antennae used in communications.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: FOOD PROCESSING, WOOD WORKING, GARMENT AND OTHER CRAFT AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Food processing, wood working, garment and other craft and related trades workers treat and process agricultural and  fisheries raw materials into food and other products, and produce and repair goods made of wood,  textiles, fur, leather, or other materials.

The work is carried out by hand and by hand-powered and other tools which  are used to reduce the amount of physical effort and time required for specific tasks, as well as to improve the quality of the products. The  tasks call for an understanding of the work organization, the materials and  tools used, and the nature and purpose of the final product.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include: treating and  processing meat, fish, grain, fruit, vegetables and related materials into  food stuffs, and tobacco into tobacco products; tasting and grading food  products and beverages; treating and processing natural fibers, skins and  hides; making and repairing furniture and other goods made of wood; preparing hides, skins and pelts for further use; and making and repairing textiles, garments, hats, shoes and related products. Supervision of other workers may  be included.

records.title: FOOD PROCESSING AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Food processing and related trades workers slaughter animals, treat and prepare them and related food items for human and animal consumptions, make various kinds of bread, cakes and other flour products, process and preserve fruit, vegetables and related foods, taste and grade various food products and beverages, or prepare tobacco and make tobacco products.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: slaughtering animals; treating meat and fish and preparing them and related food items; making various kinds of bread, cakes and other flour products; processing and preserving fruit, vegetables and related foods; tasting and grading various food products and beverages; and preparing tobacco and making tobacco products. Supervision of workers may be included.

records.title: BUTCHERS, FISHMONGERS AND RELATED FOOD PREPARERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Butchers, fishmongers and related food preparers slaughter animals, clean, cut and dress meat and fish, remove bones and prepare related food items or preserve meat, fish and other foods and food products by drying, salting or smoking.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: slaughtering animals;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: flaying and trimming carcasses;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: boning, cutting and dressing meat and fish for sale or further processing;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing ingredients and making sausages and similar products using chopping, mixing and shaping machines;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: curing meat, fish and other foods;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating smokehouses or ovens to smoke meat, fish and other foodstuffs;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: cooking or in other ways preparing meat, fish and related food items for sale ;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: selling meat or fish to customers, including wrapping, weighing and labelling products, and receiving payment.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Bakers, pastry-cooks and confectionery makers make various kinds of bread, cakes, and other flour products, as well as handmade chocolate and sugar confectionery.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: making bread, cakes, biscuits, pastries, pies and other flour products;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making handmade confectionery from mixtures of sugar, chocolate and other ingredients using hand tools and some machines;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: combining measured ingredients in bowls of mixing, blending, or cooking machinery;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: checking the quality of raw materials to ensure that standards and specifications are met;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: applying glazes, icings, or other toppings to baked goods, using spatulas or brushes;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: checking the cleanliness of equipment and operation of premises before production runs to ensure compliance with occupational health and safety regulations;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring oven temperatures and product appearance to determine baking times; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: coordinating the forming, loading, baking, unloading, de-panning and cooling of batches of  bread, rolls, pastry and confectionary products.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Dairy products makers process butter and various types of cheese, cream or other dairy products.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: boiling or pasteurizing milk to achieve specified butter fat content;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: separating cream from milk and churning cream into butter;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: dumping measured amounts of starter and other ingredients into milk;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: curdling milk, heating curd until it reaches desired firmness, draining curd and placing cheese into molds to press it into shape;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: salting cheese and piercing or smearing cheese with cultured wash to develop mold growth;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: placing and turning cheese blocks on shelves to cure cheese;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring product quality before packaging by inspecting, taking samples and adjusting treatment conditions when necessary; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: recording amounts of ingredients used, test results, and time cycles.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Fruit, vegetable and related preservers process or preserve fruit, nuts and related foods in various ways including cooking, drying, salting, or juice or oil extraction.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: extracting juices from various fruits;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: extracting oils from oil-bearing seeds, nuts or fruits;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: cooking, salting or drying fruit, vegetables and related foods;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: mixing and adding ingredients such as pectin, sugar, spices and vinegar to assist preservation and enhance texture, appearance and flavor; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: transferring preserved foods to sterile jars, bottles or other containers.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: FOOD AND BEVERAGE TASTERS AND GRADERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Food and beverage tasters and graders inspect, taste and grade various types of agricultural products, food and beverages.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: inspecting, testing, tasting and smelling agricultural products, food and beverages at various stages of processing;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: determining quality, acceptability to consumer tastes and approximate value of products and grading them into appropriate classes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: discarding inferior products;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: recording the grade and/or identification numbers on tags, receiving, or sales sheets; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: weighing and measuring products.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: TOBACCO PREPARERS AND TOBACCO PRODUCTS MAKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Tobacco preparers and tobacco products makers prepare tobacco leaves and make various tobacco products.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: grading cured tobacco leaves by type, quality and locality where grown;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: mixing tobacco leaves according to formula to obtain a blend of distinct flavor;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: tending vacuum container which moistens tobacco for further processing;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: removing midribs and stalks from tobacco leaves and shredding tobacco; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: making cigars, cigarettes, snuff and other tobacco products by hand or with simple machines.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: WOOD TREATERS, CABINET-MAKERS AND RELATED TRADES WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Wood treaters, cabinet-makers and related trades workers preserve and treat wood; produce waferboards, particleboards, hardboards, insulation boards, plywood, veneers and similar wood products; and make, decorate and repair wooden furniture, vehicles and other wooden products. They use specialized hand
tools and set-up, operate and tend wood processing and woodworking equipment, machines and machine tools.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: operating and tending treating and other equipment to dry lumber and other wood products, and to treat chemically and impregnate wood products with preservatives; operating woodworking machines to cut, shape and form parts and components; studying plans, verifying dimensions of articles to be made, fitting parts together to form complete units and checking the quality and fit of pieces to ensure adherence to specifications; setting and adjusting various kinds of machines for operation by others; setting-up, programming, operating and monitoring several types of woodworking machines to fabricate, repair or refinish wooden parts for furniture, fixtures and other wood products; and reading and interpreting specifications or following verbal instructions.

definition_paragraphs.text: Wood treaters operate and tend wood treatment processing equipment and machines to remove bark from logs, produce wood chips, season, preserve and treat wood, and produce waferboards, particleboards, hardboards, insulation boards, plywood, veneers and similar wood products.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and tending kilns, treating tanks and other equipment to dry lumber, prepare and season wood and other wood products, and to treat chemically and impregnate wood products with preservatives;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: monitoring equipment operation, gauges, and panel lights in order to detect deviations from standards and to ensure that processes are operating according to specifications;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: assisting in maintaining processing equipment and machines as required;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: cleaning, lubricating and adjusting equipment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: transporting materials and products to and from work areas, manually or using carts, handtrucks, or hoists; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: completing and maintaining production reports.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Cabinet-makers and related workers make, decorate and repair wooden furniture, carts and other vehicles, wheels, parts, fittings, patterns, models and other wooden products using woodworking machines, machine tools and specialized hand tools.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating woodworking machines, such as power saws, jointers, mortisers and shapers, and using hand tools to cut, shape and form parts and components;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: studying plans, verifying dimensions of articles to be made, or preparing specifications and checking the quality and fit of pieces in order to ensure adherence to specifications;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: trimming joints and fitting parts and subassemblies together to form complete units using glue and clamps, and reinforcing joints using nails, screws or other fasteners;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: making, restyling and repairing various wooden articles, such as cabinets, furniture, vehicles, scale models, sports equipment and other parts or products;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: decorating furniture and fixtures by inlaying wood, applying veneer and carving designs; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: finishing surfaces of wooden articles or furniture.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: WOODWORKING MACHINE TOOL SETTERS AND OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Woodworking machine tool setters and operators set-up or operate and monitor automatic or semi-automatic woodworking machines, such as precision sawing, shaping, planning, boring, turning and woodcarving machines to fabricate or repair wooden parts for furniture, fixtures and other wooden products.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting-up, programming, operating and monitoring several types of woodworking machines for sawing, shaping, boring, drilling, planing, pressing, turning, sanding or carving to fabricate or repair wooden parts for furniture, fixtures and other wooden products;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating preset special-purpose woodworking machines to fabricate wooden products such as coat hangers, mop handles, clothes pins and other products;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: selecting knives, saws, blades, cutter heads, cams, bits, or belts according to workpiece, machine functions and product specifications;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: installing and adjusting blades, cutter heads, boring-bits and sanding-belts, and using hand tools and rules;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: setting and adjusting various kinds of woodworking machines for operation by others; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: reading and interpreting specifications or following verbal instructions.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Garment and related trades workers fit, alter and repair tailored clothing; design, and make textile and fur garments, leather or fur products; repair, renovate and decorate garments, gloves and other products of textile; create patterns for garments; install, repair and replace upholstery of furniture, fixtures, orthopedic appliances and furnishings of automobiles; trim, scrape, tan, buff and dye animal hides, pelts or skins; modify and repair footwear and leather articles.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: fitting, altering, repairing tailored clothing; designing and making made-to-measure clothing, from textile fabrics, light leather and other material, or make hats or wigs; make garment style changes; creating precision master patterns for production of garments, other textile, and leather or fur products; sewing together, joining, darning, repairing, renovating and  decorating garments, gloves and other products of textile, fur, light leather and other materials and fabricating and assembling sails, awnings and tarpaulins; installing, repairing and replacing upholstery of furniture, fixtures, orthopedic appliances; seats, panels, and other furnishings of automobiles, railway coaches, aircraft, ships and similar items; trimming, scraping, cleaning, tanning, buffing and dying animal hides, pelts or skins to produce leather stock and finished furs for making garments and other products; and making, modifying and repairing standard, custom or orthopedic footwear and natural or synthetic leather articles.

definition_paragraphs.text: Tailors, dressmakers, furriers and hatters fabricate, fit, alter and repair tailored or hand-made clothing; They produce made-to-measure clothing  such as suits, overcoats, and dresses from textile fabrics, light leather, fur and other material, or make hats or wigs according to customer’s and clothing manufacturer’s specifications.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: making overcoats, suits, skirts, shirts, blouses, lingerie, corsetry, hats, wigs and similar garments often to clients' individual requirements;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: selecting textile fabrics, leather or fur pelts matching the desired size, color, texture, and quality of the garment; cutting to shape them to garment pattern and arranging them on pattern according to the design of  the garment;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: making garment style changes, such as tapering trouser legs, narrowing lapels, and adding or removing padding;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: selecting and modifying commercial patterns to customers' and clothing manufacturers' specifications and fit;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: fitting, altering and repairing tailored clothing, dresses, coats and other made-to-measure garments according to customers' requests;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: making and caring for costumes used in theatrical, television and motion picture productions;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: folding, twisting, and draping material, such as satin or silk, or sewing ribbon or cloth in the form of artificial flowers or bows around crown and brim to shape and decorate hats;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: sewing, and fastening together materials and hair strands to make wigs;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: blending shades of hair to give natural appearance to wigs and arranging woven hair in specified position and sewing hair together to form hairpiece;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: making, altering, restyling and repairing fur garments and other fur articles; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: reclaiming furs or skins from old coats, gluing fabric to interior of fur coats and trimming  fur garments.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: GARMENT AND RELATED PATTERNMAKERS AND CUTTERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Textile, leather and related patternmakers and cutters create precision master patterns for production of garments, other textile, and leather or fur products. They mark, cut, shape and trim textile, light leather and other materials according to blueprints or specifications in the manufacture of garments, hats and caps, gloves and miscellaneous products.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: creating a master pattern for each size within a range of garment sizes, using charts, drafting instruments, computers, and/or grading devices;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: creating the “blueprint” or pattern pieces for a particular apparel design with the aid of a computer;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: calculating dimensions of patterns according to sizes, considering stretching of material;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: drawing details on outlined parts to indicate where parts are to be joined, as well as the positions of pleats, pockets, buttonholes on garments, decorative stitching on shoe parts or eyelets on canvas products using computers or drafting instruments;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: positioning templates or measuring materials to locate specified points of cuts or to obtain maximum yields and mark fabric accordingly;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: laying out master pattern on fabric and cutting sample pattern;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: testing patterns by making and fitting sample garments;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: placing patterns on top of layers of fabric and cutting fabric following patterns, using electric or manual knives, cutters or computer numerically controlled cutting devices;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: cutting fabric or fur pelts to make parts for garments and other fur articles;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: trimming excess material or cutting threads off finished products, such as cutting loose ends of a finished product;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: positioning leather on cutting bed of machine, maximizing usage according to skin grain, skin flaws and skin stretch; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: performing pattern-making, marking and cutting tasks in the manufacture of other products such as soft furnishings and canvas goods.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Sewing, embroidery and related workers sew together, repair, renovate and decorate garments, gloves and other products of textile, fur, light leather and other materials and fabricate tents sails, awnings and tarpaulins. They work mainly by hand using a needle and thread but may perform some tasks using a sewing machine.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: repairing defective or damaged portion of cloth or garment by hand, using matching thread and needle;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: removing stitches from garments to be altered, using rippers or razor blades;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: selecting thread according to specifications or color of parts or dying thread to match color and shade of cloth to be darned;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: patching holes, sewing tears and ripped seams, or darning defects in items, using needles and thread;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: pulling knots to the wrong sides of garments, using hooks;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: trimming ends with scissors to make mended portion look uniform with pattern of cloth;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: sewing ornamental designs by hand over stamped, printed or stenciled patterns on fabric using needle and colored thread;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: embroidering ornamental designs on cloth by hand or machine using needle and colored threads;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: softening leather or shoe material with water to prepare it for sewing;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: sewing or gluing decorative trimmings to articles, such as hats, caps, or millinery;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: hand sewing umbrella covers to frames, tacking cover to ribs along seams and sewing corners to tip of rib and sewing ties to outside of cover to hold umbrella when folded; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: fabricating and assembling thick cloth, canvas and like materials into sails, awning, tarpaulins and tents.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Upholsterers and related workers install, repair and replace upholstery of furniture, fixtures, orthopedic appliances; seats, panels, convertible and vinyl tops and other furnishings of automobiles, railway coaches, aircraft, ships and similar items with fabric, leather, rexine or other upholstery material. They also make and repair cushions, quilts and mattresses.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: discussing upholstery fabric, color, and style with customers and providing cost estimate for upholstering furniture or other items;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making upholstery patterns from sketches, customer descriptions or blueprints;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: laying out, measuring and cutting upholstery materials following patterns, templates, sketches, or design specifications;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: installing, arranging and securing springs, padding and covering material to furniture frames;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: sewing upholstery materials by hand to seam cushions and joining sections of covering materials;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: sewing rips or tears in material, or creating tufting, using needle and thread;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: tacking, gluing or sewing ornamental trims, buckles, braids, buttons and other accessories to covers or frames on upholstered items;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: laying out, cutting, fabricating and installing upholstery in aircrafts, motor vehicles, railway cars, boats and ships;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: repairing raw hide covering of artificial limbs;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: renovating antique furniture using a variety of tools including ripping chisels, magnetic hammers and long needles;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: collaborating with interior designers to decorate rooms and coordinate furnishing fabrics; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: making quilts, cushions and mattresses.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Pelt dressers, tanners and fellmongers trim, scrape, clean, tan, buff and dye animal hides, pelts or skins to produce leather stock and finished furs for making garments and other products.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: sorting and grading pelts, hides and skins according to color, shading, size and density;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: scraping particles of flesh, fat, or protective tissue from skins or pelts to clean and soften them;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: removing  hair from skin or hides soaked in lime water;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing hides by curing them with salt;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: removing long, coarse hair from pelts and trimming underlying hair to even length;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: tanning and dressing pelts to improve luster and beauty or restore natural appearance of pelts;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: preparing bark and myrobalan liquor  for treating hides or skins;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: treating hides and skins in tanning solution to convert them into leather;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: tinting or dyeing furs to enhance natural shades of fur;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: removing wrinkles and setting grains on wet hide or skin;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: dressing and applying dyes and stains to leather;

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: stretching and smoothing dressed pelts; and

tasks.label: m
tasks.text: seasoning leather by applying chemical solution or oil evenly on surface by hand brush and allowing it to dry in open air.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Shoemakers and related workers make, modify and repair standard, custom or orthopedic footwear and natural or synthetic leather articles, such as luggage, handbags and belts, (except for leather garments, hats and gloves), or participate in the manufacture of shoes and related goods. They decorate, reinforce or finish shoes, luggage, handbags and belts.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: making, modifying and repairing standard footwear to meet individual requirements;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: making, modifying and repairing orthopedic or therapeutic footwear according to doctors' prescriptions, or modifying existing footwear for people with foot problems and special needs;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: repairing belts, luggage, purses and similar products;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: taking plaster casts of deformed legs or foot to prepare drawings;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: preparing inserts, heel pads, and lifts from casts of customers' feet;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: studying drawings and other specifications to make footwear according to customer’s needs;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: studying work orders and/or shoe part tags to obtain information about workloads, specifications, and the types of materials to be used;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: checking the texture, color, and strength of leather to ensure that it is adequate for a particular purpose;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: cutting out, shaping and padding parts for making leather articles;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: sewing rips or patching holes to repair articles, such as purses, belts, shoes, and luggage;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: removing and examining shoes, shoe parts, and designs to verify conformance to specifications such as proper embedding of stitches in channels;

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: attaching accessories or ornamentation to decorate or protect products; and

tasks.label: m
tasks.text: making and repairing articles such as saddles and harnesses for animals, luggage, handbags, brief-cases, leather bags, belts and other accessories.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Other craft and related workers work under the surface of water, using underwater breathing apparatus; position, assemble, and detonate explosives; inspect and  test,  raw materials, manufactured components and products; remove unwanted organisms to prevent damage to crops and buildings and other structures. This group includes other trade and craft occupations not classified elsewhere in major group 7, Craft and related trades workers.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: ensuring safety precautions; performing various underwater tasks, loading explosives into blast holes; mixing chemicals according to instructions; and operating and monitoring equipment for spraying pests and weeds.

definition_paragraphs.text: Underwater divers work under the surface of water, using underwater breathing apparatus to inspect, install, repair, and remove equipment and structures, conduct tests or experiments, rig explosives, photograph structures or marine life or find and recover missing items and persons.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: taking safety precautions, such as monitoring dive lengths and depths, and registering with authorities before diving expeditions begin;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: checking and maintaining diving equipment such as helmets, masks, air tanks, diving suits, harnesses and gauges;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: descending into water with the aid of diver helpers, using scuba gear or diving suits;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: working under water to lay and repair bridges, piers and harbor-wall foundations;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: inspecting for suspected damage and making minor repairs to ships' hulls and underwater installations;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: reporting on condition of wrecked ships;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: removing underwater obstructions;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: drilling holes for underwater blasting;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: performing various underwater tasks connected with salvage work or recovering dead bodies;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: gathering of shellfish, sponges, and other aquatic life forms for research purposes;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: communicating with workers on the surface while underwater, using signal lines or telephones;

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: obtaining information about diving tasks and environmental conditions.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Shot firers and blasters, position, assemble, and detonate explosives at mining, quarrying and demolition sites.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: ensuring workplace safety and explosives handling, storage and transport procedures and regulations are followed;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: planning and giving instructions for the lay out, depth and diameter of blast holes;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: checking depth and cleanliness of blast holes;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: determining quantity and type of explosives to be used;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: loading explosives into blast holes;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: assembling, or directing other workers to assemble, primer charges using detonators and explosive cartridges, and attaching electrical wires, fuses and detonating cords to primers;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: connecting wires, fuses and detonator cords into series, testing electrical circuits and repairing malfunctions, and connecting series to blasting machines;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: covering charges, filling blast holes with rock dust, sand and other materials, and tamping material to compact charges;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: ensuring all explosives are detonated, and reporting and attending to misfires;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: declaring blast areas safe before and after detonation of explosives; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: compiling and maintaining records about usage of explosives in compliance with laws and regulations.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: PRODUCT GRADERS AND TESTERS (EXCEPT FOODS AND BEVERAGES)

definition_paragraphs.text: Product graders and testers (except foods and beverages) inspect , test, sort, sample, and weigh raw materials, manufactured components and non-comestible goods produced or sold, to ensure compliance with quality standards and to identify defects, wear, and deviations from specifications, and to grade and classify them according to their quality.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: inspecting and testing products, parts and materials for conformity with specifications and standards;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: grading and classifying natural textile fibers for spinning and winding;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: discarding or rejecting products, materials, and equipment not meeting specifications;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: analyzing and interpreting blueprints, data, manuals, and other materials to determine specifications, inspection and testing procedures;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: notifying supervisors and other personnel of production problems, and assisting in identifying and correcting these problems;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: recording inspection or test data, such as weights, temperatures, grades, or moisture content, and quantities inspected or graded;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: marking items with details such as grade and acceptance or rejection status;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: measuring dimensions of products using instruments such as rulers, calipers, gauges, or micrometers; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: analyzing test data and making computations as necessary to determine test results.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: FUMIGATORS AND OTHER PEST AND WEED CONTROLLERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Fumigators and other pest and weed controllers use chemicals to remove harmful insects, small animals, wild plants and other unwanted organisms to prevent damage to crops and to buildings and other structures and their surroundings and to prevent health risks.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring equipment for spraying pests and weeds;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: mixing chemicals according to instructions;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: covering areas to specified depths with pesticides, applying knowledge of weather conditions, droplet sizes, elevation-to-distance ratios, and obstructions;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: spraying or releasing chemical solutions or toxic gases and setting traps to kill pests and vermin, such as mice, termites, and roaches;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: lifting, pushing, and swinging nozzles, hoses, and tubes in order to direct spray over designated areas;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: filling sprayer tanks with water and chemicals; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: cleaning and servicing machinery to ensure operating efficiency.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: CRAFT AND RELATED WORKERS NOT ELSEWHERE CLASSIFIED

definition_paragraphs.text: This group covers craft and trade occupations not classified elsewhere in major group 7, Craft and related trades workers. For instance, the group includes those who mold, slice, grind and polish optical lenses.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: heating, molding and pressing optical glass to make lens blanks; and

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: grinding and polishing lens blanks.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: PLANT AND MACHINE OPERATORS, AND ASSEMBLERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Plant and machine operators, and assemblers operate and monitor industrial  and agricultural machinery and equipment on the spot or by remote control,  drive and operate trains, motor vehicles and mobile machinery and equipment,  or assemble products from component parts according to strict specifications and procedures.

The work mainly calls for experience with and an understanding of  industrial and agricultural machinery and equipment as well as an ability to  cope with machine-paced operations and to adapt to technological innovations. Most occupations in this major group require skills at the second ISCO skill  level. Tasks performed by plant and machine operators and assemblers usually  include: operating and monitoring mining or other industrial machinery and  equipment for processing metal, minerals, glass, ceramics, wood, paper, or  chemicals; operating and monitoring machinery and equipment used to produce articles made of metal,  minerals, chemicals, rubber, plastics, wood, paper, textiles, fur, or leather,  and which process foodstuffs  and related products; driving and operating trains and motor vehicles;  driving, operating and monitoring mobile industrial and agricultural machinery  and equipment; assembling products from component parts according to strict  specifications and procedures. Supervision of other workers may be included.

Stationary plant and machine operators operate and monitor, on the spot  or by remote control, industrial plant and machinery and equipment that are stationary, or for which mobility is not an integral part of operation. The work mainly calls for experience with and an understanding of the  industrial plant, machinery or equipment being operated and monitored.  Ability to cope with  machine-paced operations and to adapt to innovations in machinery and  equipment is often required.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed by workers in this sub-major group usually include: setting up, operating and monitoring a  variety stationary plant and machinery; detecting malfunctions and taking corrective action; examining outputs  for defects and conformity to specifications and adjusting machine settings accordingly; performing maintenance, repairs and cleaning; recording data and maintaining production records. Supervision of other  workers may be included.

records.title: MINING AND MINERAL PROCESSING PLANT OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Mining and mineral processing plant operators operate and monitor plant and machinery which extract rock  and minerals from the earth, process minerals and stone, drill wells and bores, and manufacture and finish cement  and stone products.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: setting up, operating and monitoring a variety of mining and mineral  processing plant and machinery such as drilling rigs and auxiliary machines and equipment, continuous mining  machinery, and cutting, crushing, grinding, pumping and mixing plant and machinery; operating washing,  separating, extracting and combining equipment to remove waste and recover minerals; operating plant and  machinery to make cement, concrete, artificial stone, and precast concrete and stone products; monitoring the  performance of a variety of plant and machinery, detecting malfunctions and taking corrective action; performing plant and machinery maintenance, repairs and cleaning; and maintaining production records.

definition_paragraphs.text: Miners and quarriers operate plant, machinery and hand tools to extract rock, minerals and non-metallic deposits  from underground and surface mines and quarries.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: positioning, operating and monitoring the performance of a variety of underground and surface mining  equipment including continuous mining, cutting and channeling plant;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: setting up and operating drilling equipment in underground and surface mines and quarries;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating machinery and using tools to remove loosened rock, ore, coal and other deposits;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing, fitting and installing supports in underground workings including rock bolts;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating machinery to open new shafts, drives, air vents and rises;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating auxiliary plant such as pumps to expel air, water and mud;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: performing minor maintenance and repairs and lubricating and cleaning plant, machines and tools;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: completing records detailing operations completed during shifts; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: collecting mineral samples for laboratory analysis.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: MINERAL AND STONE PROCESSING PLANT OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Mineral and stone processing plant operators operate and monitor machinery and equipment for processing  rocks, minerals and stone to recover refined products for immediate use or further processing.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting up and operating stationary plant and machinery which grind, crush, cut, saw and slice rocks,  minerals and stones according to the specifications for the job;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: positioning blocks and slabs of stone onto machines for sawing, cutting and further working;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: monitoring and maintaining the flow of unprocessed rocks, minerals and stones from conveyors into  machines;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating washing, separating, leaching, precipitating, filtering, extracting and combining equipment to  remove waste material and recover minerals;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: combining mineral ores with solvents to facilitate further processing;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: separating metal and mineral concentrates from ore and alluvial deposits by thickening, flotation, gravity  separation, filtration, and or magnetic and electrostatic separation;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: observing meters, gauges and control panels, and adjusting valves and controls to ensure the safe and  efficient operation of equipment, and detecting malfunctions, and assisting with plant and machinery  maintenance and repair;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: examining processed materials visually or with hands to ensure compliance with established standards and  job specifications, and may collect samples for testing in laboratories;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: recording information about processing completed during shifts, such as quantities, types and dimensions of  materials produced; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: sorting, stacking and moving processed minerals and stone for packaging, further processing or shipping.

Stone cutting or processing machine operator

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: WELL DRILLERS AND BORERS AND RELATED WORKERS

definition_paragraphs.text: Well drillers and borers and related workers position, assemble and operate drilling machinery and related equipment to sink wells, extract ore, liquids and gases or for a variety of other purposes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: dismantling, moving and assembling drilling rigs and auxiliary equipment;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: assembling and dismantling pipes, casings and drill heads, and replacing dysfunctional equipment;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating controls to lower and raise drill pipes and casings in and out of wells, regulate pressure in the well and control the speed of tools;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: preparing drilling fluid and checking the operation of pumps to ensure adequate circulation of fluid in drill pipe and well;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: monitoring gauges and other indicators and listening to equipment to detect malfunctions and unusual well conditions, and determining the need to change drilling or equipment;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: maintaining, adjusting, repairing and cleaning drilling rigs, hoisting and other machinery;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: maintaining records of drilling and servicing operations;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: operating machines and tools to extract dust, cuttings and lost and broken drilling equipment from holes and wells;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: closing and sealing wells no longer in use; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: may supervise and train crew members.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: CEMENT, STONE AND OTHER MINERAL PRODUCTS MACHINE OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Cement, stone and other mineral products machine operators operate and monitor machines for manufacturing  and finishing precast concrete, bitumen, and stone products, and making cast stone for building purposes.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating extrusion, molding, mixing, pumping, compacting, grinding and cutting machinery to manufacture and finish precast concrete and stone products;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating plant to produce cement, lime and clinker, including loading and unloading ingredients and  operating continuous feed equipment such as pumps and conveyors;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating plant and machines which weigh and mix sand, gravel, cement, water and other ingredients to  make concrete;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating plant and machinery which assembles and fills molds with concrete and artificial stone mixtures,  removes castings from molds and finishes surfaces of precast products;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: cutting, grinding, drilling, sandblasting and polishing concrete products and stone blocks, slabs and products  to the specifications for the job;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: checking production plans and specifications to determine and select materials, ingredients, procedures,  components, settings and adjustments for extrusion, molding, mixing and compacting machines;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring plant and machines during operation by observing instruments such as temperature and pressure  gauges, and adjusting controls and reporting malfunctions as necessary;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: collecting and examining samples of mixtures and finished products for conformity to specifications and  adjusting machine settings accordingly;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: checking and maintaining production records, including information about quantities, dimensions and types  of materials and goods produced; and

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: arranging and assisting with plant and machinery maintenance and repair.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: METAL PROCESSING AND FINISHING PLANT OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Metal processing and finishing plant operators, operate and monitor single function process control machinery and equipment to control the conversion, processing and finishing of mineral ores and metals.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: setting up, preparing and adjusting metal and ore processing and finishing  machinery; coordinating and monitoring the operation of a particular aspect of metal processing production and  finishing; verifying equipment for malfunctions, monitoring gauges, carrying out routine operating tests and  arranging for maintenance; checking, testing and analyzing sample products; recording data and writing  production logs.

definition_paragraphs.text: Metal processing plant operators, operate, monitor, adjust and maintain, single process machinery and  equipment to process and convert mineral ores and refine, harden, roll and extrude metals.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting up, preparing and adjusting mineral ore and metal processing machinery to carry out one step in the  overall mineral ore or metal processing operation;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating single-function machinery to grind, separate, filter, mix, treat, cast, roll, refine or otherwise  process metals and mineral ores;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: observing gauges, meters, computer printouts, video monitors and products to ensure correct operation of  machine and verify specified processing conditions;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: adjusting equipment, valves, pumps, controls and process equipment;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: controlling the preparation, measuring and feeding of raw materials and processing agents into plant;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: controlling process start-up and shut-down, troubleshooting and monitoring outside process equipment;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: verifying equipment for malfunctions, carrying out routine operating tests and arranging for maintenance; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: analyzing sample products, performing tests, recording data and writing production logs.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: METAL FINISHING, PLATING AND COATING MACHINE OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Metal finishing-, plating and coating-machine operators operate and monitor equipment which finishes, plates  and coats metal articles or parts, in order to give them improved resistance to corrosion and abrasion, for  decorative purposes, or to impart electrical or magnetic properties.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring equipment which cleans metal articles in preparation for electroplating,  galvanizing, enameling or similar processes;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and monitoring electroplating equipment;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating and monitoring hot-dip equipment used to coat iron and steel products;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which automatically coat wire with non ferrous metal;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating and monitoring equipment used to spray molten metal or other substances on metal products to  provide a protective or decorative coating or to build up worn or damaged surfaces;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating and monitoring equipment used to impart a rust-resistant finish to metal articles by treating them  with chemicals and heating them;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: checking proper thickness of plating using micrometers, calipers or other devices recording data and writing  production logs; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: preparing and mixing metalizing solutions according to formulas or specifications.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: CHEMICAL AND PHOTOGRAPHIC PRODUCTS PLANT AND MACHINE  OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Chemical and photographic products plant and machine operators operate and monitor machines which process  a variety of chemicals and other ingredients to produce pharmaceuticals, toiletries, explosives and photographic  or other chemical products.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: operating and monitoring machines and equipment which blend, mix, package  and otherwise process chemicals and chemical products to give them the desired properties for further industrial  production, or to make finished products. Supervision of other workers may be included.

records.title: CHEMICAL PRODUCTS PLANT AND MACHINE OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Chemical products plant and machine operators monitor and operate units and machinery to blend, mix, process  and package a wide range of chemical products.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting up, starting, controlling, adjusting and stopping machines and plant;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: monitoring reaction processes and transfers of products in conformance with safety procedures;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: monitoring meters, gauges and electronic instrumentation on one or more chemical or formulation units, such  as mixers, kettles, blenders, dryers, tableting, encapsulation, granulation and coating machines;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: measuring, weighing and loading chemical ingredients following formulation cards;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: taking samples and performing routine chemical and physical tests of products and recording production  data; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: cleaning and performing minor repairs to machines and plant.

Pharmaceutical and toiletry products machine operators

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Photographic products machine operators operate and monitor equipment which makes photographic film and  paper, and which processes exposed photographic film and makes prints.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring equipment which makes photographic film and paper;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating, monitoring and testing photographic processing and printing equipment, and maintaining  operational standards;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: preparing exposed film for different processing batches in dark rooms and dark chambers;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: inspecting images, films, prints and adjusting settings on print-making equipment to produce required  color, brightness, contrast, number, size and type of prints;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: adjusting settings and running automatic developing equipment;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating equipment to transfer film to video tape or other electronic media;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: performing photographic processing related tasks; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: operating automatic equipment (in retail establishments) to develop color negatives, prints and slides;

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: RUBBER, PLASTIC AND PAPER PRODUCTS MACHINE OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Rubber, plastic and paper products machine operators operate and monitor machines which knead and blend rubber and rubber compounds, and  plastics or produce different paper products from paper, paperboard, cardboard and similar materials.

task_summary_paragraphs.text: Tasks performed usually include: operating and monitoring machines which knead and blend rubber and rubber  compounds, and produce various components and products from natural and synthetic rubber and plastics; operating and monitoring machines which produce various paper products; examining outputs for defects and  conformity to specifications and adjusting machine settings accordingly.

definition_paragraphs.text: Rubber-products machine operators operate and monitor machines which knead and blend rubber and rubber  compounds, and produce various components and products from natural and synthetic rubber, such as molded  footwear, domestic articles, insulating materials, industrial accessories, or tires.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which knead, mix and blend rubber and rubber compounds for further  processing;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which produce sheets of rubber or rubberized fabric by a rolling process;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which extrude compounded rubber or shape vulcanized rubber by  molding;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which build up tires on a form, vulcanize tires and mold or rebuild used tires;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: examining outputs for defects and conformity to specifications; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: locating defects and repairing worn and faulty tires by vulcanizing or other processes.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Products machine operators operate and monitor machines which knead and blend compounds to obtain plastic  materials and which make various plastic components and articles.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which knead and blend compounds to obtain plastic materials;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which shape plastic materials by molding, extrusion, blowing, cutting  and other means;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which laminate plastics and plastic impregnated materials or produce  fiberglass;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: encasing uncoated wire, cord, cable and optic fiber in plastic;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: examining outputs for defects and conformity to specifications;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: recycling waste plastic materials; and

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: making artificial eyes and contact lens discs, making and repairing spectacle frames and plastic parts of  orthopedic appliances.

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

definition_paragraphs.text: Paper products machine operators operate and monitor machines which produce boxes, envelopes, bags and  other goods from paper, paperboard, cardboard and similar materials.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which glue paper to cardboard, cut it to the required length or cut and  crease cardboard or paperboard to form box blanks;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and monitoring pressing machines which form drinking cups or other containers from paper,  paperboard or cardboard; and

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which cut, fold and glue paper to make envelopes and paper bags, or  which form bags from other similar materials.

examples.title: Envelope and paper bag production machine operator

section_markers.text: Examples of the occupations classified here:

records.title: TEXTILE, FUR AND LEATHER PRODUCTS MACHINE OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Textile, fur and leather products machine operators operate and monitor various types of machines which  prepare, process and treat  fibers, yarn, thread, leather, fur; produce, modify and repair footwear, garments and  manufacture or dry clean textiles or fur and light leather articles.

Tasks include operating and monitoring weaving and knitting machines which process yarn or thread into  woven, non-woven and knitted products; operating and monitoring machines which prepare fibers, and spin,  double, twist and wind yarn and thread from natural textile fibers; operating and monitoring sewing machines to  make, repair, darn and renovate textile, fur, synthetic or leather garments or embroider ornamental designs on  garments or other materials; operating and monitoring  machines which bleach, shrink, dye, and otherwise treat  fibers, yarn, cloth or dry clean garments, fur, rugs, carpets; operating and monitoring various  machines which  prepare leather or treat fur or wool-bearing pelts; operating and monitoring machines  which produce, modify  and repair standard, custom or orthopedic footwear and  leather articles, such as luggage, brief cases, handbags.

records.title: FIBRE PREPARING, SPINNING AND WINDING MACHINE OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Fiber-preparing, spinning and winding machine operators operate and monitor machines which prepare fibers,  and spin, double, twist and wind yarn and thread from natural textile fibers. They twist two or more strands of  yarn to prepare single stronger, smoother, uniform and heavier strands and treat textiles to make them stiff and  water resistant.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring  machines for tearing woolen rags into fiber;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines for cleaning and turning woolen yarn waste into fluffed wool;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which combine textile fibers into uniform blends;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which  clean and fluff  textile fibers,  transform them into sliver, comb  them into sliver for first drawing, combine slivers into sliver lap or sliver laps into ribbon lap;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating draw frame machine) having number of drawing sets, each set combining several slivers into one  of nearly same weight and thickness as any of original sliver;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which spin thread and yarn from roving, wind two or more threads onto  bobbin, twist two or more strands of yarn or thread into single strands of yarn to increase strength, smoothness  and/or uniformity of yarn, or wind yarn or thread from one package to another;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: operating and monitoring spinning frame that draws out and twists roving or sliver into yarn;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: operating and monitoring  machines for drawing slivers received from drawing machine into loosely twisted  strands;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: preparing sizing for use in stiffening and finishing cloth and yarn by mixing ingredients such as starch,  tallow, resins, soaps and water and boiling mixture  for specified time in steam;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: treating textiles with chemicals to make them water resistant;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: cleaning rollers and cylinders of carding machines to remove wool waste; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: operating and resurfacing metal drawing rolls of various spinning, combing and lapping machines with new  rubber or leather covers.

examples.title: Thread and yarn spinning machine operator
Thread and yarn twisting machine operator
Thread and yarn winding machine operator

definition_paragraphs.text: Weaving and knitting machine operators set up, operate and monitor weaving and knitting machines which  process yarn or thread into woven, non-woven and knitted products such as cloth, lace, carpets, rope, industrial  fabric, hosiery and knitted garments or to quilt and embroider fabric.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: setting up and operating batteries of automatic, link-type knitting machines to knit garments of specified  pattern and design;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: threading yarn, thread, and fabric through guides, needles, and rollers of machines for weaving, knitting, or  other processing;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: tending automatic looms that simultaneously weave pile yarn, filling yarn, and warp yarn material to  produce carpets and rugs with various colored designs;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating and monitoring loom on which yarn or twist is intersected and knotted at regular intervals to form  mesh;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating and monitoring large automatic multi-needle machines to embroider material or to sew lengths of  several layers of material to make yard goods, quilts or mattress coverings;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: tending circular knitting machines with automatic pattern controls that knit seamless hose;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: operating and monitoring knitting machines to knit hosiery to shape of foot and leg;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machine for knitting heel and toes of socks into ribs or tops cut from circular  fabric;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machine which seams openings in toes of socks;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: operating and monitoring crocheter machine to knit lace, trimming etc. of desired pattern or design;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: examining looms to determine causes of loom stoppage, such as warp filling, harness breaks, or mechanical  defects;

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: repairing or replacing worn or defective needles and other components; and

tasks.label: m
tasks.text: cleaning, oiling, and lubricating machines, using air hoses, cleaning solutions, rags, oil cans, and/or grease  guns.

definition_paragraphs.text: Sewing machine operators operate and monitor sewing machines to make, repair, darn and renovate textile, fur,  synthetic or leather garments or embroider ornamental designs on garments or other materials. They operate  button hole making and eyelet holing machines to cut holes, stitch around holes, stitch buttons and fix eyelets to  garments.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating or tending sewing machines to perform garment sewing operations, such as joining, reinforcing,   seaming or decorating garments or garment parts;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: attaching buttons, hooks, zippers, fasteners, or other accessories to fabric, using feeding hoppers or clamp  holders;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: tending semiautomatic sewing machines with multiple-sewing heads controlled by pattern chain that  embroiders various designs on garments;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating machines, such as single or double needle sergers and flat-bed felling machines, to automatically  join, reinforce, or decorate material or articles;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating fur sewing machines to join fur pelt strips to required size and shape and join pelts into garment  sections or shells;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating stitching machines to sew leather parts together for leather garments, handbags, gloves;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: monitoring machine operation to detect problems such as defective stitching, breaks in thread, or machine  malfunctions; and

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: performing equipment maintenance tasks such as replacing needles.

records.title: BLEACHING, DYEING AND FABRIC CLEANING MACHINE OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Bleaching, dyeing and fabric cleaning machine operators operate and monitor machines that bleach, shrink, dye,  and otherwise treat fibers, yarn or cloth.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: starting and controlling machines and equipment to bleach, dye, or otherwise process and finish fabric, yarn,  thread, and/or other textile goods;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: tending machines that shrink woven or knitted cloth to predetermined size or strengthen the weave by  interlocking the fibers;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: tending a variety of automatic machines that comb and polish furs;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines that treat silk to give it body and weight;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines that impregnate textiles with chemicals to render them waterproof;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: dyeing articles to change or restore their colors;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines that stretch, or impart luster, or other type of finish to textiles;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: tending and regulating equipment that fumigates and removes foreign matter from furs;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: operating machines that comb, dry and polish furs, clean, sterilize and fluff feathers and blankets;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: keying in processing instructions to program electronic equipment;

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: observing display screens, control panels, equipment, and cloth entering or exiting processes to determine if  equipment is operating correctly; and

tasks.label: l
tasks.text: cleaning machine filters and lubricating equipment.

records.title: FUR AND LEATHER PREPARING MACHINE OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Fur and leather preparing machine operators operate and monitor various machines that prepare leather or treat  fur or wool-bearing pelts. They trim, scrape, clean, tan, buff and dye animal hides, pelts or skins to produce  leather stock and finished furs.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which remove flesh and fat from hides or pelts to clean and soften them  prior to processing;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which remove long coarse hair from fur pelts, trim hair to even length  and dye, stretch and smooth dressed pelts;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines to remove epidermis hair roots, pigment cells and lime salts from grain side of skin;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines to reduce thickness of hide or skin to uniform size;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines to polish or roughen hides or skins to specified finish;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which separate residual wool from skins, or flesh and hair from hides;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines in which hides are split edgeways to form two or more pieces or to give uniform thickness;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which treat hides and skins in solutions to convert them into leather;

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: treating surface of leather with oil  and  operating glazing machine to give glossy finish to leather;

tasks.label: j
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which apply dyes and stains to leather; and

tasks.label: k
tasks.text: maintaining and repairing vats and other machinery.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which mark patterns and cut shoe parts;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which sew shoe parts together, or edge, polish, or apply ornaments and  perform finishing tasks; and

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machines which produce luggage, handbags, belts and other accessories, as well as  other items such as saddles, collars or harnesses.

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: placing sorted articles into receptacles and onto conveyor belts for moving to repair and cleaning areas;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: checking and removing stains from garments, and replacing buttons and making minor repairs;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: loading and unloading washing machines, driers and extractors;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: adding cleaning agents and starches to articles;

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: smoothing articles and guiding them through cleaning and pressing machines;

tasks.label: g
tasks.text: stopping and starting machines to untangle, straighten and remove articles;

tasks.label: h
tasks.text: placing articles on shelves and hanging articles for delivery and collection; and

tasks.label: i
tasks.text: packaging articles and preparing orders for dispatch.

FOOD AND RELATED PRODUCTS MACHINE OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Food and related machine operators set, operate and attend machinery used to slaughter animals, trim meat  from carcasses; bake, freeze, heat, crush, mix, blend and otherwise process foodstuffs, beverages and tobacco  leaves.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: operating and monitoring machinery used to restrain, stun, slaughter animals and trim carcasses into standard meat and fish cuts;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: setting, operating and attending machinery and ovens to mix, bake and otherwise prepare bread and flour  confectionery products;

tasks.label: d

tasks.label: e

records.title: WOOD PROCESSING AND PAPERMAKING PLANT OPERATORS

definition_paragraphs.text: Wood processing and papermaking plant operators monitor, operate, and control automated lumber mill  equipment sawing wood, cutting veneer and making plywood, and otherwise preparing wood for further use.  Pulp mill machine operators operate and monitor various types of processing machinery and equipment to  produce pulp.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: examining logs and rough lumber to determine size, condition, quality and other characteristics to decide  best lumber cuts to carry out, or operating automated equipment to convey logs through laser scanners which  determine the most productive and profitable cutting patterns;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: sorting, stacking and placing logs and wood billets onto conveyors and lathes from trucks for processing  into chips, veneers and pulp;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: operating and monitoring screening equipment, bleaching equipment, digesters, mixing tanks, washers, and  other pulp processing machinery and equipment to carry out one or more cellulose processing steps;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: observing equipment and machinery panel indicators, gauges, level indicators and other equipment  instruments to detect machinery and equipment malfunctions and ensure process steps are carried out according  to specifications;

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: operating and monitoring plywood core-laying machines and hot-plate plywood presses and machines  which cut veneer; and

tasks.label: f
tasks.text: transporting processed wood products, such as plywood, chipboard sheets and panels to work areas.

definition_paragraphs.text: Pulp and papermaking plant operators operate and monitor multi-function process control machinery and  processing equipment to control the processing of wood, scrap pulp and other cellulose materials in the  production of pulp.

tasks.label: a
tasks.text: coordinating and monitoring the operation of screening equipment, washing equipment, digesters, mixing  tanks and other pulp processing equipment from automated panel boards in central control room to control the  processing of wood, scrap pulp, recyclable paper and other cellulose materials;

tasks.label: b
tasks.text: operating and monitoring screening equipment, bleaching equipment, digesters, mixing tanks, washers and  other pulp processing machinery and equipment to carry out one or more cellulose processing steps;

tasks.label: c
tasks.text: controlling start-up and shut-down of process machinery and equipment, and observing equipment and  machinery panel indicators, gauges, level indicators and other equipment instruments to detect machinery and  equipment malfunctions and ensure process steps are carried out according to specifications;

tasks.label: d
tasks.text: analyzing instrument readings and production test samples and making adjustments to pulp production  process and equipment as required; and

tasks.label: e
tasks.text: completing and maintaining production reports.

definition_paragraphs.text: Steam engine and boiler operators maintain and operate various types of steam engines, boilers, turbines and  auxiliary equipment to provide power and other utility services for commercial, industrial and institutional  buildings, at work sites and aboard ships or self-propelled vessels.

definition_paragraphs.text: Assemblers assemble prefabricated parts or components to form subassemblies, products and equipment,  according to strictly laid down procedures. The products worked on may be moved from one worker to the next  along assembly lines.
